The headless renderer crashed across repeated capture attempts, so visuals are unverified (render did not complete in headless). The domain resolves; only the render could not be captured.

524b2fddc4834867b16c142d796b5478.description: Chowdeck is an on-demand African delivery platform covering food, groceries, pharmacy and everyday essentials. Warm cream base with Chowdeck green, plus a pastel pink, blue and orange secondary palette used to colour-code categories. Bold rounded sans headers, thick black borders, hand-drawn illustration and rounded cards give a neo-brutalist-lite feel. Two blocks worth stealing: an interactive map-to-list component that shows regional availability, and a lifestyle UI showcase where app notifications are overlaid on real photography instead of floating in a device frame.

07b07c4266134d3baf363de92a1d4be2.description: Chronicle is an AI presentation tool that turns raw notes, docs and data into polished on-brand decks. Note the site has been redesigned since it was saved — it is now a light split hero (off-white and charcoal with muted peach UI accents), not the dark treatment in the saved tags. Elegant high-contrast serif headlines sit against clean sans UI, with a subtle vertical pinstripe grid adding texture behind. The product shot is layered and overlapping, with floating cursors and avatars dropped in to sell real-time collaboration without a word of copy. Good reference for design-tool marketing where the mockup has to carry the story.

5f3b5aac72b546868a96bb209d3c875b.description: Portfolio of designer Chungi Yoo, built almost entirely on typography. Palette is cream, black and soft pink; the display face is a high-contrast serif with exaggerated flourishes and ligatures that carries the whole brand identity without needing big imagery. Massive low-opacity background lettering sits behind sharp foreground display type to create depth, and hand-drawn arrows, stamps and circular frames break the digital rigidity. Strong reference for expressive type-led portfolios and for annotation-style graphic accents.

e0697aa9e99645a697377104c82aedad.description: Cine Casero is an online archive preserving Uruguayan home movies and amateur cinema. Noir monochrome with deep greys and a persistent film-grain overlay; high-contrast serif titles over a clean sans. The whole design is an analog film pastiche: continuous grain, minimal layout, archival footage given the entire stage. Strong reference for cultural or archive projects where the interface should disappear behind the material, with a process block explaining how films are collected and restored.

2887b8e81d8880cfaeb9d64f81c9278d.description: CleanSpace is a US design-build firm for controlled environments (cleanrooms, cold rooms, dry rooms), vertically integrated across planning, design, engineering, manufacturing and construction, serving pharma, biotech, semiconductor, food & beverage, battery and aerospace. Webflow build with a bold-word-emphasis headline pattern ("Modern Design Build for Controlled Environments"), a Certainty / Compliance / Confidence triptych, a named process block called CleanFit that guarantees cost and timeline, and a photo gallery strip of cleanroom, HVAC and construction imagery. Site by Scaler Marketing. Visuals unverified (Playwright screenshot timed out twice in headless render), so hero type is left unset.

16c7b8e81d88809ba941dc3e00c55215.description: Clear Street is an independent, cloud-native prime broker and clearing/custody platform for hedge funds, family offices, ETF issuers and broker-dealers, pitched as a replacement for 1970s-era financial infrastructure. The hero is a saturated cobalt-to-violet gradient with a heavy geometric grotesque headline and a floating Studio dashboard screenshot lifted off the background with a soft glow and a deep drop shadow, all under a pill-shaped translucent floating nav. Notable blocks: a looping stats marquee (employees, shares/day, notional/day, capital raised) that turns dry numbers into motion, a video-driven scrollytelling narrative about legacy COBOL infrastructure, a Studio product-UI showcase (risk and margin, exposures, P&L), and a region-by-region clearing coverage list with "coming soon" states. Site by Büro (burocratik.com), credited "Made by Büro" in the footer.

16c7b8e81d8880eaa054d597aefe1db5.description: Cocota is a brand and design studio with offices in Madrid and London, doing branding, corporate design, web design and UI/UX, with a project-led portfolio (RPA, Faster Displays) and a blog. The site is a bilingual WordPress build with a dark navy theme colour declared in its meta, and it is fully client-side rendered. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render): two capture passes, including one with wait plus accept/close clicks, both returned a blank white frame, so hero composition, palette and block structure are not recorded here. Worth re-checking manually in a real browser before relying on this entry.

5344f6475f1e4ffeba83c66517deb4ec.description: Codex is a real-time blockchain data API for trading apps ("the fastest and most reliable blockchain data API", 70M+ tokens across 80+ networks). Dark-mode hero built on a massive wide sans headline, a neon lime CTA, and floating 3D-effect glowing chain icons (Arbitrum, Uniswap) that add depth behind the type, under a glassmorphic sticky nav. Trading-ready / sub-second / all-in-one micro-features sit directly under the headline. Notable blocks: a dedicated Compare page (competitor comparison table) and Pricing. Good reference for a dev-tool site that stays credible while going loud on scale and speed.

2147b8e81d888048a76beaddf577d98e.description: Cohere is the Canadian enterprise-AI company (LLMs plus the North agentic workplace platform), positioning around data sovereignty and private deployment. The homepage is a Swiss-style, typography-centric layout: an off-white/charcoal monochrome base, an enormous high-contrast serif headline ("Own your AI") paired with a clean sans for UI text, and generous white space. The distinctive technique is the image treatment — grainy, iridescent purple-to-warm-wood photographic renders with a deliberately lo-fi noisy texture that reads artistic and human rather than clinical tech. Notable blocks: an enterprise logos bar (Oracle, Dell, RBC, SAP, Salesforce, Notion), an industry-coverage grid, a models/products section, a developer-resources block and a testimonial carousel closing on a pill CTA.

eff0362da88040fe89f0a1372f0adcdc.description: CoLabs rents wet-lab, engineering and office space to bio and deep-tech startups across Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane — bench space up to PC2 pods and fully custom labs. The hero pairs a bold tight-tracked sans headline with warm macro science photography in yellows and creams, offset by teal and blue accent modules. Worth stealing: organic masking where the hero image resolves into the white space below via fluid rounded corners, a bento-style vertical sidebar mixing circles and rounded rectangles for stats and CTAs, and a semi-transparent floating pill nav that keeps the whole page feeling light.

706d75a421f74681b92302f629630757.description: Colors Combinations is Obys Agency's colour-inspiration experiment: six photographs, each mined for palettes and shade combinations to show how to pull colour out of the everyday environment and into design work. The selected colour becomes the entire page background (for example a muted grayish-cyan) with crisp oversized white type on top, and HEX and RGB values are treated as display elements rather than footnotes, split by a thin horizontal rule. The menu is a six-tile picture gallery, and each colour gets its own info and combinations sub-pages. A black promo card cross-links the Design Education Series.

80451e923c6c4db391e9b7e1f0d4546c.description: Awwwards Conference — the event site for the Awwwards two-to-three day conferences (the saved URL now resolves to the New York edition, alongside Valencia Leaders and Valencia Developers editions), 14–18 talks for design leaders, UX/UI designers and digital creatives, themed around AI, next-gen UX and digital frontiers. Speakers pulled from Google, Porto Rocha, The New York Times and Locomotive. Useful as an events reference: the page is organised around speaker cards (portrait, company, role, deep-linked profile), a SOLD OUT state used as social proof rather than hidden, an animated keyword marquee of conference topics (AI, Predictive UX, AR, VR, Chatbots), a past-editions gallery, a partners bar and a long accordion FAQ that doubles as event logistics. Site by estudio/nk. Visuals unverified — the headless render throws a client-side Next.js exception, so no hero type recorded.

3a37b8e81d8880469367ebb755a6a9d3.description: ConsumerAppStudio is a one-person product-design info product by Bartek Marzec — a downloadable deck of 100+ tactical "plays" across 12 stacks (onboarding, activation, retention, monetisation) for designing emotionally sticky consumer apps. Hero is a centred minimal landing composition: stark white and black with one electric-blue CTA, a bold tight-tracked sans headline, and high-fidelity floating desk objects (ruler, paperclip, playing cards) that make a digital product feel physical. Steal-worthy patterns: price baked into the button, a low-contrast "same methods used by" logo bar, a before/after comparison table, real card mockups annotated with app examples, and a multi-column review wall. Webflow, no studio credited.

2147b8e81d8880c0bec4c298890a2c74.description: Contentsquare is an enterprise experience-intelligence analytics platform (Experience Analytics, Product Analytics, Voice of Customer, session replay, heatmaps, the Sense AI agent). Distinctive for a moody dark plum/berry brand base — rare in B2B SaaS — offset by high-saturation vibrant pink CTAs and a soft peach announcement bar, with bold clean sans headings. The hero is split: messaging left, a floating product dashboard mockup right, sitting on tiered layered background shapes that add depth. Notable blocks: a tabbed product-showcase carousel that swaps large UI screenshots per capability, an animated odometer-style customer-results block that rolls numbers (Audi +7%, Pirelli, EasyJet, Ocado), team-persona tabs, G2/Gartner rating stats, an integrations grid and an interactive product tour.

f7600ef23dce44ffab8eadf97c712430.description: Contiant is a fintech / banking data platform. Instead of a flat screenshot, the hero carries a stylised floating interface diagram that walks the product's workflow step by step, set on a minimalist off-white ground with violet-purple and dark navy accents and a clean geometric sans. Worth stealing: the visual-narrative diagram that explains a complex process at a glance, overlapping cards with soft shadows for layered depth, a hand-drawn squiggle underline adding a human mark to an otherwise corporate fintech aesthetic, and a subtle bank logos bar carrying trust immediately below the fold.

4bce6eae602446eb9c12d2d9adcbc555.description: Contra is a commission-free freelance platform and portfolio network (launched 2019, San Francisco) where independents keep 100% of earnings. The hero is clean and product-led: a white field with subtle grey geometric grid, a bold sans 'Get more creative' headline, and a central rounded search field with a 'Let's go' button and pill suggestion tags, above an image-heavy 'Trending Topics' card carousel. Reference for search-first, friendly marketplace heroes with a discovery carousel.

52369435fcf34c47950500feb3d25c89.description: Project site on a subdomain of Russian digital studio Chipsa (chipsa.design / chipsa.ru), saved here as a health-products landing with big type, visible borders and scrolltelling. The domain still responds, but the page renders completely blank in a headless browser — typical of Chipsa's heavily JS/WebGL-driven scrolltelling builds — so visuals are unverified (loader/JS gate in headless render) and no hero type or blocks have been assigned. Worth re-checking manually in a real browser; Chipsa's case-study pages are usually strong references for scroll-driven narrative layouts and oversized editorial typography.

2887b8e81d888080832ef5a6a5b7ce16.description: Cora is an AI email chief-of-staff by Every that screens your Gmail inbox, drafts replies in your voice and sends a twice-daily Brief. The hero leans on a literal metaphor: a photographic blue-sky-and-clouds background (inbox clarity) with an elevated, soft-shadowed product mockup floating below, vivid sky blue and white, and a high-contrast editorial serif headline against modern sans support text. Technically the most interesting thing here is scroll-driven animation built from dozens of numbered webp frames creating layered cloud and foreground parallax, plus a postage-stamp border treatment on the logo and floating email-card compositing. Also runs a continuously looping testimonial ticker with avatars and company logos. Site by darkroom.engineering.

e8c4eaa824394142ac1c9eaba4e61ec1.description: Cosmos — a visual bookmarking and inspiration platform for creative teams ("Your space for inspiration"). Note the site now renders as a light monochrome design: stark white background, black type and heavy-weight sans headings, letting the member artwork carry all the colour. The hero is centred typography over a field of scattered, drifting image thumbnails. Strongest blocks to steal: an animated search showcase where search bars type themselves through queries like "future home" and "runway editorial", and a three-card feature grid demoing search by colour (with live hex chips), by visual similarity, and "without AI" via a real content-filter toggle — functional UI used as storytelling. Also a grayscale logo cloud (Apple, Gucci, Adidas, Chanel) and an embedded featured film module.

b685d9decc5a455abc885e1a4bed00f7.description: Cowboy, the Belgian connected e-bike brand. Hero is a wide cinematic lifestyle shot with the bike centred, sun-drenched earthy stone and greenery tones set against a strictly black-and-white UI, headline in a bold tight-tracked sans. Two details worth stealing: the geo-location redirect modal is styled exactly like the rest of the site so a disruptive function feels native, and a quiet bottom bar surfaces key value props (design, tech, security) without crowding the hero. Good reference for premium DTC hardware where the product photo has to do the selling.

906373c548064811af2e86a6f60a14fd.description: Play is a Mac/iOS tool for designing and shipping mobile apps with real native iOS elements, SwiftUI code generation and Xcode export. The marketing site leans on an oversized 'Meet Play.' statement headline and a very large social-proof engine: a logos bar of Netflix, Airbnb, Snapchat, Spotify and OpenAI, then a scrolling wall of designer tweets that doubles as testimonials, plus named pull-quotes from Andy Matuschak and Joey Banks. Feature sections pair copy with product UI showcases of prefabs, variables and real-time code export. Visuals unverified (the page repeatedly crashed the headless renderer), so hero type is left unset.

56a9256aede541e7866ee8c1ff4068e4.description: Critical Danger is a data-driven awareness campaign about wildlife extinction. Urgent palette of deep burgundy, signal red and light grey, mixing bold sans headlines, a high-contrast serif for pull quotes and big statistics, and monospace for data points. Strong reference for an unusual stats block: regional wildlife decline percentages laid out as a clean comparative list, plus drastic scale jumps from tiny data labels to massive figures like 42k+ to dramatise magnitude. Also notable are a media-clipping montage of overlapping newspaper headlines for historical proof, and collectible-style floating species cards (Amur Leopard, Javan Rhino) that enter at angles. Kinetic intro headlines resolve from blurred to sharp on scroll.

d5e32464a5574b018ec3f26dee954a80.description: FASTCUP is a competitive Counter-Strike matchmaking and tournament platform — leagues, ladders, rankings, teams, streams and highlights. There is no marketing hero: the logged-out homepage is the product itself, a dense dashboard of live data widgets on a deep charcoal-navy base with safety-orange accents reserved for CTAs and alerts. Worth stealing: live player counts and open match listings that make the platform feel populated the second you land, a horizontal marquee ticker of in-game items, a modular system of semi-transparent cards separating tournaments, matchmaking and promo slots, and colour-coded status tags ("Registration in progress") that make a crowded tournament board scannable. Strong reference for community/esports products that must show activity, not describe it.

4647786e487842f1bd0a3c056c44007b.description: Ctrl (ex XDEFI) is a non-custodial multi-chain crypto wallet supporting 2,500+ blockchains, with Gas Tank fees and cross-chain swaps. Clean white-black landing with an action-green accent, big type hero and a Download for Chrome CTA. As of mid-2026 a full-screen modal announces Ctrl Wallet is shutting down with an asset-transfer deadline; the modal itself is a nice split layout, concise high-contrast text left, soft-focus 3D illustration right. Product is sunsetting, so treat as an archive reference.

e19adb5a71614478905d8a6a7cd30ceb.description: Cuban's Edge sells intelligent trading tools and market analysis software to professional traders. The whole design argues authority through restraint: an ultra-minimal hero of massive layered typography in stark monochrome (black on off-white), pairing a bold modern sans for headings with a high-contrast serif for the logo and accents. Notable blocks include a bento-style feature grid with subtle hairline borders covering asset screener and wallet tracking, and a scroll-synced product showcase where a left sidebar menu tracks your progress through product categories (Asset Selection, Mean Reversion). Good reference for premium fintech built on negative space rather than gradients.

19ab8549fb49476ba86ff1484709c362.description: Cula is an MRV engine (monitoring, reporting, verification) for carbon removal, a B2B climate-software platform serving biochar and other CDR pathways. Recently rebranded into a 'blueprint' aesthetic: off-white ground tinted pale blue, a faint technical grid, dark navy geometric sans, the headline framed inside a thin bordered box, and navigation pushed into all four corners so the centre stays wide open. Each product section pairs a short label with a looping product-UI video (inventory tracking, on-site integrations, unit quality management, real-time production monitoring). Also carries a standards and customer logo wall (Puro, Isometric, Verra, Gold Standard, Ørsted) and an insights feed.

e687bdfdf7a54ab083dc8a8ac8f55734.description: Custo (Belgium, Shopify) sells the Custo® smart mailbox — a parcel box that opens by scanning the barcode on the parcel itself, running a 4G API check across 1500+ couriers before unlocking, paired with an app that aggregates tracking, notifications and shared access. Two SKUs (Custo 1 standing, Custo 1s wall-mounted, from €1.599). Excellent hardware-product-page reference: industrial-chic monochrome of neutral greys, deep charcoal and high-contrast white, with an oversized “CUSTO” wordmark used as a structural background layer. Its best trick is depth-layering — the sharply lit product shot is sandwiched between that giant background type and the foreground nav, producing a parallax 3D effect, with a semi-transparent Order now button. Notable blocks: a numbered four-step how-it-works, an app-feature walkthrough with phone shots, and an awards bar (CES Innovation Awards 2024, Red Dot Winner).

996d351e28334ae4a6ca75f1c0be6ab8.description: Official hub for the Cyberpunk 2077 universe from CD PROJEKT RED — base game, the Phantom Liberty expansion and the Edgerunners anime. The hero is a split layout: one side carries condensed weathered display type and the stylised logo, the other an immersive character illustration, all locked to the franchise's single high-saturation yellow against deep black. The identity holds together because that one colour is used ruthlessly. Worth stealing are the UI accents that carry the fiction — dashed rules, glitch-inspired modules, angled corner-cut "Buy Now" buttons and terminal-style tags — so even utility elements stay in world. Rest of the site is news feed, media gallery and trailers. Reference for franchise sites with a hard-owned brand colour.

485e25d7aa134ce4b12cba64ab4a10c4.description: Cyclops Club — a video production and post-production agency scaling multimedia content for brands (Business Insider, BuzzFeed, Google, J.P. Morgan). Typography-dominant hero with the headline interspersed with vector icons (play button, film strip, heart, smiley) plus a scroll-to-discover cue. Monochrome black-and-white UI with heavy sans headlines and a monospace for technical data, so the embedded footage carries all colour; a dark/light toggle sits centre-nav. Best block to steal: the services section is dressed as a fake Adobe Media Encoder output window showing metadata for CYCLOPS_CLUB_001, with a scroll-driven render progress bar and REC indicator — a UI metaphor that sells the craft. Also a cinematic montage where storyboard sketches overlay live footage to expose process, a client logo ticker, and playful offset GIFs.

3177b8e81d8880f994f6ff77707cb077.description: D2C Life Science (Rosheim, France) is a data-driven GMP consultancy for pharma, CMOs and engineering partners, covering cost of quality, QMS implementation, Quality Assurance 4.0, quality risk management and CMO oversight; its tagline is Precision in data, impact in culture. Awwwards SOTD, built by Iron Velvet, and best known for a GSAP-driven 3D hero in which the company's six service pillars are embodied by a self-solving algorithmic Rubik's cube that scrolltells through each pillar. The visual language is quiet and premium: desaturated sage green, off-white type, cryptic geometric glyphs standing in for a wordmark and small uppercase monospace for supporting copy, with vast negative space. Reference for 3D scrolltelling metaphors and restrained scientific-consultancy branding. Note: the automated screenshot only captured the minimal splash/loader frame (sage ground, glyph logo, monospace tagline), so the 3D hero is not visible in the attached image.

0e22549bb0dc4162ac39407603d74358.description: Dala is an AI-powered workplace search tool that surfaces knowledge and people across an organisation's disparate systems; the site is a showcase build by Green Chameleon (craftedbygc) using Three.js/WebGL and GSAP scroll-driven particle animation. Visuals unverified (WebGL loader in headless render): capture stayed on a dark minimal splash/loader ('LOADING'), so the animated hero could not be confirmed. Verified copy positions it as a sleek, cinematic dark-mode product site with a big-type value proposition.

25fb784c09454957ae5b98a5a4345ca3.description: Not a gallery — this is the official site of DANIEL ROTH, the Swiss high-watchmaking maison from the Vallée de Joux (founded 1989, revived under Bulgari/LVMH), positioned as "La Montre Objet d'Art" around its signature double-ellipse case. The hero is a split composition on midnight blue: an oversized cropped macro of the watch on the left against a contained cream panel on the right that acts as a lit stage for the full packshot. Typography pairs a high-contrast all-caps serif for the collection title with a light all-caps sans for labels and the 01–04 counter, and a vertical material selector (Platinum / Rose Gold / Skeleton / Souscription) sits beside the product. Strong inner pages: Historical Models and History.

57fa7a6579ac4626aae94befa6266f28.description: Portfolio of Darina Ivanova, a 3D artist and AI concept creator working with luxury brands (Chanel, Cartier) and architecture bureaus, plus her studio DAR STUDIO RENDER. Editorial split layout: a persistent terracotta left sidebar holding the logo, nav, circular portrait and CTA, against a cream content pane. Section headers are deconstructed into individual boxed letters (P-R-O-D, 3-D, M-E) and delicate dashed hairlines separate sections; navigation and copy are widely-spaced all-caps sans. Notable blocks: numbered project galleries mixing renders and video, a client logo marquee, an educational-materials card grid with item counts, a shop block with a percentage progress indicator, and a contact block. Site by Dyo Tanya.

3347b8e81d88801d908bf5ac544248fd.description: Darknode is the anti-Shahed battalion of Ukraine's 412th Nemesis Brigade, a tech unit that intercepts Russian kamikaze drones; the site handles recruitment, mission storytelling, merch and donations in UA/EN. The hero is a grainy, high-contrast silhouette photo behind an industrial condensed headline (Guarding Your Dawns), wrapped in tactical HUD furniture: live X/Y coordinate readouts, a GMT clock, a numbered scale ruler, a night-mode toggle and a sound on/off switch. Notable blocks: a hard stat line (over 1,500 Shaheds shot down), a Mission / Vision / Purpose values trio, an Our goal threat card slider profiling the Geran-2 and Gerbera drones with spec data, a two-path recruitment CTA (I'm a Civilian / I'm in Military), a merch drop section and an FAQ. Site by Qream. Excellent reference for military/defence UI, HUD overlays and dark tactical branding.

5e81b0f838c94812a26b8c276ef2bd33.description: Dash Digital (DashDigital®) is a Cape Town-based digital design studio working across research, strategy, brand identity, UX/UI and development for Lemkus, Kia, Tiger Wheel & Tyre, Woolworths, Sneaker LAB, AfriSam and Fincheck. Heavily awarded — Awwwards Studio of the Year nominee, Site of the Month, 13x SOTD, 10x FWA of the Day, CSS Design Awards Website of the Year nominee, Webby nominee. The hero is Swiss-grid and typography-led: light grey ground, charcoal text, a bold all-caps grotesk headline at massive scale with tight tracking, and colour introduced only through full-bleed project imagery below — stark text area against detailed photography. Notable blocks: a featured-work slider with service tags per project, an expanding accordion client list where each brand reveals scope and a written case summary, a candid team photo strip, and an awards-and-recognitions tally broken out by awarding body.

b796d089a536428cb7ac1022e840ff13.description: DashQ is an AI platform that automates the renter management lifecycle for the leasing and property industry (not consumer finance, despite the saved Industry tag). The hero pairs big high-contrast sans with a stylised illustration that blends technical line art and solid 3D geometry to represent digital transformation. Palette is soft cream, deep navy buttons and a vibrant mint accent. The layout device worth stealing is the large-radius rounded containers that nest and layer to create organic framing instead of a rigid grid. Good reference for proptech and vertical SaaS that wants to feel warm rather than corporate.

2d43d4cd0fd7450cac7883a99b7da0b2.description: Portfolio of Davide Parere, a Milan-based freelance art director, designer and collage artist who builds saturated, surreal, high-contrast collages from vintage books and magazines (ADC award winner), offering creative direction, brand identity, editorial, packaging and web design. Note: the site could not be verified in this headless run, both the root and www hosts returned an SSL certificate name-mismatch (ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID), so the current layout and visuals are unverified and the link may trigger a browser security warning. Description is based on the artist's documented body of work rather than a captured frame.

dae8f42654a8467d8b485a08deb9f24b.description: Laxer Brands is a Tel Aviv brand consultancy (founded 2013) doing strategic narrative, core messaging and thought leadership for founders and executive teams. The hero is a hard vertical split — white text column against a desaturated grey portrait of David Laxer, 'Chief Storyteller' — with an all-caps heavy neo-grotesque 'WE ARE LAXER' bleeding across the colour divide, bullet-dotted nav and a services list pinned to the bottom of the first screen. The whole site is numbered 1-8 like a document. Unusual blocks: a transparent pricing table that publishes exact fees and timelines ($15k / 30 days for the strategic presentation, $10k Day 1 content, $7.5k naming), a 'Do's & Don'ts' comparison listing Tennis vs Golf as real criteria, case studies framed as questions, and a 7-question fit survey replacing the usual contact CTA. Site by Obys.

612e3765c5eb4992acd559646991736b.description: Daylight sells the DC-1, a 'human-friendly' tablet with a fast-refresh, paper-like 'Live Paper' display built for deep focus, outdoor readability and no blue light. The hero is a product shot of the tablet in a sunlit natural setting; the palette is warm and organic (cream, amber, charcoal) with a high-contrast serif for headlines against a modern sans for body. Techniques worth stealing: scroll-driven background colour shifts between light and dark to dramatise screen legibility in different lighting, realistic leaf shadows cast over the product photography to sell the outdoor promise, and a philosophy-first structure that gives large-type manifesto statements significant vertical space before any specs appear. Also has a use-case gallery (reading, note-taking, writing) and a minimal monochrome app-icon UI showcase.

1969a979ded04f6bab176e07584179dd.description: Studio Debuut is a Deventer (Netherlands) branding and design studio working on strategy, identity and print/digital design (Awwwards Site of the Day). The hero pairs a bold high-contrast editorial serif headline with a dark forest-green background and neon lime-yellow accents, using vertical sidebars for social links and awards and printing the physical studio address in the header for a transparent, framed feel. Reference for dark editorial branding with acid-green highlights.

f12278f9db12454b8a3e18ff6d46d2a1.description: A single-product immersive experience for Decathlon's WLKR76 shoe, built by Index Studio: a WebGL/3D scrolltelling microsite rather than a normal product page. In a headless render it only reaches the intro state, a high-key monochrome white/pale-grey frame with a heavy depth-of-field blur and ultra-thin wide-tracked sans type dissolving into a 3D environment underneath. Useful as a reference for premium sportswear product launches where the whole page is one continuous 3D scene. Visuals unverified (heavy WebGL intro/loader in headless render), so hero type is left unset rather than guessed.

3ba4f6998850429a893246d4113ce940.description: DECEM is a UK Light Spirit brand (from the Latin for ten) selling 10% ABV low-alcohol spirits: London Dry, Spiced Blend and a Strawberry & Botanicals Aperitif, positioned in the gap between full-strength spirits (37.5%+) and low-alcohol (1.2%). Shopify-based, UK-only shipping. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render): an over-18 age gate sits in the HTML and three capture attempts returned either a timeout or a Shopify error page, so no hero was ever rendered and no palette or typography is claimed here. The only page retrievable was the FAQ, which uses a well-written product-education accordion (What is a Light Spirit?, Why 10%?) alongside shipping and stockist/ambassador enquiries.

169cc50cb611400cb3f67facfdac6dd7.description: Advocacy site arguing against the criminalisation of poverty, built as a slow scrollytelling narrative. The hero is a full-screen illustration — a Tennessee bridge scene with diverse figures — in monochromatic teal and seafoam greens with dark forest green type and lilac pops, pairing an ultra-bold condensed headline against light geometric sans subtext. Worth stealing: an explicit "scroll slowly" instruction paired with a temporal nav (Present / History / Future) that frames the page as a journey rather than a document, and grainy stippled texture over flat 2D illustration for an editorial print feel. Strong reference for nonprofit storytelling.

d9b6ede38c7646c39c67d3dd9b1510f8.description: Deed replaces repetitive manual work in logistics with intelligent automation, sold through a free on-site operations audit. Dark-mode hero: near-black ground with a fine micro-grid, a faint green radial glow behind the headline, bold tight-tracked sans with 'repetitive work' colour-blocked in mint, and a small news pill above the headline for low-friction updates. Social proof lands immediately under the fold with real KPIs from UPS Iceland (deployed 2023) plus client logos. Notable blocks: the consultative process explainer (they come on-site, watch the team, map workflows, then present what they would change and the realistic result) and the outcome stats.

239991287238471b820efc6db121715c.description: Redirected — the saved /technologies/gemini/ path now lands on the current model page at deepmind.google/models/gemini/. It is Google DeepMind's Gemini model hub, covering the model family, capabilities (agentic coding, multimodal understanding, long-horizon tasks) and benchmark comparisons against competing models. The hero is a horizontally swipeable carousel of giant rounded cards: oversized geometric Google Sans type over soft powder-blue-to-periwinkle bokeh gradients with a fine computational grain, plus paired CTAs where a solid black primary sits beside a glassmorphic secondary. Strong inner blocks: a wide benchmark comparison table and a large "Hands-on" grid of short video demos, each a one-line use case with a clip.

f725c358b61b46e5a42546b0eb1ef7f0.description: Degenesis is a post-apocalyptic 'Primal Punk' tabletop RPG. The hero uses a high-fidelity painterly illustration for instant world-building, with a slim vertical sidebar carrying navigation and branding to maximize space for the artwork. Dark, atmospheric charcoal-and-black palette with metallic gold highlights and sharp crimson accents; a single focal light source (the held object) guides the eye through the low-key composition.

2e09aeca9ead4243b22a3fa8cd8b2c45.description: Demophorius is a health-products company (existing tags point to a light, 3D, card-based, gradient scrolltelling build). The headless capture returned a blank frame with no rendered content, so visuals are unverified (client-side render did not complete in headless). The domain resolves; only the visual render could not be captured.

018f0d6bc53b41b590e1fd525e6c5151.description: Portfolio of Dennis Snellenberg, a Netherlands-based freelance designer and developer (Awwwards Site of the Day winner and Awwwards judge since 2019) known for minimalist, highly interactive sites built with GSAP, Barba.js and Locomotive Scroll. The hero is a full-screen portrait layout: a muted neutral-gray backdrop, the subject in a dark teal sweater, and his name set in bold oversized sans anchoring the lower third. Parallax depth layers the portrait between background and massive foreground type, and a signature interactive pill badge with a rotating globe plus mouse-follow motion give it life. A benchmark reference for parallax-rich, personality-driven developer-designer portfolios.

f568bef99073460f9d4e2cbdbe4a3ce4.description: Depo Studio — a digital design agency positioning on "We create award winning sites". The hero is a bento-box collage mixing the studio wordmark, headline and project imagery into one modular grid entry point. Neutral white/grey/charcoal base with a single vibrant Depo blue accent and a clean neo-grotesque throughout. Best block to steal: the transition into the portfolio, where a large blue circle expands to fill the viewport and lands on "Our Cases" with animated counters for cases, makeovers and stories — colour-block wipes used as section transitions. Also has a showreel video block, a four-quadrant services layout (Complete Website, UI, UX, Development), a scattered non-grid portfolio collage, and an awards section listing Awwwards, CSS Design Awards and FWA wins with dates.

9fc862ec28d0463d962c0873255e76ed.description: DePoly is a Swiss chemical-recycling company (Sion/Monthey) that depolymerises PET and polyester back into virgin-grade PTA and MEG at room temperature, positioned around "true material circularity". The site leads with a split hero: a large statement text card ("Our industries are still linear... DePoly enables material circularity") sitting over abstract macro photography of shredded plastic and fibres, in a muted eco-tech palette of sage, pale chartreuse, dusty blue and deep slate with a wide geometric sans. Worth stealing: using material macro-texture as background instead of literal product shots, and the legibility card pattern over busy imagery; the technology and offering pages carry a strong process/plant timeline narrative.

6f56cf428e17463484034be5c5b4a1ae.description: DES (Design Education Series) is Obys Agency's educational side project: paid mini-series on design fundamentals, currently three seasons (Typography Principles, Color Combinations, Grids) totalling around 49 episodes, sold as individual series or an all-series pass. Site by Obys (Awwwards Studio of the Year, European Design Awards winner) and documented in a Codrops case study: Three.js 3D objects mimic the proportions of the SVG/HTML elements so they collide and fall with real physics, with GSAP wiring the simulation to actual page content. Visuals unverified (numeric loader never resolves in headless render) so hero type is left unset; the season pages (/typography-principles, /grids) are the strongest inner pages.

704e4b4c38604921b3a2238d7e4c5e93.description: designstripe.com now 301-redirects to visual.app — the company rebranded to Visual, selling AI design agents for GTM/revenue teams, and the site is currently at waitlist stage. The hero is centred and minimal on off-white with charcoal text and high-contrast yellow accents, pairing an elegant high-contrast serif headline with monospace subtext and nav for an editorial-meets-tool feel. Distinctive touches are abstract organic shapes filled with checkerboard-transparency patterns and glitchy rectangular bars. Being pre-launch there is little else to mine beyond the hero and waitlist CTA; the old designstripe illustration/mockup library is gone.

06d6c8ee2dcc499ab105c8fd4c916244.description: DHNN is a design agency pitching "challengers through quality design". Starts as a minimal big-type statement on stark white, then a scroll-triggered reveal swaps the clean layout for a full-screen background video montage of urban and textured footage running behind the same typography, which is the main technique worth stealing. Monochrome throughout, bold modern sans headings. Nice details: a circular logo emblem in the top left that rotates to show the agency's 2007-2022 history, a pill-shaped animated scroll indicator, and a non-intrusive black cookie banner that stays on-brand.

3687b8e81d888032b1c4e35e1961f3a2.description: Australian health-tech startup mapping the "unified airway": its RhinoMAP platform combines nasal microsampling, proteomics and AI for precision respiratory diagnostics. Hero is a huge statement ("Eliminating respiratory disease. Forever.") over a teal-to-lime gradient with a translucent organic "bubble", subtle grain and ghost buttons. Unusual numbered stats rows (001–005) with real DOI citations as a footnote block — a rare scientific-credibility pattern; second stats set for clinical studies. Press/university logos marquee and a warm CTA close the page.

cf02b5ae85794addbb7e80a438648a18.description: Vienna-based full-service digital agency (~30 people from nine nations; clients include BYD, Subaru, Volvo, Bosch, Vienna Tourism, Zumtobel) covering digital and content strategy, web design, Webflow development, performance marketing and consulting. The company has rebranded to 'Achtzehn●Grad' — the digitalwerk.agency domain is still active and now serves the Achtzehn Grad site (same company, new name). Purely typographic hero: deep navy ground, white bold geometric sans set all-caps at extreme scale and cropped by the frame, with a vibrant orange accent. Distinctive: a live-updating metadata strip ('+ 06:14:12 | +42.7° | GOOD MORNING') that ties the eighteen-degrees brand name to real time-and-temperature data.

8ad4614ccc7349b1ae7067d6ba820dc7.description: Discovered Foods sells wild-harvested venison from free-ranging deer in Australia's high country, arguing an ethics and sustainability case (no feedlots, no live transport, invasive-species management) alongside chef credibility and a Delicious Produce Awards national title. The current design is moody and cinematic rather than the light flat style originally tagged here: chiaroscuro photography in charcoal and deep amber firelight against off-white, elegant high-contrast serif headlines paired with a minimal utility sans. Worth stealing: oversized low-opacity background type layered behind the imagery for editorial depth, and how strong lighting alone carries the "wild" narrative. An entry discount modal fires on load. Reference for premium provenance-led food e-commerce.

644b96decb7549208f70c7ffa2763e65.description: Display™ is an Australian disability- and care-oriented design studio that researches, plans and designs inclusive products with NDIS service providers. Strong example of healthcare/accessibility branding that avoids clinical cliché: warm cream background, vibrant coral and soft pink accents, charcoal body text. The hero mixes three typefaces in one headline — clean sans for “Shaping”, elegant serif italic for “the”, and a wide stylised sans with unusual terminals for “Care Sector” — alongside a vertical sidebar nav and playful minimal iconography (sparkles, flowers, accessibility symbols). Notable blocks: a single-figure stat callout (15% of the world experiences some form of disability, doubling by 2050), a four-card principles grid with custom SVG icons, a pull-quote block, and a featured-projects link-out to strong inner Works and Resources pages.

da672ab9d8124ab3ad4002eb10af243a.description: DNA Capital is a healthcare-focused investment partnership (São Paulo and San Francisco, backed by the Bueno family behind Brazilian health insurer AMIL) investing from early stage to private equity. The hero is premium and institutional: a dark charcoal field with off-white high-contrast serif brand statement, a subtle crimson accent line, a diamond 'MENU' control and a vertical 'Scroll to explore' cue, leaning on extreme negative space. Reference for restrained, editorial healthtech-finance branding.

0136e4d2bc4c4f32968b0682ee677323.description: Dominique Sire — personal site for a teacher of embodiment and soul-centred practice, selling courses such as The Maiden Series to women interested in body-led spiritual work. The hero is a full-bleed macro photograph of reddish-brown butterfly wings with "EMBODY the art of BEING HUMAN" set over it, establishing an organic, intimate register. Palette runs deep reds, muted pinks and salmon against rich forest green with off-white and charcoal type; typography deliberately alternates heavy sans caps for authority with delicate serif italics for nuance. Notable blocks: a course highlight with video trailer, a visual spirit-vs-soul contrast section, and an embedded audio player for a talk ("The Metaphor of the Tree"). Reference for full-screen type over macro nature imagery.

2ad22fe1f6fe40a08cecfc32131b3a39.description: Official site of Dom Pérignon, LVMH's prestige vintage champagne (the prestige cuvée of Moët & Chandon). The age gate is itself a mood piece worth studying: a moody wide-angle monochrome photo of bottles ageing in the cellar, a dark overlay, the elegant script wordmark and large semi-transparent YYYY placeholders for birth-year entry, all centred and symmetrical. Site content covers vintages, the house philosophy of only declaring a vintage in worthy years, and artist collaborations. Full hero and inner pages unverified (cookie-based age gate blocks the headless render), so hero type is left unset.

6babfaaf068c4794bcc74da44ed3e4c5.description: Furniture e-commerce, Awwwards Site of the Day. Dark WebGL-heavy experience with scroll-driven product storytelling (per saved tags: dark, 3D, cards, pattern, scrolltelling). Fully client-rendered; headless capture stalls on the branded 'g' loader even at 100%, so the screenshot shows the loader. Flagged for a re-shoot via full Chrome to capture the real hero and blocks.

46b0cd0d97fb4f2494cb48a9ec44a28b.description: Dragonfly is a leading crypto investment fund (Dragonfly Ventures, Dragonfly Liquid and Metastable, the oldest crypto hedge fund) with 160+ portfolio companies, investing seed to Series B from offices in New York and Singapore. The site is a single numbered scroll narrative (01 About, 02 Writing, 03 Team, 04 Portfolio, 05 Careers) that stacks compressed word lockups like GlobalSinceDay1 as graphic devices. Strongest reference blocks: a filterable Writing index with category chips (research / opinion / recruiting / legal), a large A-Z indexed portfolio directory with sector-tagged Spotlight cards, and a team grid with Show Bio reveals. Visuals unverified (JS/WebGL loader returned a blank frame in headless render), so no palette or hero details are claimed here.

ed22ac1a178a44f49e3b31b34bb67630.description: Lacoste holiday campaign microsite built around a single interactive toy: you draw and colour your own polo with brushes and stickers, then share it (#drawItYourself). The hero is a strictly centred grayscale wordmark that contrasts solid-fill "DRAW IT" against thin outlined "YOURSELF" — a cheap, stealable way to build hierarchy from one typeface without adding colour or weight. Everything else is the canvas: a WebGL polo you paint on, with an animated sticker preloader setting the playful tone before load completes. A good reference for brand-toy campaign sites where the product page is replaced by a creative tool.

c1dbdfd207104f9f909ac35ce18334ad.description: DrawHistory was a Perth-based social-impact strategy and design consultancy for the Asia-Pacific, immigrant-founded, BIPOC-owned, women-driven and a Certified B Corp, co-founded by Jeffrey Effendi and Angel Chen. The site is live but archived in tone: copy now reads in past tense and a persistent announcement modal covers its July 2025 integration into national impact agency Today, so it is a design reference rather than a live-agency reference. Visuals unverified (the announcement modal blocked the hero in headless render and the close-click retry was also blocked); from HTML the hero pairs the line Designing new futures for people, with people. with hand-drawn scribble illustration, and the modal uses muted olive drab (theme #3D3B2F), charcoal and white with a high-vis orange ticker and monospaced bulletin text. Notable: a 5-slide case-study carousel (Karitane rebrand, YouTube Creators for Change, ForWhen parent mental-health helpline) and a clients block where each logo carries a short narrative instead of sitting in a bare grid. Site credited to DrawHistory, Replica and Hatchet.

9bc72c1c98e449ef8b6e25bf989951d6.description: Advocacy scrollytelling piece about unreliable field drug test kits and the wrongful arrests they cause. Opens as a full-viewport intro: provocative all-caps hook on muted beige-taupe with a low-contrast line-art map behind, plus Skip Intro and Scroll Slowly prompts that set the pace for the narrative. Clean minimal UI keeps focus on the story. Good reference for editorial scrolltelling openers and pacing cues.

951ca8bc4ab54ff8b2e1e9fde3c980ca.description: Dead: the site serves its own branded error page reading "An unexpected error has occurred" on both the apex and www hosts across two attempts, so no real content is reachable. Only the chrome renders, a minimal white body over a beige footer bar with a central swan mark flanked by "THE CHRONICLES OF A CREATIVE STUDIO" and "BASED IN MALMÖ, SWEDEN". Dunderville is a Malmö creative studio; since the shell still renders this may be a CMS outage rather than a permanent death, worth a manual re-check.

6c813edccb6d473590ca0e9af82dbe83.description: Portfolio of Dylan Brouwer, a Dutch digital designer and Webflow developer (in-house at studio UNCOMMON, Enschede) with Awwwards recognition. The hero is typographic and kinetic: a massive uppercase grotesque headline where the word "MOVE" carries a motion-blur "ghosting" effect, set in dark-mode charcoal and slate gradients against a cream floral visual shown inside a 3D-tilted monitor mockup. Technical touches, plus-prefix navigation and live local-time/location metadata, reinforce a precise, developer-designer identity. A good reference for expressive, motion-led personal portfolios that signal both design taste and build skill.

01c5f777dcf5400789647a9d2a266f0c.description: Portfolio of Dyo Tanya, a freelance web designer working in Figma, Tilda and Webflow (Awwwards SOTD/HM and CSSDA badges on display). The hero is asymmetric editorial: an elegant high-contrast serif headline scattered off-grid across an off-white field, charcoal text inside a soft dusty-blue border, with a fluid hand-drawn scribble weaving through the type and overlapping a small circular portrait to add depth to an otherwise flat layout. The most useful block for a freelance/studio site is a nine-step numbered Process (01–09) leading into a project-brief CTA with explicit budget tiers (EUR 5000–12000+) — qualification built into the form. Also strong: looping marquee strips, client gallery and testimonials. Inner /smooth-scroll and /horscroll pages are technique demos. RU and EN versions.

a3d84a8fe14d48b6a114bd8ddc88b1eb.description: Eat My Socks is a Barcelona brand turning foods into whimsical socks and accessories (hair claws, scarves, pouches). The hero is a multi-panel lifestyle photo collage in a Gen-Z streetwear register, showing product re-purposed in unexpected ways such as socks worn as hair accessories, with different crops and angles creating movement across the fold. Palette pairs soft lavender with punchy coral-red CTAs against stark black-and-white type; a chunky distressed sans logotype sits against a high-contrast Didot-style serif and serif navigation. A lavender newsletter colour-block modal overlays the fold on load, acting as a visual rest-point against the busy photography.

16c7b8e81d8880989187e4fd2b431f74.description: ECI (Endowment for Climate Intelligence) is a non-profit that collectively owns and governs ClimateGPT, an open-source ensemble of climate-focused AI models trained on renewable energy, built with Erasmus.AI, Apptek and EQTY Lab. The hero is an editorial photo composition: a moody desert-at-dusk photograph inside a container with a very large corner radius, overlaid with a high-contrast cream display serif headline ("Artificial Intelligence for the Planet") against sandy ochre and desaturated teal-green tones. The signature move is editorial numbering — nav items and section tags carry small superscript indices (01, 02, 03...) so the whole site reads like a curated report, and even the cookie banner is styled into the design system instead of defaulting to a generic widget. Solar-panel video loops carry the "AI Powered by Nature" / Genesis Node section. Strong inner pages: /climategpt, /responsible-ai, /governance.

025a18e242af447e92b96601672f99fb.description: Ecopia AI digitizes geospatial imagery with AI, producing high-definition vector maps at scale for civil engineering, insurance, telecom and government. The whole site uses the product as its visual language: satellite imagery with coloured vector overlays is the hero, and map textures reappear as backgrounds for later sections, so the value prop is demonstrated rather than described. Palette is white, soft mint green and dark charcoal with a clean professional sans. Notable blocks: a features trio (Accurate / Scalable / Up-to-date) built on map imagery, an industries/use-case list with preview images, a credible logos bar (World Bank, Snap Inc., ESRI) and a full-bleed map-background CTA.

2bd9051bab37453891495d206925b5b5.description: Edifis is a purpose-driven industrial real-estate developer and manager near Montreal (Mirabel/YMX campus), renting modular industrial space and running mixed-use and residential projects. The homepage hero is a WebGL 3D scene in which the Edifis logo morphs into a building the cursor can orbit, with an interactive 'Press enter to open loading doors' prompt on the truck bays. Notable blocks: an image-slider stats set (1M ft², 5 Buildings, 10 Corporate Tenants), vertical MP4 space cards, a tenant logo bar (Airbus, Foliot, Syscomax) and a named-executive testimonial carousel; deep navy brand colour. Site by Tux. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render).

7ac527d4649c47028287e7a7e310c42b.description: Type specimen site for Editorial New, the narrow high-contrast serif by Mathieu Desjardins for Pangram Pangram, with the site built by Locomotive and recognised by Awwwards. The hero is a single skeuomorphic "digital poster" specimen floating in a charcoal void — a cream page centred against near-black, framed by a vertical table-of-contents sidebar and a working Invert Colors toggle, with one Get the font CTA in a minimal top bar. Excellent reference for foundry and single-product launch pages: full-screen specimen isolated in negative space, everything else stripped out.

d9b5d1fecccb4b9ca283dc6df37b2f24.description: The editorx.com domain now serves Wix Studio — the Editor X brand was fully retired and folded into Wix's platform for agencies and enterprises, so the original Editor X design is gone. What is there now: a centred big-type hero on a near-monochrome black-and-white canvas with generous whitespace and a single electric-purple CTA as the only colour accent, in a clean modern sans with a heavy headline weight. A partial product-interface mockup is cropped at the bottom edge to tease the editor and pull the eye downward. Still a decent reference for premium minimal SaaS heroes where one saturated accent carries all the emphasis.

2147b8e81d88803593b9c6e90e63dbf0.description: Effortel is a Belgian MVNE/telecom platform (Effortel Mobile Suite, MVNO LaunchPad, eSIM and IoT enablement) that lets brands launch and run virtual mobile networks. The hero is radically image-free and type-driven: deep charcoal ground, a massive heavy sans headline, electric-cyan accents, and technical uppercase mono micro-copy wrapped in brackets for an engineered feel, plus an animated percentage counter as an award stat. Notable blocks: a full-width client logo marquee (Vodafone, Orange, Carrefour, Telenet) where each logo links to a case study, a numbered 01-04 product feature sequence, a bento of LaunchPad benefits, and an unusual year-stamped awards timeline (2016-2024). Site by Onion (onioncreative.studio).

3177b8e81d8880a59ca6e83379725966.description: EigenPal (YC-backed, San Francisco) is an eval-first document automation platform: you show its AI agent 3-5 example documents, it builds the extraction workflow, then proves accuracy on your historical data before anything goes live. The hero is deliberately technical minimalism, a monospaced headline and subheadline on a soft off-white ground with a faint background grid, a purple gradient CTA, and the Y Combinator badge parked directly above the H1 as social proof. Notable blocks: a three-card value trio (Learns from examples / Test before you trust / Deploy anywhere), a Loom-embedded process walkthrough, a US retail bank case study with hard numbers (80% faster, 93% straight-through automation, 2 months to production), an accuracy split showing 87% automation-ready vs 13% needing human validation, a deployment grid (AWS / Azure / GCP / on-prem) with compliance badges, and a side-by-side Traditional workflow tools vs EigenPal AI Copilot comparison (2-4 weeks vs 5 minutes). Site by Grafit. Good reference for eval-first AI positioning and honest accuracy communication.

1d07b8e81d88808abd4adf70356684db.description: Einride is a Swedish company building electric and autonomous road-freight infrastructure (trucks, smart charging, and the Saga AI operating system). Built on Framer. The hero is a full-bleed cinematic Vimeo loop, an extreme close-up of autonomous truck hardware, shot in a moody near-monochrome palette of blacks, deep blues and hard white highlights, with navigation pushed to the far corners so the footage owns the frame. Restrained sans-serif typography throughout. Strongest block is the four-pillar platform module (Autonomous / Electric freight / Charging / Saga AI) where each card opens into its own page, plus a partner-proof section naming PepsiCo, Heineken, DP World and Mars. Good reference for premium industrial tech with heavy video and near-zero visual noise.

2147b8e81d8880489abbf46529a30c68.description: EISLAB is a Düsseldorf-based premium artisanal ice-cream brand (four German stores) that doubles as a franchise pitch. The hero is a split composition: an oversized ultra-condensed heavy sans headline with a 3D-style emoji substituted directly into the type, set against a high-saturation top-down product photo — deep navy, vibrant orange and off-white with pastel purple accents. Steal-worthy: the emoji-in-headline typographic trick, tactile overhead food photography, a horizontally scrolling flavour selector with cut-out product PNGs, a large playground image-wall gallery, and a repeating BECOME A FRANCHISE PARTNER marquee. Awwwards-featured; site by Huyml (huyml.co), built on Next.js + Prismic.

619cc91ccbfe4577a2e724f5f407ead9.description: Electronic Materials Office is a London consumer-hardware company whose sole product, the Altar I, is an ultra-low-profile wireless mechanical keyboard in a precision-machined recyclable aluminium monobody with waste-derived polymer, Kailh Choc switches and ZMK firmware (currently sold out, so the whole site funnels to a waitlist). The hero is a player-as-frame treatment: a cinematic launch-film player UI wrapping a high-fidelity product render on a stealth matte charcoal/black/silver palette with a single high-visibility orange accent. Typography is a deliberate industrial-luxe clash, editorial serif (Tobias, Displaay) against an ultra-wide geometric sans (GT Flexa, Grilli Type), both credited openly in the spec table. Most stealable block: an orthographic/isometric CAD-drawing technical specification section pairing engineering line drawings with a dense spec list; section headers also repeat four times as marquee bands.

6f19036ed9a44c02ad712451392b6b12.description: Elegant Seagulls is a Michigan-founded digital creative and brand agency ('Creative that converts', 'Ugly birds, beautiful ideas') with work for Audible, Red Bull, Lionsgate and ESPN. The homepage runs a reel video section, a client logos bar, a deep case-study set (Verint, Dig Insights, Booksy, Invicti, Audible, Lionsgate), a conversion stat (99% lift for Quest Nutrition) and Strategy/Creative/Branding/Development service blocks. Experimental WebGL work lives on decade. and demo. subdomains. Visuals unverified — the hero is a react-three-fiber 3D scene that fails in headless render and exposes a raw WebGL stack trace instead of degrading gracefully, so hero type is left unset.

3177b8e81d8880ee87c5caa64afc0182.description: ElevenLabs is the AI audio platform (text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing, conversational agents). The homepage is a masterclass in restrained multi-product presentation: a clean white and black base warmed by soft grainy pastel gradients (lavender, peach, sage, sky) rendered as abstract 3D blobs, a bold sans headline with sharp hierarchy, and rounded card-on-card containers with soft shadows for depth. The key move is an embedded product tab strip inside the hero, letting a broad product ecosystem be shown without a cluttered nav or a wall of feature cards. The grain applied over the gradients is what keeps it feeling premium rather than generic SaaS. Reference for light-mode AI branding, tasteful noise/grain treatment and multi-product hero tabs.

8efb941ff1f14085b59e2c037794b3cc.description: Dead: the domain still responds but renders a completely blank off-white page with no markup, text or branding across three separate capture attempts (two scroll recordings and one static render), suggesting a failed front-end build or a geo/bot block rather than a live site. Originally saved as the English site for Mana Yerba Mate. Worth a manual re-check from a normal browser before removing.

e3fa1cf12db84ce58f847505af424a34.description: A Richard Mille microsite celebrating the RM 07-01 Coloured Ceramics launch, built as a "never-ending summer" experience that invites visitors to deep-dive into the essence of a summer day and let the colour of their summer guide them to a matching timepiece. It is a client-rendered Next.js app that ships an empty HTML body and threw an "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred" in the headless render, so hero composition, palette and typography could not be observed — visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render). Meta and copy confirm an immersive, colour-driven single-product narrative for luxury watchmaking; worth opening manually in a real browser to assess.

3687b8e81d88804a85cbcdf45f99c743.description: Industrialized construction system (Spain), brutalist-technical aesthetic. Vermilion red and black hero with exposed grid lines like an architectural blueprint, heavyweight grotesque headline against tiny utility metadata (SYSTEM, EST. 2025), background process video. Below: numbered solution sections 01-04 with tall photography, project cases labeled with plan numbers (P112, P158), value cards, factory replication pitch. Strong ref for construction and industrial B2B with editorial-brutalist layout and drawing-style annotations.

0c128f99b252454898945080209a315e.description: Energy Park is a UK B-Corp certified EV charge-point operator specialising in retrofitting apartment blocks and other multi-family dwellings, and acting as a long-term CPO for landlords rather than just an installer. The site is built around a hardware picker covering eight charge points with kW specs (Zaptec Go and Pro, EO Mini Pro 3, EO Genius 2, Easee One and Charge, Garo Entity Pro, Schneider EVlink Pro AC), a manufacturer partners block, and a bespoke-solution contact CTA. Visuals unverified: the site returns a 403 to headless renderers, so hero type is left unset; the saved tags describe a light, card-based, big-type layout with motion.

95a7916dd4e741fcb6668cbfa6353e0d.description: Escape Coffee Company is a Montreal specialty roaster with a cycling-culture streak, selling single-origin beans and blends online. Full-screen big-type hero: oversized cropped all-caps lettering in warm greys on off-white, with a minimalist vertical sidebar holding navigation and shipping info. Playful brand-aligned cookie banner copy (Want some cookies with your coffee?). Good reference for typographic e-commerce heroes and sidebar navigation.

ba6a5f6d428d4ff49b3feefe5a2f5a6a.description: ESPN long-form editorial feature on tennis player Carlos Alcaraz, built as a full scrollytelling story. The hero is a layered parallax illustration of Alcaraz on vivid blue with his name in massive condensed sans, and career stats reveal progressively as you scroll down his body — a strong reference for an unusual stats block. Later sections pin a green tennis-court illustration as a sticky background while text scrolls past, with a ball that bounces in sync with scroll progress, plus bar-chart data viz comparing him to Federer and illustrated pull quotes. Also worth stealing: the achievements marquee ticker under the hero and video clips embedded inline in the reading flow.

2435d385215347b1ac4c26f2cd8d2bf4.description: Estudios Victor Cordon is a performing arts and dance hub in Lisbon running programmes, residencies and choreography. Cinematic full-screen hero video of a dancer in slow motion on black, overlaid with a very bold condensed display font, held in strict monochrome throughout. Notable blocks: horizontal featured carousels for individual events (Kick Off '26) that introduce lateral movement inside a vertical scroll, a cleanly ranked programme grid, and a well-organised sitemap footer with partner logos. Good dark-mode reference for arts and culture where typography-as-graphic defines the space.

027e1ca9c2d84674b50fda746d67be7b.description: Ethnocare is a Montreal medical-device company selling the Overlay, a breathable fabric sleeve with an integrated air expansion system that manages residual-limb volume and socket fit for transtibial and transfemoral amputees. The hero is stark dark-mode: a true-black ground with "OVERLAY" set wall-to-wall in a heavy extended geometric sans in mid-grey, no imagery at all — a metallic, clinical-industrial authority that is rare in healthcare UI and very stealable. A thin announcement bar carries the HCPCS reimbursement code without breaking the aesthetic. Notable blocks: a TT/TF product toggle that drives specs and downloads, a numbered five-step how-to-wear sequence, an amputee testimonial with portrait, and a country-by-country distributor directory. Site by Locomotive.

2887b8e81d8880898fd0f687463de041.description: Euveka is a French fashion-tech company building Emili and Emineo, adaptive robotic mannequins that morph into roughly 10,000 body shapes for apparel, sport, medical and defence prototyping (Nike, adidas, SMCP among its customers). Framer build with a minimalist product-centric hero: the dark robotic mannequin sits centred in the foreground with the headline layered behind the object to create depth, over a low-contrast charcoal on warm-sand palette. High-contrast serif headline against wide-tracked sans labels, moody low-key product lighting, a subtle technical background grid signalling precision engineering, and a scroll-to-reveal cue. Strong stats section (10,000 fits, 90 seconds, 80% of body types, 40% less prototyping) plus a bento grid of product details. Site by tonik.

508c8ff798194212b47c78b08b8f0d68.description: EventBeds is a UK booking platform for event-adjacent hotel accommodation, aggregating 1M+ rooms across 180 countries with event-exclusive discount codes and secret rates. The hero is a soft clay-render 3D cityscape in monochrome off-white and grey with a phone mockup planted inside it and floating lime-green price bubbles placed at varying depths — the mixed 2D-mockup-in-a-3D-world trick is the thing to steal. Type is an extra-bold uppercase sans with deliberately overlapping letterforms in "STAY", and lime green carries the CTAs and logo mark. Notable blocks: a three-step phone-screen walkthrough (Preference/Save/Book), an infinite partner-logo marquee, a hotel-brand card wall, and a co-founder letter with headshots. Site by Outcrowd.

3ff84a4af7a74b9db7b478edaf9a22df.description: Everyday Robots was Alphabet X's helper-robot project, presented with clean, tech-forward design. The hero is a product photo of a robotic arm at work in a real environment (sorting recycling), using environmental storytelling and a shallow depth of field to communicate practical utility while keeping focus on the hardware. Clinical white, grey and black neutrals are punctuated by functional yellow accents on the robot's joints.

0c91fa9148354104a91ff423b058e67b.description: Portfolio site of Exo Ape, a Netherlands-based global digital design studio known for immersive, WebGL-driven experiences and awards from Awwwards, FWA and Communication Arts. The hero is photography-led: a full-bleed, blue-hour architectural image in deep navy and slate, crisp white sans copy with warm golden highlights, and a massive bold display word cropped at the bottom edge to imply scale. Fluid scroll-based motion and “scroll to explore” cues carry you into a curated grid of case-study work. A benchmark reference for cinematic, emotion-led studio branding where oversized type and full-bleed imagery do the talking.

d191c9a4c32144f895d0ba5b93e5585a.description: Immersive product microsite for the Dr. Dabber Boost EVO, a portable electric dab rig (e-rig), built by studio Locomotive as a cinematic “experience” rather than a plain product page. It opens with a 21+ age gate wrapped in a cyberpunk loader (cyan-on-black, monospace terminal copy like “receiving transmission / initiate handshake protocol”). Inside, full-bleed product videos drive the story alongside feature blocks (six calibrated heat settings, patented atomizer, quartz-to-glass vapor path), a “Rise” marquee, pricing, and a product collection grid. Strong reference for narrative, video-led DTC product storytelling. Note: the headless render stayed behind the age gate/WebGL loader, so full visuals are described from HTML plus the verified loader aesthetic.

08f7ede2f5d34ccdbb5b426aa49d6211.description: Fabric Ventures is a thesis-driven VC that has backed Web3 since 2012 and now brands itself "Venture Capital For The Machine Economy" across robotics, AI, fintech and distributed computing, with 196 companies backed plus the R[3]sidency accelerator. The homepage is an unusually confident diagrammatic hero: an off-white grained background with a faint visible architectural grid, black neo-grotesque type, and information cards wired to nodes by thin diagonal connector lines, so the hero doubles as the primary navigation into About, Portfolio, Team and R[3]sidency — a strong reference for turning a nav into the visual idea. A single vibrant orange accent appears only in the R[3] brand element, and the micro-grain keeps the minimalism tactile rather than sterile. A public Brand Kit / styleguide page is worth a look.

66eff1e300c64b1088266772cb1c63bb.description: Fallen Grape is a Shopify DTC brand selling organically farmed, low-intervention natural wine from California's Central Coast. Both the 21+ age gate and the hero run on a warm earthy palette (sage, terracotta, dusty ochre, muted lavender) with a high-contrast serif headline and a grain overlay that gives the whole thing a tactile, printed feel. The hero's trick is product-as-art: the bottle is drawn into the illustration style rather than photographed, and foreground foliage layers over it to build depth in a flat 2D scene. Below it is mostly lifestyle gallery and commerce grids, closing on a newsletter CTA ('Great wine makes life better').

d49f79234a0244489adfdbd2750176df.description: Site of Pablo Farias, an Argentine-born master luthier based in Cremona, Italy, hand-making violins, violas and cellos in modern and baroque styles. The homepage uses atmospheric photography as the interface — a non-linear grid of image tiles ('Creations', 'Interview', 'Contacts') in sophisticated monochrome with a single warm orange-brown color-pop on one violin to guide the eye, set in a tall high-contrast condensed serif. Reference for photo-as-navigation and minimalist color-pop wayfinding on a craft/artisan site.

3177b8e81d8880ce9112d7d5a87cd653.description: Farm Minerals (SOSV-backed) makes carbon-encapsulated fertilizers and feed additives, headlined by CropTab, a 13 g tablet claimed to replace up to 150 kg of bulk NPK with near-100% uptake and zero manufacturing emissions. The hero shoots the tablet like a luxury object: museum-style spotlight on a metallic pedestal against a forest-to-sage green gradient, hyper-real grainy capsule texture against smooth chrome, framed by a large geometric sans headline (Fertilizer, Reinvented.). Notable blocks: a problem-framing section built on a full-bleed corn video with a single FAO stat (up to 70% of nitrogen is lost before crops can use it), a product-anatomy feature list (smaller than a plant cell, just drop it, zero emissions, zero run-off), a hard results stat row (4 continents tested, 100x lower transport cost, 0.5 ton CO2 saved per acre, 5x return), an interactive world map of live field trials by country and crop, a three-product card set, a next-update transparency note and a qualification-gated early-access application form. Site by adelt.io. Excellent reference for AgTech premiumisation and stats-led credibility.

9045f395d3d7429ab70d7c33197d8662.description: Vestiaire Collective's 2023 Fashion Sustainability / Impact Report, built as a standalone scrollytelling microsite rather than a PDF. Opens on a themed percentage loader (0–100%) that sequences geometric and organic shapes — sunbursts, grids, interlocking circles — into place before the site resolves. Soft modern palette of sage green, pale cornflower blue, bright yellow and coral on a grainy off-white paper texture, with a high-contrast elegant serif for headlines against minimalist sans utility type. The hero is a split-screen: sage colour block carrying "Our Unique Model Has A Unique Impact" beside a high-fashion editorial photograph, with a thin fixed top bar holding breadcrumbs and a download-the-full-report link. Good reference for turning a corporate ESG report into a brand piece. Sections below the hero unverified (loader delayed the headless render).

3a37b8e81d88801eaa96cfcad3d0a4fb.description: Fauna Robotics (NYC, now an Amazon company) makes Sprout, a 3.5-ft soft-bodied humanoid developer platform. The hero is a centred product layout: bold geometric sans with rounded terminals and tight tracking ("Capable, safe, fun. Robots for everyone.") on a warm cream ground, coral-orange CTAs and a large rounded-corner video window — a deliberate rejection of cold blue robotics tropes for a friendly lifestyle palette. Distinctive blocks: a "Trusted by" logo bar (Disney, Boston Dynamics, UCSD), a three-column audience split for developers/enterprises/researchers, abstract SVG blob shapes as use-case icons, and a masonry "Real robots, real fun" UGC video wall — a strong pattern for showing hardware in the wild. Webflow.

763c022546e54188a588a009fffb3e67.description: Ferrumpipe manufactures galvanised steel fences and security gates using a weld-free folded-seam technology; this is the live demo domain for the award-winning Cuberto project (Awwwards SOTD, CSS Design Awards, FWA). The hero is airy and white with a medium-weight geometric sans headline and a soft peach button, dominated by a large shaded 3D render of glossy emerald-to-mint diagonal pipes filling roughly half the viewport — deep forest green type, generous whitespace, subtle light-and-shadow gradients. The rest of the page walks through the production line via 3D scroll sequences and filmed full-cycle video. Site by Cuberto.

a2d319916ab344229ea0db92cfbd8ec8.description: Fey was a premium financial-research and portfolio terminal for retail investors — broker sync, a keyboard-driven Fey Command palette, and curated asset pages stripped of noise. The original dark, 3D-heavy product site has been replaced by a single announcement page saying Fey has joined Wealthsimple: near-monochrome off-white ground, dark charcoal text, zero imagery, generous whitespace, and three hand-drawn founder signatures at the bottom. Worth keeping as a reference for a dignified acquisition or sunset page; the original product design now only survives in archives.

f7cb2da4dffd49e8b0a5b249c1956085.description: Field Day is a creative sound and music company doing sound design, original music and mixing. Extremely stripped-back off-white and black layout with pink accents, mixing an elegant script logo, clean sans navigation and a bold ultra-condensed tall sans for the main event. Two things worth stealing: a branded loader that shows a loading percentage alongside the actual value proposition ("We are a creative sound and music company") instead of a bare spinner, and a giant horizontal client ticker (Nike, Yeti, Manscaped) running across the viewport that turns the logos bar into the primary graphic element and instant credibility in one move.

50f77773c5324a5ebd8e7cf72ca7a2d7.description: Figma's editorial marketing page explaining variable fonts, how a single file carries the full range of weight, width, grade, and optical-size axes instead of shipping separate files. Built as a high-impact typographic display: a lavender background with pop accents (emerald, coral-salmon, golden yellow), bold high-contrast sans headlines, and oversized geometric sticker motifs that break the grid. The standout technique is scroll-triggered variable-font animation where weight and width shift fluidly as you scroll, alongside interactive axis toggles and a linked Figma playground file. A strong reference for teaching a technical concept through live, expressive type.

21b7b8e81d888037a9daed4708a7b64a.description: Fin (formerly Intercom, now fully renamed) sells an AI customer agent for support, sales and ecommerce. The hero is an oversized editorial serif headline in black on off-white cream, anchored by a large high-fidelity 3D render in warm metallic copper — the scale contrast between giant type and a larger-than-life object is the main technique. The whole homepage is one long numbered manifesto, "22 reasons to hire Fin", with bracket-numbered markers ([ 01.A ], [ Personio ]) and hard performance numbers baked into the copy (76% resolution rate, 2M weekly resolutions, $400M ARR, -65% hallucinations) — a strong reference for a stats-heavy, list-as-narrative homepage rather than conventional feature blocks. Also notable: a real headshot grid of the deployment and AI-engineering team, plus inline demo videos attached to each claim.

ea2d144a938c4ad0852f3fcfb634020c.description: Fitonist is an AI gym workout planner for iOS, Android and Apple Watch (600+ exercises, adaptive plans, Apple Health sync); landing designed by Outcrowd, an Awwwards SOTD. Note: saved link is the Webflow staging domain, production lives at fitonist.com. Hero layers phone and watch mockups over a pastel blue-lavender gradient inside a rounded light container on a dark backdrop, with blurred 3D spheres for texture and bold geometric sans headlines. Good reference for dark-plus-pastel app ecosystems shots.

cd56cbffc25143b9bd71784adba3dce2.description: Fitsole is an Egyptian (Cairo) sneaker and lifestyle retailer on Shopify carrying Adidas, Nike, Puma, Jordan, Converse and NBA product; this URL is a standard Ozelle Cloudfoam PDP. The identity is sharp and high-contrast — white chrome on a black stage, all-caps sans nav, and a bold red italic wordmark where red is reserved almost entirely for sale flags, a disciplined single-accent system worth stealing. Product shots are consistently background-removed on transparent PNG with a hover-swap to a second angle, and promo type deliberately runs low-contrast dark-on-black for a fashion feel. The homepage carries the stronger blocks: a live countdown flash-sale timer, an audience splitter (Men/Women/Kids), a shop-by-sport selector, a brand logos bar and a 4.9★ testimonial carousel.

3177b8e81d8880a19916fe478cc979f5.description: Flank (Berlin) sells autonomous AI agents that run high-volume in-house legal work end to end (intake, drafting, redlining, negotiation, review) inside Outlook, Teams, Jira and Salesforce, so lawyers only touch finished work and high-risk moments. The hero is a split layout: an organic, high-fidelity 3D render on the left against a dark charcoal panel on the right, with the headline mixing roman and italic weights (Insource legal work to supervised agents) and compliance badges (SOC 2 Type II, GDPR/CCPA, ISO 42001) sitting directly under it as instant trust. A slim live-webinar ribbon runs above the nav.
