34e7b8e81d88801497ffcc24742c89a7.description: Isidor is an applied-research company (SF + London; backed by Seedcamp and Gradient) that turns raw enterprise data into RL-ready training pipelines: evals, verifiers, reasoning-trace data and post-training. "Tech-noir blueprint" aesthetic: deep cobalt-to-navy gradient, generative topographic waveforms, dashed borders and corner-tick markers on cards, monospace section tags (INTRO) next to clean sans headlines. Numbered 01-05 capability cards, investor/angel logos wall (DeepMind, JPMorgan, Apple), a plus-sign grid pattern divider and Greenhouse job cards. Strong reference for engineering-credibility visual language in AI infrastructure.

3177b8e81d8880488038ca2b1c9c304a.description: ISO Meet is a waitlist landing page for an upcoming iOS app that lets creative professionals (photographers, models, stylists, videographers, makeup artists) connect, collaborate and get hired in one verified space; built by the team behind Superb Studio. The hero is a split composition: an editorial headline that mixes upright and italic glyphs inside single words, a floating minimalist profile card overlaid on warm lifestyle photography, and a subtle "5,000+ creatives" social-proof row. The standout block is a dual-row infinite marquee of role cards (Photographers, Models, Drone operators, Florists) that communicates breadth without a list. Also has a Hirer/Talent tabbed feature flow, a paid $10 username-reservation form with FAQ, and a clean off-white/black palette with soft gradient washes.

5be127d2f5404b84a4e6232e895bcbcf.description: Jacques Marie Mage is a Los Angeles luxury house of collectible, limited-edition eyewear handcrafted in Japan and Italy, extended into jewelry, small leather goods and the Circa Compagnon objects collection. The Shopify site leads with full-width editorial product photography (oxblood leather on leopard print) under a minimalist black-on-white header pairing a stylized serif logo with widely-spaced uppercase sans nav. Textural layering and diagonal product placement make the imagery the brand ambassador, and a standout worldwide Galleries grid presents each boutique as a photo card with address and "schedule an appointment". Strong reference for high-fashion minimalism, heritage storytelling, and letting rich imagery carry a spacious UI.

2497b8e81d888080bd38f0ea7db6e84f.description: Jasper is an AI-agents platform for enterprise marketing teams (100+ specialized agents, a brand-governance "IQ" layer, GEO / AI-search optimization), built in Webflow. The hero is centered and text-first: a high-contrast authoritative serif headline in deep navy on off-white, geometric sans for nav and sub-copy, a small feature-chip announcement badge above the headline, and orange-red reserved strictly for the primary CTA — generous whitespace, no hero imagery. Techniques worth stealing: Rive-animated feature cards, customer-story stat cards used as social proof (10,000+ hours saved, 7,500 product descriptions in 24h), a role-switcher tab block whose cursors are little photo avatars, and a paper-texture footer. The navy-plus-orange serif direction is a deliberate move away from the usual purple AI-SaaS look. Strong inner pages: /agents, /platform, /geo.

1d07b8e81d8880f2aa80f5d4c76db7b3.description: Jeton is a UK-licensed global e-wallet and multi-currency card (1M+ users, 25 countries, 50+ payment methods). Site by Buró / Burocratik. Big-type hero over a warm salmon-to-coral gradient with vast negative space, and the navigation moved into a floating translucent pill bar at the bottom of the viewport rather than the top, which is the single most stealable move here. The standout block is a five-step interactive payment walkthrough (Account, Add, Method, Review, Done) with a Restart control, letting you replay the flow without signing up, plus a live currency-exchange widget. Also has a testimonial wall, a compliance/trust badge row (ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials, FT 1000), and a West Ham sponsorship module. Good reference for fintech that wants energy without looking cheap.

47b9e1cc932446c9a0ab286436e71c26.description: Product detail page for "The Dora" eyeglasses from French eyewear brand Jimmy Fairly. Neutral white and caramel palette, elegant serif headings over clean sans body copy, large-scale product photography and a deliberately minimal layout. Useful reference for a premium DTC product page that sells on imagery and restraint instead of badges, countdowns and urgency stacking, with the gallery and feature blocks carrying the specs.

2147b8e81d8880f4a37ec1d51e6a4015.description: Jitter is a browser-based collaborative motion-design tool (Figma import, keyframe-free timeline, Lottie/4K export, AI Superagents). The homepage hero is a restrained SaaS-minimalist layout: pure white and deep black with a lavender accent, an extra-bold geometric sans headline with tight tracking, an announcement pill badge above the headline, and a desaturated logo bar (Google, TikTok) for instant social proof. Its real design value sits in the product pages, which are dense with looping animated feature demos — every capability (masks, gradients, easing presets, text-by-letter animation) is shown as motion rather than a static screenshot — plus a 300+ template gallery and customer stories (Perplexity, Deliveroo). Strong inner pages: /product, /templates, /customers.

58dc3ddf75f64c9d875bfbfa73f220dc.description: E-commerce site for JOCO, an Australian brand of artisan-blown borosilicate glass reusable coffee cups, bottles and flasks, positioned as an anti-single-use-plastic lifestyle brand. Hero is a full-bleed lifestyle photo carousel with the product held at eye level in an urban setting, sophisticated neutrals (charcoal, black, crisp white, muted grey-brown), an elegant serif headline over a strategically darkened image area, paired with a functional sans for nav and outlined CTAs; carousel dots are deliberately unobtrusive. Beyond the hero: a product-category tile grid, a "Turning The Tide" sustainability section built on a full-width autoplaying video, and a live Instagram UGC grid. WooCommerce/WordPress with regional storefronts and a region-picker modal.

344c16272cd948dd898e00ac95c80184.description: Clyde (now part of Cover Genius) is an e-commerce "ownership enrichment" platform for DTC brands, extended warranties, product registration, global shipping protection and automated claims resolution from one integration. Site credited to Studio Freight. The hero is illustration-led with a rotating set of playful product illustrations and bold sans (Inter) messaging; below it, a floating product gallery, a logos bar (SharkNinja, Marshall, Tempo, Bugaboo, Raycon), a scrolling marquee of benefits, hard-hitting stats (78% would spend more, NPS +65), testimonials and case studies (Lull, Senville, Liteboxer). Strong reference for making an intangible service (insurance/warranties) feel like a tangible product. Note: headless render returned a loader, so visual palette is described from HTML rather than a verified screenshot.

34e7b8e81d8880a28a8ee9a70fe414bc.description: AI mental health companion by Sword Health. Split hero: elegant serif over warm sunset tones left, photographic portrait right, a dotted-to-solid arc line bridging both panels into the CTA. Below: benefit chapters with soft gradients and circle doodles, expert credibility cards (Harvard, Yale, Stanford), past-vs-future comparison columns, large testimonial wall, FAQ. Strong ref for calm healthtech with emotional storytelling plus clinical trust signals.

54b544c05936448cbfcc19f72adeaac9.description: MITA is a marketplace where fans buy and trade shares in artists' companies, which collect income from music royalties, shows and merch. The page is structured around five value blocks: joining an artist's first offering or buying later in the open market, a members' social feed ('like X but for music'), artist discovery, portfolio tracking with custom artist watchlists, and a collection you can show off. Visuals unverified: the headless renderer crashed repeatedly on this site (typical for heavy WebGL/3D), so hero type is left unset and no visual details are invented; the saved tags describe a dark, 3D, big-type layout with horizontal scrolling and visible borders.

cb89905978554231bc532270e89d6567.description: SPARQ is a $129 one-time-purchase OBD-II car diagnostics dongle plus an AI companion app (SEMA 2025 Product Award winner) that gives drivers mechanic-grade inspections and a conversational AI to ask about their car; built on Framer. The hero is minimal big type (Get to know your car intimately) on a light-grey ground with black type and a vibrant orange-red CTA accent, with the phone app UI cresting into frame below. Rich inner scroll: an animated health-score counter (0-100), a systems checklist running a live diagnostic sweep, phone-UI showcases for photo and audio diagnostics, and a blunt subscription comparison table pitting $0/month against Others $20/month. Good reference for healthcare-style diagnostic UI patterns applied to automotive.

be8ab63889444a40a5a35d8e5217319c.description: Shopify storefront for Joseph Joseph, the London design-led housewares brand (kitchenware, cookware, storage, laundry, bathroom) founded by twin brothers Antony and Richard Joseph. Hero is an atmospheric video lifestyle scene with a light-weight sans headline ("A place for everything.") centred over a darkened overlay and a bold all-caps CTA; palette is earthy and muted — sage, forest green, charcoal, stone and ecru — matched to the product colourways. Worth studying: the press-quote marquee (VOGUE, ELLE, LIVING ETC), the "Your home, your way" category carousel of large image cards, and New In / Bestsellers product rails. Inner pages of note: /pages/our-story, /pages/awards and the UGC gallery. Regional sites with an entry localisation modal.

3687b8e81d888022ad1accc4b1fc1f76.description: Portfolio of freelance design director Juan Mora (Webflow, GSAP, Lottie). Hero: massive name split by an inline media window ('Juan [work] Mora') in warm sepia-copper palette; scroll-driven shape animations with click/scroll counters. Below: service sections with looping project videos, playful folder icon linking to work, value checklist, tools credited in footer. Strong ref for personal portfolios with type-as-layout and dense micro-interactions.

91acd901f6b94e9eb34eaeeb1281d96d.description: Kanak Naturals makes sustainable, compostable packaging and dinnerware from bamboo and sugarcane bagasse for foodservice, retail and medical clients (Fort Wayne, Indiana; plants in India and UK). Earthy big-type hero on a textured paper-grain beige with charcoal type and orange and olive accents. Brand voice swaps C for K everywhere (KUSTOM, KONSCIOUS, KONTACT), backed by a physical ribbon-style contact tab and a circular endorsement badge. Good reference for tactile eco branding with horizontal-scroll product sections.

1558b9204ea245639978ac527a56866b.description: Site of KARAK, an Austrian (Vorarlberg) studio making handmade Raku-fired ceramic tiles to order using a centuries-old technique, where each glowing tile is pulled from the furnace into sawdust so no two are alike (founded by Sebastian and Thomas, now a ~9-person team expanding into architecture, furniture and lighting). The full-bleed hero is moody and monochrome, deep blacks and textured grays that echo the scorched Raku aesthetic, with sophisticated serif headlines against minimalist sans. Its standout technique is extreme macro-photography of tile textures paired with small inset process videos, giving a sparse, elegant layout a strong sense of materiality. A benchmark for tactile, craft-led brand storytelling where the material is the hero.

b9332b73fa2743faa4a82b538387c0f0.description: Campaign microsite for Kasama ('togetherness' in Filipino), a collection from fine-jewelry brand Limnia, built as a one-page ?section= experience that links out to limnia.com for commerce. The interesting move is editorial-as-merchandising: instead of a product page, the collection sits alongside cocktail recipes, a curated Spotify playlist, book picks and podcast picks, so the jewelry is sold through a world rather than a grid. Warm terracotta and beige lifestyle photography, high-contrast serif headlines against all-caps sans labels, and forms built from simple underlines rather than boxes so imagery stays dominant. Hero unverified — a full-screen 'Join the circle' email-capture modal blocks the render in headless and would not dismiss.

1d27b8e81d8880b99670df8fd71741a9.description: Keikku (by Lapsi Health) is the first FDA-cleared digital stethoscope with an integrated AI scribe — a clinical platform combining Scribe, Diagnostics and Reference in one device, with EHR integration and AI auscultation analytics for cardiac murmurs and lung sounds. Minimalist typography-driven hero: a stark white canvas, a massive bold sans headline, vibrant brand-blue CTAs, extreme whitespace and a centred symmetrical layout for a premium medtech feel. The best technique to steal is conversational UI storytelling — a floating speech bubble ("Hey Keikku, resume scribing") layered over a subtle 3D render of the device, communicating voice activation without a demo video. Inner pages: /keikkuai, /about (team), /product/keikku. Featured as an FWA case.

8a0070de30b5410894f957a7d1e000c3.description: Immersive one-page editorial "experience" about TikTok star Khaby Lame by ICON Magazine, now rehosted at the studio's own domain (moved from khaby.iconmagazine.de). Opens on a stark monochrome typographic entry screen with a sound toggle and a subtle white-on-white "PRESENTS" watermark before the Start Experience gate. Inside: a word-slider lockup (NO 1 / TikToker / Actor / Icon), drag-scrub photo galleries, oversized pull quotes and a film-credits footer. Site by Rocani Studio. Sections beyond the entry gate described from markup; those visuals unverified in headless render.

8b4844de6ace4f528ba5a2c435384890.description: Portfolio site for Kieran Clarke, an award-winning stuntman, precision rider/driver, stunt coordinator and filmmaker (former motocross champion and Superbike road racer). The hero is a moody cinematic photo: a motion-blurred yellow motorcycle shot in dramatic low key, with minimalist all-caps sans over charcoal and black, and a live British Standard Time clock in the corner as a bespoke detail. Nav includes a hidden "Secret" section. Notable blocks: Projects and Films case-study reels. Worth stealing: motion blur as the whole brand statement, the live-clock micro-detail, and the near-total absence of decoration on a personal brand site.

f2b515b843584846a6aed3896ea17d4a.description: Kikin is a London fintech (FCA-registered) that pays SMEs' supplier invoices so they can extend runway without equity dilution, and rewards ESG-strong businesses with lower fees. Brand identity by Koto. Dark forest-green hero with vibrant lime accents and a full-width hand-drawn outdoor illustration (two people carrying a canoe at sunset) sitting under a heavyweight stacked headline, which is a rare warm, non-dashboard direction for fintech. Notable blocks: an interactive funding calculator, a numbered four-benefit list, a 'who we fund' three-icon qualifier, an SDG / B-Corp / 1% for the Planet badge wall, a long testimonial carousel with founder photos and logos, and a tabbed FAQ.

2cd7b8e81d8880e8bd30db74cba54e60.description: Kinsta is premium managed WordPress and application hosting on Google Cloud (28 data centres, 230k+ customers). Split hero: headline plus dual CTAs on the left, a lifestyle image panel on the right, layered over a subtle geometric grid. Warm off-white base with charcoal type and green/red accents, and the detail worth stealing is the serif headline paired with a modern sans for nav and body, a serif-in-SaaS pairing that reads distinctly premium against the usual all-sans hosting crowd. Strong supporting blocks: a tabbed MyKinsta dashboard walkthrough and a value comparison table framing $300+ of bundled features against other hosts.

ff6aed98630b4a7283496d2986aaf621.description: Kirschberg is a New Zealand studio/agency site (existing tags point to a dark, card-based, animated build). It failed to render across repeated headless capture attempts, so visuals are unverified (loader or heavy-motion/WebGL build in headless render). The domain still resolves; only the render could not be completed.

1987bb6ae2b64d3ca269624679620c54.description: Landing page for KMBCH, an artisanal kombucha brand. The hero is an editorial still-life: bottles staged on minimalist geometric plinths against a pastel lilac-peach gradient, with a heavy geometric sans headline layered over a giant low-opacity "KMBCH" wordmark for depth. The standout is a scroll-linked flavour gallery where a 3D bottle rotates 360 degrees while the entire page background transitions colour to match each flavour (chokeberry, strawberry, ginger). Closes on a kinetic parallax footer where the brand name breaks into individual letters drifting at different speeds behind floating bottles.

ce5b2f53434d4b78a33fc1cd755e44ca.description: Camel Kids, the children's range from Indian stationery brand Kokuyo Camlin — art supplies and activity kits presented as a playful mini-universe. The hero mixes big playful sans, product shots and illustration on clean white with a high-contrast primary and secondary palette. Two devices worth stealing: anthropomorphised type, with character eyes built into the O and M so the wordmark itself becomes a character, and product shots held in hands to give scale and a human connection instead of flat packshots. Floating swirls and shapes add energy between blocks. Good reference for kids, toy and education e-commerce that needs personality without going twee.

5cfbec51338745ccac8b21da8adb3771.description: KPR is a sci-fi NFT/metaverse world project; the domain now boots under APXVERSE branding with a SIGN IN affordance, so the property appears to have evolved past the originally saved KPR identity. The intro is a narrative loader worth stealing: a stark black-on-white monospace terminal that cycles fake system URLs and status lines (SPACESHIP, WEAPONS_GRADE-A, TITANIUM_SHELL) so world-building starts before the site does, with a click-to-enable-sound button doubling as the progress focal point. The experience never advances past the loader in a headless render, so visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render).

5634a50f3cf948b8a6a06585a944f26d.description: Krepling is a no-code commerce platform for building storefronts and automating customer journeys through visual 'workflows' and integrations. The hero is a light 3D scene of floating integration icons and abstract shapes; the palette is white and light grey with a signature purple accent, punctuated by high-contrast dark feature sections. Two things worth stealing: a minimalist sticky side-navigation on the right that tracks scroll progress and lets you jump between platform pillars (Workflows, Storefront, Dashboard), and animated logic mockups that explain automation by acting it out (abandoned cart triggers a reminder email) instead of describing it. Section transitions swing deliberately from light UI blocks to dark feature blocks to signal a change of subject.

a005f4fd43ce46b8a5a22de364dfcfc2.description: A tribute site chronicling the work and life of Stanley Kubrick, with /timeline as its second chapter. The entry screen is deliberately near-empty: a horizontal split-tone background that bisects the frame exactly, a single grayscale portrait centred in a huge field of negative space, and no display type at all beyond a hamburger toggle. Stark monochrome throughout. Good reference for cinematic, restrained entry screens and for chaptered biography timelines that let one image carry the whole viewport.

2497b8e81d88806a9a89f111d2125b94.description: Kyoso (Lumina Platform) is an agentic AI creative platform — AI designer, marketer and ad creator in one, currently in beta behind a waitlist. The hero is airy and premium-minimal: a bold tightly-tracked geometric sans headline in black on off-white, monospaced sub-copy for a creative-meets-technical contrast, subtle light-grey geometric line art in the background, and a partial dashboard UI mockup cropped at the fold to pull the scroll. Every hero and diagram asset ships in both light and dark variants. The steal-worthy block is the "No more platform hopping" before / after comparison, where a messy scattered tool-chain diagram morphs into a single centralized hub. Also an examples gallery, tiered pricing (including an education / research tier) and an accordion FAQ.

0da4b4cbcec34defa8a3beca809bb114.description: KZero (Kelvin Zero) sells a passwordless authentication suite — passwordless login, SSO, next-gen MFA, a biometric password vault and security keys — packaged multi-tenant specifically for MSPs and MSSPs. The hero is a pure-black canvas with vivid neon 3D light ribbons (magenta, electric blue, orange, purple) flowing behind a bold geometric-sans headline, with a monospaced "/ PASSWORDLESS" eyebrow label setting the technical register and a coral-orange CTA colour reused for every primary action. Navigation floats in a semi-transparent rounded pill and a login-interface product mockup is layered over the abstract background so the software sits inside the brand's visual world. Worth knowing: the ribbons are a looping MP4, not live WebGL, so the effect is cheap to reproduce. Below: a partner logos bar, an animated stat/chart video block on credential breaches, an MSP-focused capability comparison table and an FAQ. Astro front end on WordPress.

de14a4a908414d4abab41ef6cc195e90.description: Lama Lama, an Amsterdam-based creative digital agency building brands, products and experiences. Hero pairs a massive uppercase sans headline with a cinematic dark background, deep charcoal and crisp white broken by a glowing gold accent, and monospaced micro-labels for a technical feel. Two details worth stealing: a live status bar in the footer showing team headcount, location and a real-time clock, and a CTA button with an actual team member's photo inside it. A floating "this is us" video card breaks the grid and adds depth without clutter.

65a440ef65f2488492ca365518bda5f2.description: Lazarev is a San Francisco digital product design agency specialising in AI, data and B2B/SaaS UX, with 120+ awards, a 2026 Webby for Best Visual UI in AI, and clients including Boeing, Hewlett Packard, Shopify/Peel and Corel. Confident dark-mode system: deep charcoal ground, crisp white bold tightly-tracked geometric sans headlines, and a single high-saturation emerald accent carrying all CTAs, softened by pill-shaped buttons. The strongest steal is the stats treatment: metrics are slash-numbered (/01, /02 ... /006) and split into a big figure over a two-line caption, used twice, first as a credential strip under the hero ($500M+ funding raised, 120+ awards, founded 2015) and again as a results grid (+300% sign-up conversion, +42% retention, 25M monthly visits). Also notable: an 11-step numbered process rail grouped under Strategy / UX / UI / Delivery, and a client-outcomes block where each logo carries a one-line result instead of sitting in a bare logo wall.

d2d8e4c9cf9543fd98ae39f521eb88e0.description: Lemkus is Cape Town's sneaker and streetwear retailer, trading since 1935 and stocking Nike, Jordan, New Balance, Asics and Puma with a launch/raffle calendar. The hero is a three-panel vertical triptych of high-detail sneaker photography (heel detail, on-foot profile, sole from below) set on a warm burnt-orange field under a vivid red header bar, with cyan and iridescent accents coming from the product itself. Type is bold sans for navigation with small vertically-set text blocks placed directly into the imagery for an editorial feel. Good reference for saturated colour-blocked sneaker drops and multi-panel product photography heroes.

3c5ab7cc768b45218fd11276c59e9094.description: Personal portfolio site of designer Leonid Kostetskyi. The site is alive and serves a percentage-based preloader (a small "0%" counter on a white canvas), but it never advances past that state in a headless browser even with extended waits. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render). Saved tags describe a light, big-type, flat design with visible borders and a grid layout.

5714146902734aa490468b2ee859e635.description: Levora Dragons is a medieval-fantasy metaverse MMORPG on Binance Smart Chain — 8,888 evolutionary dragon NFTs, LV token, play-to-earn, community DAO. The site is a Cuberto showcase piece: full-bleed fantasy art chapters (trading strategies, evolutionary NFTs, epic lore, token generation, whitepaper/security) stitched into a scroll narrative on a deep purple base, with Cuberto's signature cursor and motion work. Useful as a reference for how a thin crypto proposition gets carried entirely by art direction and scroll pacing, and for the closing subscribe block that sells a pre-sale waitlist instead of a product. Site by Cuberto. Visuals unverified (splash/loader in headless render).

3177b8e81d888059bcc5dee47c92b6fc.description: Lightweight (a brand of Carbovation, Friedrichshafen) is a premium German maker of fully handmade carbon bicycle wheels - Meilenstein, Obermayer, Fernweg, Pfadfinder - built on a Rim-to-Rim monocoque and Alpha Rib Technology, with Tour de France and Olympic heritage. Site credited to VKZ Studio. The homepage is a full-bleed cinematic scrolltelling sequence: chaptered sections (Welcome / Philosophy / Craft / Innovation / Evolution) each carried by a looping Vimeo background film with a short label-plus-headline overlay, so the page reads like a brand film rather than a shop. Also has a mega-menu with hover-preview imagery per wheel, a #ridelightweight Instagram gallery and a newsletter block. Visuals unverified: the site sits behind a WebGL preloader and cookie gate that never resolves in a headless render, so hero details are described from HTML only.

ebb87b8d25d14b25b45839d1b679e71d.description: Linear is a product development and issue tracking system for software teams, now leaning heavily on AI agent workflows. The reference dark mode: deep blacks, subtle charcoal gradients, crisp white sans. Scroll-triggered animation brings the UI to life, glassmorphism on floating cards, and integrated code-diff visualisers. High-fidelity product captures do all the selling, showing command-line style interactions and AI task delegation as working software rather than static screenshots. A timeline block covers the changelog/roadmap story.

7e29dd57ceef41a48658d67b0afa956d.description: Linktree is the original link-in-bio tool, now at 70M+ users, letting creators consolidate links, products, music, videos and a storefront behind one URL with analytics on top. The hero is a split-screen with an acid-green field, forest-green type and a vivid magenta announcement banner — a heavy oversized geometric sans headline against clean body copy. Two things worth stealing: the floating rounded pill nav bar, and the inline username input placed straight in the hero so sign-up starts before the click. Notable blocks: an animated creator-card marquee looping Lottie avatars, a named-creator logos strip (Selena Gomez, HBO, Comedy Central, Pharrell, Tony Hawk, LA Clippers), a three-up solutions grid, an as-featured-in press bar, a testimonial set with creator photos, and an accordion FAQ.

2487b8e81d8880fc9581c150effb10b3.description: Liveblocks sells realtime and multiplayer infrastructure (CRDT sync, presence, comments, notifications, AI copilots) for collaborative apps and AI agents. Pitch-black centered big-type hero with a promo pill, dual CTAs and a vibrant purple-pink gradient texture; a hand-drawn handwritten annotation arrow points at the product mockup, injecting human warmth against the geometric sans. The signature block is a tabbed before / after product comparison (Document / Workflow / Sheet / Dashboard) showing the same UI with and without Liveblocks. Also notable: a "like Figma / like Notion / like Google Docs" use-case gallery of feature thumbnails, and a live comment-thread demo running beside real code (React snippet with an AI agent replying in-thread). Trust block with SOC 2 / HIPAA badges and 99.99% uptime. Strong inner pages: /examples, /showcase, /customers.

e70442cad6c94c59b816b6987bab7c2d.description: Living Corporate is a media platform and consultancy on workplace equity, amplifying underrepresented voices in corporate life; site built by Workshop Built. Editorial single-stage hero: a high-contrast side-profile portrait against flat mustard yellow, with a heavy all-caps sans headline in stark white. The technique worth stealing is the EXPLORE button doubling as a circular lens cursor that masks and reveals the headline underneath as it moves, giving a layered peek-a-boo depth from nothing but type and one photograph. Good reference for carrying a whole brand on a single portrait plus colour.

76fa63df58de43b4ac1fbd0662f9360e.description: An awareness and education site about Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder — explains the disorder, treatment options (ERP, SSRIs), and collects first-person stories to cut stigma. Hero pairs a light-weight geometric sans headline with a central 3D scene of abstract balanced forms standing in for internal tension, over cobalt blue, vibrant orange and soft off-white with generous white space that keeps a heavy medical topic calm. Strong reference for healthcare/mental-health UI that isn't clinical stock photography. Notable blocks: an animated counter rolling up to the prevalence figure, a scrolltelling "vicious cycle of obsessions and compulsions" section that walks the loop step by step, and numbered subtype cards (contamination, perfectionism, losing control, harm) mirrored by compulsion cards. Vertical side navigation and "keep scrolling" cues break the standard grid. Site by LA (designedbyla.com).

16b90c6767e449ee81d8e7d50834d01b.description: Site of the Ljubicic Tennis Academy, Ivan Ljubicic's pro tennis camp on Losinj island, Croatia (moved from ljubicicacademy.com). Full-width photographic hero of a seaside clay court with heavyweight geometric sans headlines, a transparent header and punchy lime-green CTAs popping against natural Adriatic blues and terracotta. Long first-person testimonial section from campers and a full-bleed Vimeo promo video block. Site by NeoLab.

792e4016d0de4bf09500d9e60ab30a31.description: Loctax is a tax governance platform for in-house tax teams. The hero drops imagery entirely and runs on authoritative messaging alone — a bold sans headline in crisp black on off-white, deep forest green for branding and CTAs. Worth stealing: a "220+ JURISDICTIONS COVERED" badge doing trust-building work as micro-copy right at the fold, and an asymmetric layout that puts the heavy headline left and supporting body text right, creating an efficient reading hierarchy without needing a visual. Good reference for a minimal B2B hero that still feels premium. Cookiebot banner covers part of the fold.

8312473532ab4320be41432ba9e8b41a.description: Loeven Morcel is a Montreal cabinetmaking workshop (since 1991) building high-end custom furniture, kitchens and millwork for designers and architects, with a small e-commerce collection alongside the project work. The hero is pure editorial big type: an oversized high-contrast serif line ("here, quality takes PRECEDENCE") on cream and black, generous whitespace and thin horizontal rules that read like a print magazine spread. Strongest blocks are the horizontal projects slider with a rotating wheel control, a numbered No.1–No.5 service process (measurements, drawings, manufacturing, finish, installation), a single pull-quote testimonial and an Instagram gallery strip. Small UI accents like the starburst close button add personality to functional elements. Site by Jomor Design, built on Webflow.

6e503511b3824c8f9f0f5cf6033fa148.description: Loket Design is a New York (Dumbo, Brooklyn) industrial design studio with Dutch roots, doing product, furniture, brand and packaging design (Stojo, True Places, Eku, Mrs Meyer's). Hero pairs a warm cream ground with oversized vermilion display type and a soft-pink product shot layered directly over the lettering, with a three-column intro underneath anchored by solid brand-colour bullets. Standout technique is the extreme scale contrast between small structured copy and the huge background type. Notable blocks: a 13-frame sequenced product animation of a folding chair, alternating day/night lifestyle shots, a packaging line-up, and an awards & patents list with outbound links (Red Dot, Fast Company IxD, A'Design).

e6911b68235947b8b7dfd19482703229.description: Longines Spirit Flyback is the Swiss maison's aviation-inspired flyback chronograph collection page, tying the 1936 flyback patent and pioneer-aviator heritage to a COSC-certified product story. The hero is a soft-focus lifestyle wrist shot with large white all-caps sans overlaid on a deep navy, off-white and cool grey palette; the neat luxury-retail move is laying the collection nav (MASTER / CONQUEST / SPIRIT / ELEGANCE / HERITAGE) centred across the hero image instead of in a separate bar. Below it sits an eight-product filterable grid of soldier pack-shots showing every strap and dial variant against white, then an editorial "About our movements" block and expandable trust rows for warranty, Swiss Made and shipping. Individual reference pages (e.g. the Titanium L3.821.1.53.2) are strong inner pages.

2497b8e81d88804e94c5da993673bb58.description: LottieFiles is the motion / Lottie animation platform (800k+ animation library, Lottie Creator, dotLottie runtimes, Figma / After Effects / Canva / Webflow plugins, 16M+ users). Character-led hero: a massive left-aligned heavy black sans headline balanced asymmetrically against a dense cluster of playful animated characters in teal, purple, orange and yellow on off-white — the illustration group is the counterweight to the type, and every element is itself a live Lottie. Below it: a huge multi-row marquee gallery of real animations with a ⌘K search field acting as an interactive demo, and an unusual comparison-style stats block (dotLottie 90% smaller than GIF, 10x faster to ship, 3x engagement, 5x page load, 40% SEO lift). Testimonial carousel links straight into case studies (Webflow, Airbnb, Canva, Wise, Duolingo, Gojek).

34e7b8e81d8880e58de1f104297015bf.description: Lovart bills itself as the world's first AI design agent: one conversation produces logos, packaging, posters, social content and video ads. Dark hero with an elegant oversized serif headline styled like a live prompt — key words underlined as if being typed into the agent — which instantly communicates the product. Below, a simulated agent chat ("Analyzing user intent → Explored visual trends") acts as product UI showcase, followed by feature sections for Touch Edit (before/after object removal), Style Consistency and layered Text Edit, plus poster galleries. Great reference for prompt-as-hero and agent-workflow storytelling.

3a37b8e81d8880a990d0df2823c4e886.description: Lovi is an AI skincare assistant iOS app (face scanner, cosmetics Fit Score, science-backed AI chat), built in Framer by a Cyprus team. Hero is a clean near-white duotone product-shot layout with a large phone mockup, a pill-shaped award badge floating above a tight-tracked geometric sans headline, and generous negative space for a calm medical-premium feel. The page is structured as three numbered "Superpower" chapters, each pairing looping app-UI video with an animated data toy — a skin-issues condition list, a Jan–Dec skin-tracking timeline, an ingredient safety card stack and a scripted AI-chat replay with % fit scores. Also a 20-brand logo wall, a benchmark bar chart against BioLinkBERT/PubMedGPT, and a medical-board team carousel.

0a5ec19aa7974ad38df872f25697c133.description: Innovation lab of Fortune 50 retailer Lowe's, exploring AI, AR and spatial computing for home improvement (Style Studio for Apple Vision Pro, Lowe's Vision AR app). Headless render stalls on the intro: a white 3D wireframe polyhedron centered on pure black, an elegant minimal preloader worth noting on its own. Full-page visuals unverified (loader in headless render); saved tags describe a light, card-based scrolltelling site.

022441337560433cab32e99b0371c98c.description: La puce à l'oreille is a Quebec producer of documentary podcasts for kids aged 6–12, plus live events and school mediation programmes. Visually it is a soft pastel-pink canvas carrying ultra-bold black sans headlines and scattered hand-drawn micro-illustrations in primary colours — playful without going childish. The most useful block is the faceted browse system: the whole catalogue is filtered by format, collaboration, duration, theme and age range, feeding a card grid of illustrated podcast covers, with a "random listen" shuffle button as a discovery shortcut. Also worth stealing is the voice-message CTA ("Allo la puce" – record a question) and the row of platform subscribe icons. Good reference for content libraries that need playful multi-axis filtering.

f817da2e3abf4be0b0e690529770bd71.description: Lucid Motors, the American luxury electric vehicle maker. Hero is a full-bleed cinematic video of the Lucid Gravity moving through a mountain landscape, palette of earthy tans, sandy browns and muted blues with warm beige buttons and white text. The model name sits in a refined high-contrast serif while navigation and body copy stay clean sans, a deliberate pairing of traditional luxury typography with futuristic product design. A slim utility bar at the top carries high-conversion offers without polluting the hero. Reference for automotive video heroes and premium serif-plus-sans systems.

3177b8e81d8880da96bdc4d613e212c8.description: Luffu, from the founders of Fitbit, is a family-care app that pulls health data from wearables, medical portals, photos and voice notes, then proactively alerts caregivers about missed medications or shifting health patterns. The hero is warm golden-hour lifestyle photography with the oversized serif wordmark layered behind the subjects so the brand sits inside the scene. Underneath sits a row of avatar heads, each triggering a short looping video that answers a real caregiver question ("Is Grandma recovering from her surgery OK?") - a clean, very stealable way to show use cases without a feature list. The rest of the page is video-driven scrolltelling with phone-in-frame app captures, a soft pastel gradient palette, high-contrast serif headings on sans body, and a founders' letter that carries the trust story.

3b38e9b6866443438441321d60f81257.description: Lunchbox is enterprise ordering software for restaurant chains — branded web and app ordering, loyalty, marketing CRM and third-party order aggregation, positioned around protecting margins against delivery-marketplace fees. The hero is aggressively minimal: near-black and off-white, one massive tight-kerned sans headline, and a single high-vibrancy yellow pill CTA as the only colour in the frame. The detail worth stealing is the floating capsule navigation — a detached rounded bar instead of a full-width fixed header, which makes the page feel modular and lets the hero breathe edge to edge. Below it the site moves into product UI screens, client logos and feature breakdowns per product line. Good reference for B2B SaaS heroes that resist the urge to show the dashboard immediately.

3687b8e81d88805c96afcff929a8431b.description: About page of Lusion, the multi-award-winning UK creative production studio (58 Awwwards, FWA and Webby awards; clients include Porsche, Apple, Google, Coca-Cola). The page is a heavy WebGL scrolltelling experience: giant "WE ARE A CREATIVE PRODUCTION STUDIO" typography, an awards ledger styled like a numbered index (001 Site of the Year ...), brand-logo marquees, expertise accordions and a playful "Is Your Big Idea Ready to Go Wild?" CTA. Screenshot currently shows the site's black preloader/counter — the WebGL scene does not render in headless capture, so visual details above come from page content. Site by Lusion themselves.

9d9092b88def445e9d7bf1ee7e3c2329.description: A Culture page on a Netlify-hosted site, not indexed by search, so the company identity is unconfirmed and the screenshot is the only evidence. The hero is a high-energy streetwear-styled composition: ultra-bold wide-set sans at massive scale layered over black-and-white lifestyle photography, with sticker-style cut-outs (floating heads, fries) overlapping the letterforms to create depth. Palette is high-contrast monochrome accented by warm skin and food tones, with rounded container edges and a grainy bottom texture giving a tactile, zine-like feel. Worth stealing: oversized type used as a focal mask over imagery, plus the collaged cut-out layering.

b8997e6761c54e8f9328996d79671343.description: Madbox is a Paris/Barcelona mobile game studio (Stickman Hook, Pocket Champs) with 500M+ downloads. The homepage is built as an explorable 3D island world rather than a scrolling page: a WebGL map with named islands (Cemetery, Creativity, Automation, Scale) that each open a piece of the studio's story, plus playful mechanics like holding Spacebar to reveal live players, an easter egg and a quiz prompt. Supporting blocks include a big-number stats row (+500M downloads, 15 games live), game cards linking to App Store / Google Play / Poki, a careers section and a Discord community CTA. Strong reference for scrolltelling-plus-3D studio sites where the site itself has to feel like a toy. Note: the headless capture only reached the gradient-logo loading screen, so hero visuals beyond the 3D map are unverified.

2497b8e81d888018a7b8c43e252a0026.description: MIUX Studio is a Seattle brand and digital design studio (branding, web, UX/UI, packaging) working with founders and growing businesses, built on Next.js and Prismic. The hero is an asymmetrical multi-pane grid rather than a standard split: a large warm-beige type block on the left, a vertical lifestyle image on the right, and nav items floated as vertical columns overlapping the imagery. Muted quiet-luxury palette of sandy beige and charcoal over warm sunlit interior photography, with an editorial high-end sans and tight kerning. Worth stealing: nav laid directly over photography with arrow affordances, generous negative space, and grid-within-grid inset images breaking up the text zones. Solid case-study and process structure for a studio site.

3fa1b6e4251f41ab8ebd2aae6337aca9.description: "The Magic Bottle" — an Awwwards Conference sponsor microsite by Buenos Aires studio estudio/nk, built purely as a talent flex: an immersive WebGL experience around a single water bottle, with the pitch "if we could do this with a bottle, imagine what we can do for your brand". Structured as gesture-driven scrolltelling chapters (tap to start, drag the cap off, shake the bottle super fast) with an audio layer and a percentage preloader. Two blocks are worth stealing: an FAQ written in blunt, funny first person that answers the real questions including actual price ranges (branding $15–40k, web from $40k), and a "we're attending" team block with per-person cards routing you to the right contact (CEO for business, CTO for projects, creative dev for tech). Site by estudio/nk. Visuals unverified (loader/audio gate in headless render).

ab701cd9c63045f4b84d2edda88bde57.description: Make HR Work is the first online HR community of the Dutch province of Gelderland, aimed at HR professionals in construction and infrastructure and backed by Provincie Gelderland. The hero sets a huge headline on a warm off-white canvas that mixes a heavy rounded geometric sans with an expressive brush-script "HR" breaking the baseline, plus a hand-drawn scribble character overlapping both the type and the lavender section edge below, with saturated forest green carrying the accents. Worth stealing: the floating thin-bordered capsule nav, the informal dashed tilted scroll cue, and the layered paper-like section edges. Notable blocks include a video section with custom play/pause icons, an infinite marquee of member portraits, and a best-practice case library. Site by UNCOMMON.

0e6d9132f21a4836b22d7b2eb3007bd4.description: makemepulse is a Paris/London global creative studio (founded 2008, 30+ staff, FWA Hall of Fame 2025) building immersive digital platforms for Louis Vuitton, LOEWE, Audemars Piguet, Brunello Cucinelli, Estee Lauder, UNESCO and Meta, on its own NanoGL real-time 3D engine. The hero is a stark monochrome typographic composition, high-contrast off-white on charcoal, set in a bespoke elegant sans with unusual geometric ligatures and laid out on a deliberately broken grid with diagonally offset lines. Worth stealing: extreme scale contrast between massive display type and tiny underlined sub-copy, plus taglines nested inside the whitespace of the headline so the text reads as one graphic composition. Also runs a games sub-studio, makemeplay.

177c4f740bde4fceaa04983b8f0d8b8e.description: Makepill — a Paris-based venture studio uniting strategy, design and technology across seven domains to build market-ready products. The pill is the whole visual system: a themed loader rotates a 3D black pill while counting to 100% ("Just a second, we are crafting some pills..."), then 3D pills animate, rotate and crack open on scroll to reveal contents — pink inside for the strategy section, a robot head inside a yellow "Ai" pill for the philosophy section. High-contrast black/white with an acid lime accent, bold sans, section headers prefixed with a forward slash (/ Our philosophy). Also worth stealing: seamless black-to-white background inversions triggered by scroll, and oversized horizontal marquees ("Build growth. Sustain leadership."). Closes on "Brief us now".

59caf7df41fc4d1c9df021c3c3606275.description: Marble is a climate-tech venture studio based at STATION F in Paris that partners with scientists, engineers and operators to build deeptech startups over a 12-month programme, then invests as first cheque and helps raise the seed. The hero is high-contrast dark mode: deep black canvas, a massive bold geometric sans headline with tight kerning, and a single translucent multi-tonal blue/violet organic 3D form that the headline sits partially behind for depth layering. A “New Ventures” notification card sits top-left to drive a specific action without cluttering the main message, and arrow-based CTAs keep the micro-interactions restrained. Copy is unusually confrontational for the category (“Radicals Welcome”, “Do you believe climate is the only problem worth working on?”) — a good reference for recruiting-led positioning. Notable blocks: a founder pull-quote with portrait, a how-it-works explainer and a companies index. Site by Numbered.

b47a958d21114a7db5324499053d36e3.description: Portfolio for Margot Priolet, a makeup artist and beauty consultant, showing editorial work and skincare guides. High-contrast cream, red and black with oversized serif headlines. Signature moves: a massive hero headline overlapping a central red circle, and a saturated red footer that anchors the whole page. Case studies and an awards/press logos bar carry the credibility. Site by Shyne.

1002f7e9acb349bb95de71ffc2a2f529.description: Marie Fresh Cosmetics is a Ukrainian manufacturer of natural and organic skincare selling face, body and hair care direct to consumers across Ukraine. The layout reads clinical rather than boutique: neutral white and soft grey base, natural greens and earthy tones borrowed from the packaging, bold sans headings such as ANTI-ACNE stacked over lighter subtext, and a persistent vertical left-side navigation instead of a top bar. Useful reference for localised e-commerce — language and currency modal, loyalty programme section, a routine-builder content layer and an editorial posts hub all feed the catalogue.

2bb8c575d07c48b98f0c01fa1e7e0a00.description: MARKAWARE is a Japanese sustainable menswear label (with its sister line marka), built on Shopify, known for full domestic production and material traceability tags. The hero is a split composition: generous off-white negative space on the left against a tall editorial photograph of a model on the right, shot in soft natural light. Typography is a restrained modern sans with wide letter-spacing on the wordmark, and floating white modal-style overlays carry New Arrival and newsletter prompts for a layered feel. Credited Site by SN. Useful reference for quiet Japanese fashion ecommerce, muted neutral palettes and lookbook gallery grids.

2ada2781b36c4cd59eae7213e468cef5.description: Mate Libre is a Montreal yerba mate beverage brand selling organic, fair-trade, low-sugar energy infusions on Shopify. The hero is a soft off-white stage with a diagonal receding line of colourful cans shot in shallow depth of field, balanced against oversized all-lowercase bold sans headlines ("the ideal dose of energy / nature / creativity") that rotate through a slider — the type is scaled large enough to act as a compositional element rather than a caption. Product tiles pair flat fruit illustrations with cut-out cans over pastel fields, and the page runs benefit callouts backed by academic citations, a sustainability block, a founder pull-quote carousel and an FAQ accordion. Site by Locomotive.

d9b75785cb94473e8005f0220f71301d.description: Product microsite for NODO Film Systems' Inertia Wheels MAX, a cinema camera-wheel controller built on printed solid-state motors. The hero is low-key product photography: matte black field, cinematic cyan and orange rim light picking out the dials, a wide geometric sans set at massive scale with tight leading, thin white hairline borders that give a blueprint feel, and a minimal play button laid over the product. Strong supporting blocks include a spec stats row (3x torque, 4x encoder, 6x current, 0 cogging), an interactive Arc Engine demo with per-feature Wheel/Camera toggles, transparent pricing tiers ($5,950–$11,200), and a 'Filmed on NODO' credits list (Obi-Wan Kenobi, The Gray Man). Site by Lazarev.Agency.

3437b8e81d888033ae49e5502e658093.description: Maxima Therapy is a US provider of therapy and support programs for neurodivergent children, adults and families, split into four age-based programs (0-3, 3-18, 18-65, 65+). The design leans entirely on bold flat vector illustration: a lush green landscape scene with a punchy orange color-blocked panel, a pencil-tree motif and animated stacked letters spelling play / learn / grow, all set in a chunky condensed sans. Notable blocks are the age-segmented programs grid with image-preview navigation, a clean 3-step onboarding process (Start with a Referral / Create a Customized Plan / Learn and Grow Together), and a Next stop CTA that chains each program page into the following one. Strong reference for healthcare UI illustration and warm, non-clinical medical branding. Site by Koki Kiko.

2157b8e81d88802e817fc07dac8b55af.description: Maze is a user-research and usability-testing platform (a panel of 6M+ participants, AI moderator, prototype and live-site testing, automated reports), built on Gatsby + DatoCMS. The hero "Research at the pace of change" is a collage-style product shot: an oversized tight-kerned black sans headline on white, with an overlapping cluster of floating UI cards, chat panels, report screens and a "Moderated interview" video snippet creating depth — punchy lime-green and blue accents against a mostly monochrome base. The most steal-worthy blocks are a scroll-driven three-step process section (Recruit → Research → Analyze) and a dense scrolling marquee of feature pills (card sorting, tree testing, surveys, MCP server, AI study builder), plus a lime-tinted crowd-photo band behind the logo wall (Atlassian, Volvo, Cisco, Revolut, Lowe's, Lenovo). Strong inner pages: /platform, /customers, and the "Future of User Research Report 2026" landing.

2b491d7d6ea7411b89d6aff9eeb046a7.description: Meadlight is an Italian drinks brand marketing "Principio", a fermented aperitif made from six unpasteurised honeys, drunk neat or mixed. The hero is text-forward rather than product-forward: a bold condensed sans headline on a warm cream paper-textured background with charcoal type and amber-gold accents, plus a hand-drawn yellow underline that breaks the typographic rigidity. Faded botanical line art sits behind the copy and a left-aligned vertical dot-nav with rotated labels gives the single-page scroll a modern editorial feel. JS-required SPA; body copy is Italian despite English meta tags.

16d7b8e81d88806cafcfd233236effe9.description: MEASURED Guide (founded 2023, Australia) is an editorial publication and reference directory for spirits, liqueurs and non-alcoholic drinks, with cocktail recipes and a sister product/brand studio, Measured Studio. Structure is closer to a design-led magazine than a drinks shop: a stories feed with category labels and bylines (Culture, Profile, Behind the Bar), a card-based tasting directory where each bottle gets a portrait-crop image plus category and producer, and a recipe index. Consistent soft-radius containers and a restrained sans-serif voice throughout. Visuals unverified (a cookie-based age gate blocks the headless render, so the hero could not be confirmed) — the age gate itself is a clean pattern: dark translucent overlay, solid "Yes" button against a ghost "No".

278b7c9703654e79ae7cde3f8957b2a0.description: Measured is a fintech offering securities-backed lines of credit, pitched as "the modern wirehouse for independents" — letting advisors' clients borrow against their portfolios from $10,000 without selling assets or triggering a tax event. Webflow build with a centred bullseye hero: a warm natural-light office photograph with shallow depth of field, faded out under a soft cream gradient so the black big-type headline and deep forest-green CTA stay legible — a clean solution to putting type over photography. Notable blocks: a benefit grid mixing line icons with soft product-UI screenshots, a two-part use-case section (new lines vs. refinance), a genuinely long expandable FAQ that doubles as risk disclosure, and a $225B+ AUM trust CTA.

25549f63d1b4472dbab715e1f0633e7b.description: REDIRECTED: meetcampfire.com now forwards to campfire.ai after a rebrand (the old domain only survives for the app login and community). Campfire is an AI-native ERP for high-growth finance teams: general ledger, revenue automation, close management and 'Ember', an AI accounting assistant. The current site is a dark forest-green hero with sage/mint accents and an orange brand mark, a tilted 3D product shot with deconstructed UI cards floating around it and subtle orbital lines suggesting an ecosystem; the headline colour-switches on the word 'accounting'. Notable blocks: a marquee of accounting tasks, a customer logo wall (PostHog, Replit, Decagon), quantified case-study cards (20x revenue, 70% faster close, $300k saved) and a testimonial pull-quote. The saved tags describe the older site.

2147b8e81d8880778f77c611eed54c62.description: Mercury is a fintech offering business and personal banking for startups (checking, treasury, cards, bill pay, invoicing). The hero is a full-bleed cinematic video composition — a surreal desk placed in a misty mountain landscape, atmospheric teals, forest greens and ochre with a signature Mercury blue CTA — using deep depth of field and a frosted-glass email capture floating over the imagery. Steal-worthy: the scroll-scrubbed hero video, the surreal banking-from-anywhere metaphor imagery, alternating product-flow cards where each feature is paired with its own looping UI clip, a portrait-photo testimonial carousel with industry labels, and a clean 4-up stats row (300K+ entrepreneurs, 1 in 3 startups, $20B+ monthly volume). Strong inner pages: /personal-banking, /pricing.

2887b8e81d8880a48c7ede49539f61b8.description: Merge sells connective infrastructure for production AI: a unified API across HRIS, accounting, CRM, ticketing and file storage, plus an agent handler and an LLM gateway (customers include OpenAI, Mistral, Dropbox, Perplexity, Ramp). Minimal centred hero on an off-white ground, deep-charcoal bold sans headline with tight tracking, a single high-contrast black CTA, and a faint radial concentric line pattern in the background adding depth without noise. Premium neutral restraint. The strongest block is the logos bar: customer logos expand into inline pull-quote and case-study cards, turning social proof into a browsable section. Testimonials are tabbed by team (Product / Engineering / GTM / IT).

4f877d19e68b43508efed0e716258ef6.description: Meridian Capital is a BVI-based, market-neutral approved fund focused on AI-assisted equity derivatives, managed by Kaiju Capital Management and built around its proprietary Mechanisms of Reasoning and ARC system for an 18–60 day position lifespan. The site sells an algorithmic edge to international and institutional investors, with the terms-of-use and disclosure pages typical of regulated fund marketing. Visuals unverified — the headless renderer crashed on three separate attempts, so hero composition, palette and typography are not confirmed.

2887b8e81d8880e89163fe6843567b39.description: MetaMask is Consensys' self-custody crypto wallet for buying, swapping, earning and spending BTC/ETH/SOL, now extended with perps, prediction markets, RWAs and a card. Typography-led centred hero where copy is the primary visual asset: a massive ultra-bold blocky display face, tightly tracked and treated as a graphic object, with an italic accent letter in "Where your money lives". Deep forest teal against icy pale cyan, a looping webm sitting behind the type, and soft pill buttons deliberately set against sharp heavy letterforms for texture contrast. The stats block is worth stealing: 4.7 stars, 100MM+ downloads, "#1 most secure wallet", each rendered as its own illustrated card rather than a plain number row. Unusually deep SEO footer (price pages, converters, buy guides).

2147b8e81d8880d5a8f2e177c0d7e170.description: Micro is an "everything app" that merges email, CRM, meetings, tasks and docs into one AI-organised workspace (founded by Brett Goldstein; currently waitlist-gated). The hero breaks SaaS convention: a vibrant sky-blue gradient field, a bold rounded serif headline in white, and an oversized illustrated character mascot peering into frame, with the product UI cropped as a peek along the bottom edge instead of a full screenshot. A pill-shaped floating announcement widget sits above the nav, and the page even embeds an audio player with album art — an unusually playful, personality-forward touch for a productivity tool. Good reference for injecting character into B2B software. Fully client-rendered Next.js app, so inner-page structure is not exposed in source.

2fc7b8e81d888066aec3d688f82e7822.description: Midlife Engineering is an interactive sound-therapy toy by Lee Black (built in Framer, Awwwards SOTD): you craft ambient soundscapes with real-time audio encoders, four visualizer modes reacting to frequencies, and an Autoplay mode that randomises samples, loops and crossfades for you. The whole page is the product. Charcoal and cool greys with safety-orange accents, clean grotesque type, and a skeuomorphic Teenage-Engineering-style hardware panel that sits on top of massive background lettering for a spatial, layered effect. Worth stealing: making the hero itself the interactive demo instead of a screenshot, using a device UI with a status display ("SYSTEM STATUS: DORMANT") as the hook, and soft drop shadows that lift the panel off the canvas. Great reference for tactile, non-generic product-as-site landing pages.

1849bf2bc8704dd0a24fc31a6e009489.description: Milk Network presents itself as a brand development firm working in strategy, branding and design ('works in thought and in action'). The page is effectively one interactive hero: a split layout with large cycling typography on the left ('We Grow … Ideas / Dreams / Brands') synced frame-for-frame with a central media carousel that swaps the corresponding brand clip, so the headline and the showreel argue the same point at the same moment. Monochrome black-and-white base with the brand colour coming entirely from the video reel; bold grotesque sans; navigation pushed to the edges. Note: the site's live content reads as a branding firm, which does not match the existing Charity tag — worth a manual re-check.

d6f38aabf6cb448d880c4fdfa1ccd7a8.description: Portfolio of Minh Pham, a freelance digital designer. Dark mode throughout — black background, white text, clean high-contrast sans — with generous whitespace and a big-type hero that dissolves into project visuals as you scroll. The signature detail is the 'bat eyes' loading animation, a tiny piece of brand personality doing the work an intro copy block usually tries to do. Case studies lean on high-fidelity motion graphics and video for UI previews rather than static shots, with hover-triggered project reveals. Good reference for a senior solo-designer portfolio where motion quality is the proof of skill.

2147b8e81d88802dac79f1118d1ca230.description: Miros is a paid Webflow ecommerce/SaaS template aimed at fintech, accounting and financial-advisory products; Home V1 is one of three homepage variants, alongside three pricing, three contact, features, blog and account pages. The look is muted-meets-neon: a warm stone/beige canvas with a low-opacity checkerboard grid texture, deep charcoal type and buttons, and electric lime accents; a bold tight-tracked geometric sans carries the centred headline, with tilted floating pill badges breaking the grid and a phone mockup surrounded by floating UI cards. Steal-worthy blocks: a compact three-up stats row sitting inside a dark insights panel, a three-step numbered financial-journey process section, and a light-bulb-iconed pricing block. Useful as a reference for neutral-plus-neon fintech systems.

2487b8e81d888093b2a8cd537265cd4d.description: Miter is a connected construction platform — payroll, HR, expenses and field ops in one system for 1,000+ contractors. Split hero: left-aligned high-contrast headline ("Build with confidence.") plus CTA, right side stacked mobile and desktop UI mockups with soft drop shadows for depth. Palette is deep chocolate / near-black with vibrant violet accents and off-white neutrals, and violet is used consistently for every action state (buttons, active UI, data points); minimalist isometric line art adds construction context without clutter. The standout block is the odometer-style animated counting stats ("Trusted by 1,500+ contractors", "We've helped 4,900+ companies…") where digits roll through values. Also strong: a case-study carousel with company-profile metadata chips (employee count, Sage Intacct, Procore, prevailing wage, states), a wire-mesh background texture behind stories, and a purple US map for the US-based support section.

fa775d57a2864da2877bf0d68ed6c150.description: MITI Navi is a luxury sailing-yacht brand and shipyard (Golfe-Juan, France; yard in Bodrum, Turkey) offering 26–50m super sailing yachts, crewed charter, custom builds and refit. The hero combines a large sea/yacht photograph with an elegant high-contrast serif headline, a cream-and-navy palette, and a distinctive arch-shaped image mask that peaks at the centred logo; a vertical 'Download our brochure' side tab and EN/FR toggle sit alongside. Saved as a bare domain; site serves under /en. Reference for arch-masked photo heroes in premium marine branding.

4827fed06aab40d2a506de83809210d9.description: Mixpanel is a product- and digital-analytics platform for tracking user behaviour, funnels and retention. The hero is centred and typography-led on white, anchored by deep purple brand accents and soft vertical pastel gradients in lavender and cream, with a bold high-contrast sans headline in tight kerning over a highly legible secondary sans. Distinctive techniques: soft-rounded UI cards, subtle glassmorphism on an AI-assistant overlay, and layered product mockups building depth across generous whitespace — a good reference for light, airy analytics-SaaS styling.

6c466bf6a399496592712cd2c00efe5a.description: MKTLM ("Magic Key To Little Me") is a nostalgic storytelling experiment by Obys Agency about childhood memory. Strictly two colours — red and white — carried across the whole narrative. The hero is pure typography: heavy blocky sans interleaved with delicate outlined script flourishes, plus a thin-line clock graphic carrying the memory theme. The header is split into four parts holding navigation, a thematic quote and credits, and the layout leans on whitespace for a minimal high-concept feel. Steal-worthy: a two-colour system sustained across an entire site, and outline-script overlays used as ornament layered into headlines.

939bc9a7347a43d8ac276313c0cb0227.description: Mode is a collaborative business intelligence platform combining SQL, R, Python and visual analytics (acquired by ThoughtSpot in 2023). The hero stacks lime-green containers in a staircase offset that frames the headline while letting lifestyle photography peek through the gaps — the most stealable thing on the page, and a neat way to add depth without a hero image. Palette is forest green, neon lime and white; a heavy serif headline over functional sans body copy gives a data product an unusually editorial voice. Good reference for analytics and BI sites that want to feel human rather than dashboard-grey.

5bc25ff88c644ea0948b2320ad555eac.description: MODELEC is a French maker of high-end electrical fittings — switches and sockets in brass, wood, aluminium and steel — manufacturing in the Paris region since 1976. This Know-How page sells the craft rather than the catalogue: a near-black stage, ultra-thin sans-serif set at massive scale, and a single metallic gold product teased at the very bottom edge of the viewport as a scroll hook. Worth stealing: the numbered "KNOW — 1 — HOW" editorial label that chapters the narrative, the scale contrast of hairline type at huge sizes, and the custom outlined scroll indicator that overlaps content to create depth.

e0b1727e318c4312985798c5a9175da6.description: Moheim is a Japanese homeware and interior brand with a quietly luxurious, minimalist site. The hero leans on extreme negative space over a dark charcoal canvas, setting the wordmark in a geometric sans and breaking convention by anchoring it in the bottom-right corner to force the eye across the empty frame. Product presentation continues the 'less is more' language with generous whitespace and restrained typography.

2497b8e81d888033918fec99ef230c08.description: Moment is "the AI operating system for investment management" — a New York fintech founded by ex-Citadel Securities quants, serving wealth firms and fintechs (Edward Jones, LPL, Hightower). Restrained institutional dark-mode design: a deep charcoal-green ground, stark white heavy sans headline with tight tracking, generous negative space, and a wireframe-geometric texture strip in the announcement bar that signals fintech without any photography. Details worth stealing: a live market-status ticker in the header ("Market closed · —:— ET"), numbered inline link labels ("01·read memo", "02·read press release"), a scrolling announcement marquee, and a stats line doubling as social proof ("$10T+ in assets. 60K+ financial advisors.") sitting directly above the client logo bar. Strong inner pages: /memo, /series-c, /customers. Note: the site is fixed-income / wealth management, not NFT.

16c7b8e81d8880ff99acf1be838ddb52.description: Monolith Studio is a contemporary tattoo studio in Brooklyn founded by fine-line and micro-realism artists Okan Uçkun and Oscar Akermo. The hero is a strictly monochrome brutalist-editorial scene: a photoreal 3D marble bust floating in a smoky, textured off-white atmosphere and physically overlapping a colossal tight-tracked MONOLITH wordmark behind it — the subject-over-giant-type sandwich for fake depth, plus the extreme scale contrast between the headline and tiny all-caps UI text, is the thing to steal. Corner-anchored chrome (live NYC clock, sound toggle, "keep scrolling" prompt) gives it a concierge feel. Notable blocks: an artist roster with style tags (fine line, micro realism, geometric, blackwork, stick & poke) that doubles as an SEO taxonomy, a scrolling artist marquee, Google-sourced collector reviews, an Instagram grid and a press row. Webflow; design and development by Artemii Lebedev.

2fc7b8e81d888090b45fe65c2c8ee8f5.description: Monologue (from the Every studio) is an AI voice-dictation app for Mac and iOS that cleans up speech into what you actually meant to write, syncs dictionaries and modes across devices, and connects to ChatGPT/Claude via MCP. The look is editorial-meets-terminal: a deep charcoal textured background, a giant high-contrast serif headline used as a background graphic layer, and utilitarian monospaced type for body copy and buttons, with cyan highlights. Worth stealing: oversized type treated as texture rather than content, the matte-vs-metallic depth on the floating product panel, and how the raw serif/mono pairing signals "crafted software" instead of generic SaaS. Blocks include an app-in-context showcase (works in every app), an iOS section, a simple Free/Monthly pricing table, and real user quotes.

4aa971456ac14f76bc7db85232e3964f.description: monopo Saigon is the Vietnam studio of Tokyo-born creative agency monopo, working across creative direction, brand experiences, motion design, CGI and film (FWA and Awwwards winner). Visuals unverified (loader in headless render): the site is a heavy WebGL/motion experience that stayed on a loading spinner during capture, so the hero could not be confirmed. Described from HTML and public sources; expect a dark, motion-led showreel aesthetic consistent with its awards profile.

0387d893246c4abbbd949c3e03c664ab.description: Montvel makes the first French-made wood-pellet barbecue, positioning it as gastronomy plus tech plus design rather than as outdoor hardware. The site is bilingual (FR/EN at /en/). Visuals unverified (the page repeatedly crashed the headless renderer, typical of heavy WebGL or video-driven product sites), so no visual details are recorded here — worth a manual look for the product-storytelling and scrollytelling treatment the saved tags suggest.

3daa4edc19cf4569a31c87280504cab7.description: Moooi is the Dutch design brand founded in 2001 by Marcel Wanders and Casper Vissers, selling lighting, furniture and accessories under a "creative luxury" positioning. The homepage is a cinematic full-bleed architectural interior in warm earthy tones — terracotta, cedar, deep charcoal — with a refined serif wordmark centred over an almost invisible navigation bar and a slim top notification strip. Good reference for premium e-commerce storytelling: designer profile pages, editorial story articles, press and physical store pages all funnel back into the catalogue. Note the aggressive stacking of a promo modal on top of the cookie banner at entry.

1d07b8e81d8880639832e10cd1165e19.description: MOOOOR is an Italian premium supplement brand (vegan, additive-free vitamins, minerals, antioxidants and omega-3, sold as bundles up to €192). Shopify, Italian-language. The hero is driven by extreme typographic scale: the "MOOOOR" wordmark is set as a giant condensed sans that anchors the whole composition, on a warm cream background with charcoal UI and muted pastel product tones (lilac, sage, terracotta, dusty blue). Above it sits a draggable horizontal product strip that acts as a visual header before you ever read the brand name. Floating pill-shaped dark buttons and a serif support voice keep it feeling apothecary-premium rather than fitness-brand loud. Good reference for luxury-minimal supplement or wellness e-commerce.

03d33dcc66294bc7bcc732e3416d1cc9.description: Mooosor is an award-winning educational/charity project (Awwwards Site of the Day, built on Tilda by Marina Looo) that teaches five simple habits to reduce global waste. The hero is high-impact editorial: a photoreal crumpled-plastic texture behind massive all-caps geometric sans typography, with a bold 'X' graphic and vertical text breaking the horizontal flow in a saturated red-orange, black and white scheme. The visceral contrast between organic material and clinical type is worth stealing for cause-driven scrolltelling. RU/EN versions.

2cd7b8e81d8880c0b382d9a156577c8a.description: Webflow-built product landing page for MORE Nutrition (German supplement brand), promoting a high-protein Iced Matcha Latte powder. The hero is product-led: an oversized layered wordmark sits behind the pack render, with a circular ring of benefit callouts orbiting the product and funnelling the eye toward Buy now. Palette is a monochrome-organic green ramp (pale sage to deep forest) on crisp off-white, with bold rounded sans headings and a fluid custom More wordmark. Techniques worth stealing: film grain over flat colour for a tactile natural feel, hand-drawn annotation marks softening an otherwise polished grid, and extreme type-scale contrast.

7a85afd1988742869a7d6b40d839eb5c.description: Mosey is an AI-powered multi-state compliance platform covering HR, payroll, tax and entity filings across all 50 states (now part of Gusto). Off-white and forest-green landing with a narrative hero illustration: mock UI checklists and alerts wired together by dashed paths and concentric circles that explain the product at a glance. Below: tabbed feature nav (Initial Setup / Ongoing / Recurring), rounded cards, and workflow snippets joined by connector flow lines over a dotted-grid teal band. Soft rounding makes dry compliance software feel approachable.

e45731cd5acb42dd99aa9551bf7b5114.description: Motion.ED is an interactive educational guide to UI/UX animation principles, built by Zajno as a self-promo showcase (CSSDA Best in Class 2023). Hero is deliberately austere: pure black and white, monospace type throughout, a razor-thin full-width horizon line with a single circular 'eye' dot centred on it, plus Pacman-style eye icons and a sound toggle — vast negative space with the message pushed to the lower half. The body is eight numbered lessons (easing, offset & delay, fade, transform & morph, masking, dimension, parallax, zoom), each pairing looping video demos with a classic Disney-animation analogy and three Dribbble implementation examples; an interactive easing comparison and a full ambient/hover sound design layer are the standouts. Site by Zajno.

2810ee96b3c849afba80f3c2c9ea68a0.description: Site for Mova, a Ukrainian beer brand. The entry experience is a full-screen age gate over a blurred, soft-focus product photo in moody forest green with off-white type, set in a bold ultra-wide condensed sans; a legally-required alcohol warning runs as a scrolling marquee ticker along the bottom, which is a neat way to satisfy compliance copy without killing the composition. A discreet floating utility dock of icons sits pinned to the right edge. Visuals unverified beyond the gate (cookie-based age gate blocks the page in headless render).

181889114a5345f78028d325825e15c6.description: Site for Moxion Power and its MP-75 mobile battery unit, which supplies temporary clean power to film sets, construction, events and EV fleets. Site by Rejouice (preprod domain). The hero is a scroll-triggered 3D scene: the MP-75 lifts off its trailer and rotates as the landscape environment dissolves into a flat neutral backdrop — a strong reference for product-hero 3D that resolves into studio space. Cream and charcoal palette with a mint/teal accent, heavy tight-kerned sans and generous whitespace. Other notable blocks: a six-item value grid (Clean, Quiet, Mobile, Smart, Mighty, Dependable), video framed inside large rounded non-rectangular masks, a horizontal industry use-case carousel, and a press-cards section.

b3691db862e946a1b947c63e4f55f971.description: Mr. Pops is a Ukrainian premium ice cream brand (eskimo and mochi, also selling in Poland and Germany) whose site leans on voice rather than product grids. Hero is a big-type "True Ice Cream" statement in a condensed uppercase sans over warm cream with pastel cloud art, followed by a long stream-of-consciousness monologue written as an overheard customer conversation — an unusually brave copy move for a food brand. Ingredient provenance is used as proof (Bronte pistachios, Alfonso mangoes, Belgian chocolate, Sagano matcha). Worth stealing: the flavour gallery with inline out-of-stock and "New" states, an image marquee, an illustrated map routing to points of sale, and a partnership section that reads as a three-step qualification process ending in a Google Form. Site by Advanced Team.

12781d6557a34f5a8cee873be42cadab.description: Musotoku designs and builds premium tattoo tools — the Machete MK-1 power supply and Rover R-1 battery pack — assembled in Madrid. The hero is a numbered two-slide product carousel where dramatically lit metallic copper and deep green hardware renders float over huge sans-serif background type that bleeds off-canvas, with the product overlapping the lettering to build depth on near-black. Standout blocks: a numbered 01–04 Think / Learn / Invest / Repeat process section, an artist pull-quote, a full-bleed Vimeo video section, a cutout product grid with pictogram icons, and vertical repeating logo strips running as a marquee down the page edge.

2157b8e81d8880079677e841da1bc39a.description: MyHealthPrac is a pre-launch (waitlist) functional-medicine platform that interprets blood work — 290 to 500+ biomarkers mapped to around 200 predictive patterns — for practitioners and individuals. Built in Webflow with a warm golden-sepia palette: the hero is a macro, soft-focus body / skin photograph with a looping video, white sans typography and pill-shaped CTAs with inline arrow icons, using blur rather than a dark scrim to keep text legible. The best block to steal is the horizontal marquee of biomarker cards (Vitamin D, Ferritin, Glutathione), each showing a value, unit and plain-language explanation next to abstract imagery — a strong pattern for healthcare data storytelling. Also a Personal vs Professional two-column comparison, an iPad dashboard UI showcase, a Minutes / Days / Months timeline, a long taxonomy of conditions by body system, and a large FAQ. Site by Artemii Lebedev.

f362e7f2ef08495e945c9b630f125707.description: Portfolio of Naba Zabih, a Portland wedding and elopement photographer. The hero is cinematic golden-hour photography with the couple set low in the frame and oversized poetic typography taking the top two thirds — an elegant high-contrast editorial serif with elongated strokes and stylised ligatures, white on warm sepia and deep umber, the luminance contrast alone carrying legibility with no overlay scrim. The useful block for any service business is a five-step numbered Process walking clients to 'your dream elopement', plus a strong testimonials set and packages split by occasion. Heavy SEO blog (Portland venues, planners, dress shops). Note: the footer says 'Based in Florida' while the rest of the site says Portland.

2f0102e512b7448180ded3e23a6a795c.description: Site for Nas Studios, the Dubai/Singapore production arm of Nas Daily, selling viral short-form video and creator campaigns to brands.
