The hero is a full-bleed aerial photo under a dark legibility gradient with a heavy all-caps sans headline that highlights a single word in signature yellow, plus a large centred play button. The standout blocks are an outsized stats section (52,000,000 followers, 20,000,000,000 views), a testimonials row quoting Mark Zuckerberg and Bill Gates, case-study cards carrying per-video Reach/Views figures, and a filterable video gallery (Travel, Education, Culture, Science and Tech). Looping marquees of creators and languages carry the scale story between sections.

e3b113680c42449b9646afe830911fd0.description: Natroceutics is a Cape Town-based premium supplement brand selling nature-based therapeutics for integrative healthcare practitioners. The hero is pure big type — a large forest-green sans-serif statement on off-white with extreme negative space, a thin vertical rule splitting logo from nav, and a hairline down-arrow scroll cue; the cookie banner deliberately switches to a monospace typewriter face to separate legal copy from brand voice. Notable blocks: a full-bleed looping brand video, a click-and-drag / swipe horizontal gallery of 18 lifestyle images, a scrolling product range list, and a regeneration/sustainability grid of six numbered initiatives. Site by Malvah.

3177b8e81d88800ea433ff04aaa1e6a3.description: Neon (a Databricks company) is serverless Postgres positioned as the full backend for apps and AI agents: database, auth, functions, storage and an AI gateway. The hero is pitch-black with a massive tight-tracked geometric sans headline over blurred vertical light-leak streaks in cyan, lime and gold, an abstract stand-in for data flow; a small A Databricks Company badge sits above the H1 as instant authority, and a patterned promo bar rides above the nav. Notable blocks: a five-tab product switcher in the hero, each tab swapping a looping product video (Postgres / Auth / Compute / Storage / AI Gateway), an anchor-linked feature rail (AI, Autoscaling, Branching, Auth, Production features), an animated autoscaling chart comparing Neon against fixed provisioning, copy-paste CLI snippets ($ npx neonctl init) used as CTAs, a stats block (12,000,000 Postgres databases started daily) and a compliance grid in the footer. Strong reference for developer-tool dark mode and product-tab heroes.

3c270fccca9843c99dcf395d8662f402.description: Neoplants is a Paris synthetic-biology company (founded 2018, out of Station F) selling bioengineered air purification — the Neo P1 pothos, engineered to capture and recycle indoor VOCs, plus Power Drops microorganisms that boost ordinary houseplants. The hero pairs an elegant high-contrast serif at massive scale with deep forest greens, stark white and a pale mint accent. Worth stealing: color-coded typographic hierarchy where the final word flips to mint green to pull the eye down and tie the copy to the biology, and cinematic high-contrast lighting with harsh sun and deep shadow that pushes a biotech brand into prestige territory.

921f63109c1f41b68950b4c0e9ab4b88.description: NetZero connects businesses with local afforestation and ecosystem-restoration projects so they can offset emissions and hit sustainability targets. The hero is a detailed isometric landscape illustration, and the same illustration system anchors the footer, giving the page bookends. Palette is mint green, forest green and off-white with a clean sans. Techniques worth stealing: photography masked into abstract organic shapes, and floating UI cards / data overlays laid on top of the photos so the product is shown working against real terrain. Also has a logos bar, a stats block and a closing CTA.

3a37b8e81d88808dafe0eaa689392839.description: Single-page microsite by type foundry Pangram Pangram for the PP Neue Montreal grotesque, framed as an "Official Travel Guide" to Montreal — a font specimen crossed with a city guidebook. Hero is a full-bleed coral-red field with massive charcoal display type, film-grain noise over flat colour, thin horizontal rules anchoring the letterforms and a detached pill-shaped floating nav. Standout blocks: a horizontal typeface-evolution timeline (2018–2026), a circular in-use carousel, an interactive weights chart, a ligature showcase, a display-vs-text comparison and an accents/diacritics band. Framer build, site by Demande Speciale.

2147b8e81d888088886ae325ca9ba9a7.description: NEVERHACK is a French sovereign cybersecurity group (SOC/MSSP, CERT emergency response, the PROMETHEUS sovereign AI advisor) selling defence-grade security to government, defence and critical infrastructure. The hero is stark white and black with a bold large-scale sans headline and, instead of a screenshot, a live Ask PROMETHEUS chat input styled as a soft-shadowed floating field with electric-purple accents and compliance trust badges (EU-sovereign, SecNumCloud-aligned, zero retention) sitting directly under the CTA. Notable blocks: a scrolling marquee of served sectors, a defence-culture stats row with unusual metrics (120h+ training per consultant, <5% selectivity, 40+ years), numbered 01/02/03 capability cards, an ISO/ENS certification badge gallery, and a live-looking CERT emergency panel showing time-to-deploy, severity and analysts on case.

176a2455686044b89024951c6f82bc19.description: New Form Capital is a New York VC investing at the intersection of fintech, blockchain and data since 2019, with Polymarket, Sentora and BitVault in portfolio. The hero stacks massive black headline type (Advancing / the Economic / Networks of / the Future) on off-white with floating rounded-corner grayscale photos interleaved between the lines, an editorial collage that pairs crypto imagery against NYSE/Wall Street imagery. Lime-green accents, a fine wavy moire background texture and a preloader percentage counter. Notable inner structure: a stats block (90%+ pre-seed first checks, 100% blockchain allocation, 30+ investments, $100M+ AUM, founded 2019), image marquees captioned Wall Street Capitalism to Running on Blockchain Rails, and a three-circle Venn diagram (Finance / Data / Blockchain) with a green triangle marking the intersection. Built on Gatsby.

baeca0fcd9284172a4efc7b38f8f2625.description: YoungCapital NEXT is a Dutch traineeship programme placing young IT and finance talent with 2,000+ employers. Palette is forest green, off-white and black with a coral-orange accent; bold condensed sans throughout. The signature technique is shape-bleed: large organic green blobs mask and frame the lifestyle photography, giving an asymmetric, fluid composition instead of rectangular image blocks. Notable blocks: a 'Choose your path' finance/IT selector, a numbered four-step growth process (bootcamp, personal development, coaching, Club NEXT community), a trainee testimonial carousel with video, an animated stats trio (3,209 / 350 / 8.1), an FAQ accordion and an employer logo marquee.

94095d32fd4049febc4a66843a682434.description: Canopy's "Next Gen Now" campaign site — an environmental non-profit working on next-generation, forest-free materials, supercharged by The Audacious Project. The standout technique is the hero: a realistic torn-paper edge acts as a mask, and scrolling rips the black top layer away to reveal a cinematic video of craftspeople working with red textiles underneath, so the content feels uncovered rather than scrolled to. High-contrast black-and-white UI with the organic tan fibre texture of the paper tear as the only warm note, clean geometric sans, pill-outline buttons, and a floating bottom-left attribution block. Strong reference for tactile masking against digital-smooth video. Sections below the hero unverified in headless render.

3177b8e81d8880da8fd8c8b687197b67.description: Nfinite (Nfinite Nanotechnology, a University of Waterloo spin-out) makes ultra-high-barrier paper that replaces flexible plastic packaging: an invisible ceramic coating applied by Spatial Atomic Layer Deposition, 100% curbside recyclable, backed by Amcor, PepsiCo and Unilever. Site by Numbered. Deep-tech materials story told through consumer product photography (chips, protein bar, energy gel, granola, milk) shown as a swipeable card rail, a spec grid of barrier performance (WVTR, OTR, grease, grammage) that reads like a datasheet but stays elegant, an animated cross-section diagram of the SALD two-gas coating process with a dotted-pattern layer, and an impact block built on big claims (40% lower carbon footprint, 2 trillion fewer plastic packages). Quotes from Amcor/PepsiCo/Unilever executives act as testimonials, plus an FAQ and a press-release list. Visuals unverified (JS error in headless render), so structure is described from HTML.

48f02286f3b043e1b53b6d6c3006151f.description: Portfolio of Niccolò Miranda, an interactive designer and developer working in motion, typography and creative coding. The site is styled as a printed newspaper: a split editorial grid with thin vertical rules and structured columns, textured parchment background with a subtle paper grain, stark black ink and colour arriving only from the project thumbnails. Type is high-contrast serif, anchored by an ultra-oversized condensed serif in the lower band. Extreme scale contrast between display type and tiny utility text, plus a small "TIP!" microcopy hint teaching the horizontal navigation.

a03c5b43d77340c789be9ae8b00384f0.description: Personal brand site for Nick Velten, a Dutch entrepreneur, investor and advisor selling business growth consulting, interim management and board-level advisory. It is a strong reference for the 'solo operator as premium brand' problem: bold high-contrast sans headers on a beige, black and sage-green palette give it an editorial magazine feel instead of the usual consultant-portfolio look. Notable blocks: a geographic timeline that turns career history into a route, a marquee of scrolling expertise labels used as a credibility strip, and a testimonial section. Smooth scroll-triggered entrance animations, a minimal sticky nav with capsule buttons, and a decorative animated scribble line threading sections into the footer.

16c7b8e81d88803b98c2c522b6652359.description: Nod is an onsite coding bootcamp in Stockholm (10-week GenAI and Data Analytics tracks with a money-back guarantee, plus short corporate trainings). The hero sits on a warm cream canvas where the word "CODING" is literally built out of primitive geometric shapes (circles, arcs, triangles) in saturated orange-red, sky blue, royal blue, sage and mustard, with thin black connector lines dropping from the shapes like technical leads — a proprietary letter-construction system worth stealing. Type is a friendly geometric sans and the subhead is offset asymmetrically so the centered graphic never feels stiff. Notable blocks: a bootcamp dates-and-pricing table, a five-panel "Stockholm Experience" city slider, review-score badges (Course Report, Switchup, Career Karma) and a graduate testimonial set with employer names. Site by Waaark.

3a37b8e81d8880cd8b25d20c606c9398.description: Nolla Health is a US telehealth product offering AI-guided symptom triage with licensed-clinician review — a chat-first "How are you feeling?" entry point, $39 clinician message reviews, prescriptions sent to pharmacy, plus a dermatology app and a skin-cancer scan tool. Structure centres on a conversational input hero with clinician portrait avatars and HIPAA trust marks, a numbered three-step care flow, editorial cards for Nolla MD and Knowledge, a specialty-care section with "In Development" states and a long FAQ accordion. Strong inner pages: /technology, /skincare and a 615-article /learning library. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render).

1d07b8e81d88800fb2d5cd05f0bfb93e.description: Noovo is a Las Vegas camper-van manufacturer building premium Class B RVs (Lite, Plus, Next AWD) with European craftsmanship — "we convert lives, not just vans". Site by Rejouice (credited in the footer). The homepage is a full-bleed photographic hero with large overlaid statement type ("Welcome to the great indoors"), running as a stacked multi-model scroll narrative where each van model gets its own photo panel with a price-from figure and dual CTAs. Notable: a live-tracking banner following an owner road trip to Alaska, a full van configurator (/configure), a dealer and ambassador map, an owner-testimonial avatar block and an FAQ accordion; modal UI uses large border radii, warm neutral greys and a golden-yellow CTA. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) — a newsletter modal plus cookie banner block the headless capture.

adcc4ba9056045a6814cf2b05424bb40.description: Nord Quantique is a Canadian quantum computing company building fault-tolerant machines with bosonic error-correcting codes and a 1:1 logical-to-physical qubit ratio. Visually it avoids the usual 'tech blue' quantum cliche: the palette is deep plum and dusty lavender with white type, warmed by gold and copper metallic tones from the hardware photography. The hero is a large product shot of the gold-plated dilution refrigerator paired with the value prop, entered through a pixel-block dissolve transition over a video background. Strongest inner blocks are a vertical 'Our achievements' timeline (2020 to 2025 milestones) and an image-backed feature grid; there is also a lab video section and a people/team block.

922ba2c354c649388cbd53e4af82aa87.description: Norgram is a Danish design studio (Copenhagen and Aarhus) co-founded by Mathias Host Normark and Sebastian Gram, doing brand identity and digital for Google, SPACE10, Nike, AWS and IKEA, with 50+ awards including D&AD and Webby. The hero is an asymmetric split: a scrolling visual portfolio on the left against an oversized typographic statement (Forming Essentials) on the right, in high-contrast charcoal and off-white with a single red accent. The standout technique is an OS-style floating notification widget carrying studio news into an otherwise static layout, plus barcode-like vertical glitch graphics used to break up flat minimalist space. Work index is numbered with dotted date codes (01.19 / 2024); studio pages use section numbering (N11-N15) and four diagram-icon principle cards.

1de4d7d865cf408685eb396a2465b650.description: Product page for Nortera, a North American canned and frozen vegetable manufacturer selling custom private-label products to B2B buyers. The hero runs a full-width background video of a canning production line with an all-caps sans headline and a circular inset image of fresh vegetables. The page is structured as a numbered narrative (1–4) walking through the value chain — technology, product characteristics, packaging, shipping — with an interactive illustrated carrot selector for cut types (julienne, slices, cubes, whole) and a clean line-drawing grid for packaging formats, which makes dry technical spec content genuinely browsable. Earthy forest-green and sage palette, closing on oversized NORTERA footer branding.

3177b8e81d88800e97e6c5e2e34e747a.description: Nuraform is a free AI-powered form builder positioned squarely between "Google Forms is too plain" and "Typeform is too expensive": describe the form in a prompt, get a conversational, animated form plus built-in analytics (views, drop-offs, completion, AI summaries). The hero is loud and modern: electric orange-to-magenta-to-lavender gradient blobs, a high-contrast serif headline, and lifestyle photography masked inside a large circle, with a frosted-glass AI prompt bar sitting directly on the image so the product demos itself above the fold. Strong blocks: an audience switcher where hovering a persona swaps the portrait and copy, a 01/02/03 process section built entirely from autoplaying product videos, and chat-bubble testimonials. Decorative SVG motifs frame each section instead of plain dividers.

3d17553581fc4a80a39722abdb82ace6.description: NutsDev is a Kyiv-based creative design studio (Framer, Webflow and Wix specialists) selling client work alongside a large template library. The hero is pure black with heavy film grain and a massive tight-kerned white sans headline "We speak fluent design" layered over a scattered asymmetric masonry of darkened project thumbnails — an editorial mood-board feel where the type overlaps imagery for depth, plus a pulsing orange "Available for work" dot in the nav. The homepage is essentially one giant scroll- and drag-to-move interactive portfolio canvas holding 30+ named projects with category labels, with deeper Works, Labs and About pages.

db6ca4d0d88443379132e455e153f8c5.description: NZero is an AI-powered energy optimization and decarbonization platform — automated utility data collection, peak demand management and retrofit planning. Split hero: copy on the left, product dashboard UI on the right. High-contrast structure with a dark charcoal hero and footer bracketing white content sections, amber/orange as the accent, clean sans throughout. The block worth studying is the numbered solution storytelling (Solution 1, 2, 3), where each claim is paired with the specific UI snapshot that delivers it, plus bold oversized percentages carrying the data-backed claims. Also has a logos bar, a features section with background video, an industry-category gallery and case studies.

16d7b8e81d88804ca37ae6f3497ba8f9.description: Oakâme is a French furniture brand making indoor and outdoor pieces from reclaimed 18th–19th century oak beams salvaged from old European buildings (sofas, benches, dining tables; €1,200–10,100). WooCommerce; site credited to Beaucoup Studio. Hero is a full-bleed lifestyle photograph with a big-type collection name overlaid and a small thumbnail strip in the bottom-right that lets you swap the hero image without leaving the landing state, all held inside a thin structural border that makes the page feel like a gallery wall. Quiet-luxury palette of warm sand, natural oak, terracotta and olive. Best inner block: the KONNEKT NFC traceability section, where scanning a chip in the furniture reveals the history of the beam it was made from, a genuinely good sustainability-storytelling device.

3437b8e81d888091a80ced7c8a99ede6.description: The Obsidian Assembly is a speculative design project by Fiddle.Digital (part of its Imagine Possible initiative), presented as a secretive private collective of makers running seven undisclosed physical spaces and the objects created inside them. The hero is a photoreal 3D obsidian stone floating in a warm sand-and-charcoal palette, with editorial high-contrast serif type weaving in front of and behind the object and hairline connector lines pinning labels to it; a grain overlay keeps the gradients tactile. Notable blocks: an Explore Places section with a counted room carousel (Silent Room 4/7), an Origin Objects gallery linking each item back to its place of origin, a rolling Updates / Now Forming status feed (place status, item release, formation), a People section, and an Admission application form written as a vetted request rather than a signup. Excellent reference for mystique-driven luxury branding, restrained dark editorial layouts and gated-access UX.

59c50b95d6a448e186240882acd7a444.description: Obys Agency, a Ukrainian digital design studio with a heavy awards record. The site is live but gated behind a long numeric preloader: a pure black-and-white void with a centred geometric mark and a tiny off-centre progress number, which never completes in a headless browser. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render). The intro screen itself is worth noting as a reference for "void" premium branding, extreme negative space and microscopic edge-anchored UI counters.

3177b8e81d8880b8aacad2c36cbe0688.description: Occupied is a brand site for Occupy, a Taiwanese bespoke jewelry label that sells rings and regalia as "symbols of personal power" through a ritual, members-only process. Design by UN@DSGN, build by Ning Huang. Luxury-punk art direction: black and chrome with a visceral red fold, hyper-real 3D metallic thorn/crown renders, thin vertical grid lines dividing the composition, and a typographic pairing of high-contrast serif English with sharp thin-stroke Chinese calligraphy. Notable blocks: a numbered collection index (Scars of Dominion, Thorned Regalia, Crown's Eclipse) where each name reveals its own image, a dated event timeline of rituals, salons and club nights that reads like an occult diary, a kinetic word marquee (Power / Sacrifice / Oath in Shadows / Ritual), and an invitation form gated by a code instead of a normal signup. Good reference for dark editorial commerce and scrolltelling.

6ad607815b5646a282251c7e9ed28174.description: OCHI is a presentation and storytelling agency (Vancouver + Lviv) building pitch decks, executive keynotes, sales decks, branded templates and brand identities for innovation teams and global brands — Yahoo, DoorDash, Medallia, Uber, Lexus, Salience Labs, Trawa, All Things Go. Awwwards-recognised, site by Obys. The hero is off-white and black with an ultra-bold condensed sans headline at extreme scale; the technique worth stealing is visual-in-text — an image container dropped inline into the headline flow so a picture becomes a word. Colour arrives only from embedded project imagery and a Site of the Day badge. A full-screen percentage preloader sets the tone before the reveal. Notable blocks: a WE ARE OCHI marquee, a featured-case grid with service tags per project, and an unusually long client-review section with named roles and services listed per testimonial.

16d7b8e81d8880d89129ddd0640537c8.description: Shaga Odyssey is the pre-sale page for what it calls the world's first web3 gaming controller, from Shaga, a community-powered cloud-gaming network. The controller splits in half via a metal-blade "unified clip" so it converts from a console pad into a mobile grip, and carries a removable hardware wallet and fingerprint reader for in-game crypto transactions. The page is built as a long feature scroll: a token-tier progress ladder with live sale counters and scarcity copy ("756 left to epic tier"), then feature-by-feature hardware breakdowns (haptics, IP54, thumbsticks, weight target), closing with a full spec sheet. Visuals unverified (the headless screenshot render failed repeatedly, likely a WebGL/3D scene), so the hero treatment is not confirmed.

8108037ef4b34be68ffca14a6c4f8c7a.description: Off Menu is an AI-native product studio designing agentic interfaces for startups; senior-only team, 18+ years of experience, clients raised $600M+ in 2024 (Flex case study on site). Stark white hero with black high-contrast sans and an orbital layout of circle-masked project vignettes floating around the central value proposition. Pill-shaped CTA and a dotted scroll indicator add polish; whitespace does most of the work. Good reference for calm AI-studio positioning without gradient cliches.

34e7b8e81d8880dca5ede4d62c485084.description: OGAKI is a NYC/LA social-first agency for prestige beauty brands (Laura Mercier, EltaMD, T3, NuFACE). Editorial, fashion-magazine aesthetic: cream/off-white background, oversized overlapping sans letterforms bleeding off-canvas, tilted and layered behind an elegant serif tagline, plus a live localized clock in the header. Client-logo marquee, award badges wall (three-time Digital Agency of the Year), photography-led service teasers and rotating case-study cards. A small cookie notice remains visible in the capture. Great reference for type-driven "prestige" branding without hero imagery.

16c7b8e81d8880109202f0773a0320fd.description: Oilstainlab is a California hypercar house selling the HF-11, a 1,950 lb, 650 hp, 12,000 rpm car with a swappable combustion/electric powertrain, all in a maximal "maniac" brand voice. The site opens with a WebGL splash gate: macro carbon-fibre weave and a motion-blurred chassis, huge staggered all-caps words (BESPOKE / MYTH / CHAOS / MANIAC) layered both in front of and behind the imagery for a 3D sandwich effect, an all-black-and-grey palette broken only by a single safety-orange ENTER button, and a drag hint. Past the gate the page runs a big-type HF/11 hero with a spec stat row, a horizontal chaptered "car tour" (Power, Origin, Beauty, Asylum, Obsession, Strength) each with its own gallery, an engine-sound player, marquee text loops and a commission form. Post-gate visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render); the splash itself was verified.

f5f53099cdfe4e7a9c0df4b8bdfe921d.description: OK C'EST COOL — "new playgrounds new ideas" — a French interactive/creative studio site. Note the apex domain (okcest.cool) now returns a Vercel "deployment not found" 404; only the www host (www.okcest.cool) still resolves, so the saved link may need updating to www. Visuals unverified: the www host repeatedly crashed the headless renderer on both desktop and mobile viewports, so hero type and blocks are left unset rather than invented. The existing 3D / motion / scrolltelling tags suggest a WebGL-heavy build, which matches the render failure.

3648177335f146be92f03377c1c43237.description: Portfolio of Olha Uzhykova, an LA-based design director, mentor and consultant working in UI/UX and design management. Sage green, cream and charcoal palette with a high-contrast serif over a clean sans. Worth stealing: organic fluid shapes that react to scroll, a circular text-path animation, and portfolio hover reveals that show project imagery inside circular masks. Includes an awards logos bar and a separate teaching/speaking gallery.

e48c11eefdab4b87ac188d97fca350aa.description: Personal/brand site whose existing metadata points to a pastel, illustrated, patterned design with big type. Across two headless capture attempts (including a longer wait) the page rendered only as a dark loading state, so visuals are unverified (loader in headless render). The domain resolves; only the visual render could not be completed.

3347b8e81d8880ef94e8dfbd2972134a.description: ON.energy builds and operates hyperscale power systems (battery storage, power electronics and the ON.command control layer) for AI data centres, mission-critical facilities and grid-scale assets. The hero pairs a light-weight geometric sans headline (Perfect Power for AI Factories) with a semi-transparent x-ray render of the hardware over a looping video, lit by a deep bottom-weighted gradient and a single safety-yellow accent; a floating bottom-right discovery card pushes the AI UPS product without crowding the headline. Notable blocks: a four-item trust strip (Tier-1 components, gigawatt-scale supply chain, US manufacturing, fault-tolerant architecture), a three-card expertise selector (AI Workloads / Power Quality / Grid Volatility), an animated stats block (3 GW+ operating, 99.9% uptime, 10+ GW capacity, 75+ projects) driven by a scroll trail video, and a segmented press/news feed. Clean reference for industrial dark-mode B2B and x-ray product visualisation.

93089b5b603c403bb1b51015ea3c863e.description: one.app is now OnePay, a consumer super-app bundling banking, saving, investing and crypto in one account — rebranded since it was saved, so the current design differs from the saved tags. The hero is a handheld product shot: a phone held at an angle with a bright yellow case acting as the focal point against warm blurred lifestyle photography with shallow depth of field. UI in the mockup stays black-and-white with sky-blue accents so the app reads clean against the busy backdrop. Rounded high-contrast CTAs. Solid reference for consumer fintech that wants tactile and aspirational rather than illustrated.

ab86cf05d7b94d309e5f27de322cc347.description: Oneflow is a Swedish contract-lifecycle-management and e-signature SaaS that turns contracts into structured data. The hero is a left-aligned split: bold geometric sans headline on a dark charcoal-plum field, with layered floating product-UI fragments on the right (risk doughnut charts, GDPR compliance tags) building depth through overlapping cards. High-energy gold/yellow accent buttons pop against the dark base — a strong dark-mode B2B palette worth stealing. Also useful for its layered product-UI showcase, customer logo bar and stats treatment.

795d2695e9cc4e2bbdc230537fa38558.description: OneKey is an open-source, self-custodial crypto hardware and software wallet company (Classic 1S, Pro, Touch), backed by Coinbase Ventures and YZi Labs. The hero is a polished isometric 3D scene on a clean white-and-grey base with neon green accents: hardware sits among floating frosted-glass UI panels lit by soft emissive under-glow. The clever bit is spatial iconography, where platform mascots (the Android bot, Tux, the Windows mark) are placed as physical props in the scene to communicate cross-platform support without a feature list. Below, product cards carry each device, and the footer is an unusually deep sitemap spanning shop, developer, security and migration guides.

c583cde0f68a4de2972c85a440e65554.description: One Right Eye is a browser-based patient-education tool for ophthalmologists, built around detailed interactive 3D models of the eye and visual system. The hero floats a high-fidelity exploded 3D eye over oversized sans type, white background with purple accents and anatomical reds for a clinical-but-premium feel. Floating pill navigation and a Scroll to discover cue lead into scrolltelling sections. Great reference for medical 3D storytelling and healthcare UI that does not feel sterile.

586c92394ed14c0a90994885074c4bed.description: REDIRECTED: the saved Opal Tadpole product page now sends you to op.al, Opal Electronics' single-page manifesto ('the table', June 2026) announcing the rebrand and the fact that the camera line is being retired. What is there now is a narrative hero, a bottom-up shot through a glass table showing prototypes and components in industrial greys, warm wood and cool glass with primary-colour accents, lowercase minimal sans, long-form essay copy and no conventional CTA. Still a useful reference for manifesto-style landing pages and product-as-still-life photography, but it is no longer the Tadpole webcam page it was saved for.

c9e79104bf81446cb81a66f87777128d.description: Due is a borderless multi-currency payments platform (stablecoins plus local currency, 150+ countries, fully non-custodial wallet, API for developers). The hero is high-contrast black and white with a single vivid blue focal point: a massive ultra-bold geometric headline layered behind a translucent blue card, a globe rendered as a stylised halftone dot pattern, and a floating pill nav. Notable blocks: a rotating verb carousel (Pay / Send / Receive / Exchange / Get paid), a set of cursor-following card videos, an expandable country-coverage list grouped by region with per-country currency icons, a developer/API block, and a 'SECU-RITY IS EVERYTHING' section built on biometric video. Solid press logos bar.

88a4fae11f3f4cc68ab8f1143f44820f.description: Openhome is a developer platform for ambient, always-on, local voice AI devices ("Build Real World AI Devices", deploy on your own DevKit). The hero runs a high-contrast editorial serif headline over near-black, with a layered translucent purple-to-magenta gradient waveform as the central visual metaphor for voice, and a restrained monochrome integrations logo bar (Spotify, Apple Music, Nest, hue, ChatGPT, Uber) doing the social proof. Rare and useful reference for a serif-led dark AI site that avoids the usual generic sans + blue treatment; the DevKit and Developers pages are the strongest inner pages.

44b9d766adc84df5ab1d340bf58aca2c.description: Opera is the browser maker's main marketing site, selling the desktop and mobile browsers plus the Opera GX gaming variant. The hero is centred copy over a soft lavender-to-peach background gradient, with a large bold geometric-sans headline, a blue-purple download CTA and a cropped browser-product preview anchored at the base; the signature red logo is the lone high-saturation accent. Depth comes from layering — subtle shadows on the product preview plus a floating modal overlay — and a promotional banner strip runs above the header. Useful reference for airy pastel-gradient consumer-software heroes.

d7c67e05155d4b678546fd0da7a661f5.description: ORE is an exclusive bespoke diamond house (bridal, custom cuts, diamond sourcing) with celebrity collaborations including Drake, 88rising and Rich Brian. The hero is a full-bleed video with macro brand typography used architecturally: the ORE letterforms frame the footage rather than sit on it, creating collage depth, with nav pushed to the extreme margins. Palette is quiet-luxury muted taupe, warm sepia and desaturated blush, with tiny wide-tracked all-caps sans contrasting the massive display type. The most distinctive block is a recurring diamond-fact stats device: a bare number (3.5-3.53, 12.011, 160.93, $600 billion) paired with a trivia line, reused as a rhythmic interstitial between sections. Portfolio uses hover-triggered video thumbnails in a numbered slider.

16c7b8e81d8880ddb1eac9cdadee3983.description: ORKEN is a fantasy transmedia IP (novels, setting books, illustrated tomes, a game) from Berlin art studio SIXMOREVODKA, launched via Kickstarter with Wave 1 now shipping. Website by Spatzek Studio. The hero is a duotone illustration play: flat safety-orange field, a grayscale armoured character rim-lit in the same orange so figure and background bleed into each other, an aggressive brush-script logotype, and a single blunt line, "Together we fight. Some of us will die." Massive flat negative space forces attention onto the character art. Notable blocks: a four-slot teaser video grid with runtimes, a numbered lore/world section written as in-world narration ("THIS IS EDOM"), a product render gallery for the books, and a newsletter block with a live signup counter framed as recruitment ("Abiders have already signed up"). Excellent reference for IP, game and entertainment launches.

8e65c5181c574a49b15f0f118ec560cd.description: Orson is a Paris-based executive advisory firm for strategy and communication, founded in 2021 by Patrick Ropert and Mouna Sepehri, positioning itself as AI-centric, senior-led and business-focused. Instead of a classic services grid the site is built as a set of manifesto-style pillar pages (is AI-Centric, is Business-Focused, is Senior-Led, and Forward-Thinking), individual founder profile pages, and an Opinions editorial section — a useful model for consultancies that want depth and point of view rather than a feature list. Visuals unverified (client-side JS exception in headless render), so hero composition, palette and typography are not confirmed.

2cd7b8e81d888013bdb3ee5a3354ddf9.description: Osmo is a dev toolkit and resource vault for creative developers by Dennis Snellenberg and Ilja van Eck (35+ Awwwards Site of the Day wins between them): 190+ production-ready components, animations, page transitions, sliders, an SVG icon library and a private Slack community, all documented for Webflow or plain HTML/CSS/JS, with a free 20-resource demo and a paid full Vault. Off-white and black base energised by lime green and royal purple, bold tight-tracked sans, and a large purple star glyph set inside the headline as a visual anchor. Worth stealing: the fanned, curved arrangement of product cards that adds depth and invites hover exploration, the neon marquee ticker that keeps the page feeling alive, and the way the components demo themselves live rather than sitting in static screenshots. Basically a reference site about reference-quality interactions.

3687b8e81d8880529cd8e9cd32167074.description: Merch store of design agency ++hellohello (Uruguay). Viewport-filling brand headline in red on cream, editorial spec-sheet grid under a thick horizontal rule; preloader counts 000-100 with flashing product images. Minimal e-commerce: product grid of apparel with typographic-joke names (Kerned Confidence, Whitespace Matters), bare cart. Strong ref for designer merch, editorial e-commerce minimalism and type-as-image heroes.

7b2c3b51f3ec479687aee19fd8d6c470.description: Outhere Music is an independent music label group. The hero is a stark black-and-white editorial composition: a massive, kerned-out serif headline over grainy, atmospheric photography, with asymmetrically placed descriptive text. The dramatic scale contrast and monochrome palette create a sophisticated magazine aesthetic.

16c7b8e81d8880618924f7be02b7ef7a.description: Work index of Outloud, a Bratislava/Dover design and software studio building for clients "from startups to NASDAQ giants" (moved from work.outloud.co, now the /our-work page on the main domain). Massive typographic header over a striking peach-to-dark-burgundy vertical gradient, with pill-shaped filter chips and a filterable case-study grid (CloudTalk, Forbes, OVB, Pohoda) where entries carry five-star ratings. Closes with a dual-CTA contact block featuring real offices and a direct line to the CEO.

71b2a97f73d84443a60efdb7fefc7dc4.description: Poklonnaya 9 (P9) is the developer site for ANT Development’s 34-storey premium residential tower in the Dorogomilovo district of Moscow, its silhouette explicitly modelled on the Stalin-era Moscow high-rises and New York skyscrapers. 521 apartments (49–176 m²) offered in three interior schemes — industrial, modern elegant and ageless classic — plus penthouses of 250–428 m² with terraces, over a five-star hotel base with restaurants, boutiques, spa, Olympic pool, gym and banquet halls. Good reference for premium real-estate storytelling: rather than a spec sheet the site is built as lifestyle chapters, with a strong Lifestyle / 24h “day in the complex” narrative page alongside Location, Infrastructure and About. Available in EN and RU. Visuals unverified — the site does not respond to headless render or fetch from foreign infrastructure (likely geo/IP filtering), so no hero type recorded.

96f1dadb3e7e472fb7f4f35c6c340c19.description: Palette Supply is a Shopify store selling premium digital downloads for working creatives — real-photo mockups, Canva/Figma/Adobe-compatible templates, planners and branding resources, made with real photographs by working photographers and designers. The saved URL points at the Furniture collection, which currently renders as an empty-state collection page. Visually it is an editorial e-commerce reference: near-monochrome white/black with deep-blue accents in the announcement bar and a floating 15% Off badge, a clean geometric sans for nav paired with a monospace-inspired face for category labels, and extreme whitespace with hairline dividers doing all the structural work instead of boxes or cards. Notable blocks: sticky promo announcement bar, minimal category/collection nav, categorised footer and newsletter sign-up.

2497b8e81d88809d8b8dd6a823b040c1.description: Pallet is an AI logistics workforce automating freight workflows — quoting, data entry, billing, customer service — for brokerages, forwarders, carriers and warehouses. The hero is a split, layered composition: left-aligned clean sans headline over a moody aerial night photograph of a container port (deep teal and navy with warm golden industrial lights), with a multi-layered product UI window overlapping the photo and a floating "Agents" menu on top for a glassmorphic depth effect. The key technique is grounding abstract AI software in real industrial photography. Notable numbers-driven case-study cards (10% margin lift, 95% automation, 98% touchless load entry) and an unusual benchmark bar chart comparing Pallet's touchless rate against GPT-5, Claude and Gemini. Dedicated inner pages per operation type. Built on Astro + Sanity.

34f9208e91e046aea83009fedad2883d.description: Pangram Pangram is a world-renowned independent type foundry (founded 2018 by Mat Desjardins) selling premium, free-to-try fonts on a Shopify storefront, licenses from $40. The homepage rotates image-led hero banners where warm macro photography is matched to each font's personality (fizzy citrus for the humanist Palma), set against a stark white/black UI with a red "New" badge and pill-shaped solid/outline buttons. Notable blocks: a font catalog grid with card/list toggle and animated live specimens, a "Fonts in use" case-study gallery, a "Trusted by" logos bar (Apple, Netflix, Pepsi, FIFA), microsite promos, and a Pangram Academy blog. A benchmark for how a foundry merges e-commerce with editorial specimen craft.

7a42ff847faa436eac1044543df47f84.description: Site of Panic, an award-winning animation and design studio (founded 2014 by Gints Gutmanis) that builds brand stories through illustration, animation, CGI and motion graphics, with clients including Netflix. The full-screen hero is an immersive, cinematic scene in a vintage 70s palette (deep teals, earthy browns, warm reds, cream) with a bold high-contrast serif headline, retro film grain, scratches and soft-focus tint. The studio's cheeky personality shows through censored symbols and playful background animation, all funneling to a single "Explore works" CTA. A strong reference for retro-cinematic branding and personality-forward motion studios.

3177b8e81d88802f897bf20aaaaee8fb.description: Parable is Anne Lee Skates' solo-GP venture firm (ex-a16z; Whatnot, Kindred, Cider) writing up to $10M cheques into consumer and prosumer AI. The whole site is built on the literary conceit in its name: the hero is a surreal layered scene of deep blues, cerulean and peach cloudscapes with a fine line-art dome, under an elegant high-contrast serif headline (To miracles shaping humanity), with a mask-reveal video used as a scroll transition between sections. The standout block is Philosophies of Parable, six numbered investment principles each illustrated by a story and a painterly image (Maya Lin and the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, David and Goliath, Odysseus and the Sirens, Steve Jobs on beauty), turning a thesis page into narrative content. Other blocks: a portfolio list that names stealth companies by one-line description, a prior-investments list annotated with stage and entry point, long-form founder testimonials, and an essays index. Excellent reference for narrative-led VC positioning and how to make a thesis feel like a worldview.

2497b8e81d8880b7a94eeeaf75042120.description: Paraform is an agentic hiring platform and recruiter marketplace ("Hire on easy mode") connecting 1,000+ companies with 10k+ specialist startup recruiters. The hero is a full-bleed background MP4 — shallow-depth-of-field macro footage in deep forest green, charcoal and warm wood tones — overlaid with a bold serif headline, a pill-shaped inline email capture and a logo ticker (Palantir, Rippling, Scale, Hex) pinned at the bottom. Distinctive: stats are woven into the feature sections rather than isolated in one band (10k+ recruiters, 70% interview rate, 3x faster to hire, 98% satisfaction), video testimonial cards link through to full customer stories, and the site ships a custom cursor. Premium serif-on-video treatment is unusual for HR tech, closer to a hospitality brand. Strong inner pages: /customers, /product, /specialties.

310d6707d9a04a77a5b8ea362626c28a.description: Parhelie is a French tax and legal consultancy for innovative businesses; this is their agency/cabinet page. The hero is the whole idea: a glowing orb suspended inside a wireframe cube that tilts with cursor parallax, set in midnight black with crisp white bold sans type, yellow logo accents and subtle cyan-purple iridescent gradients on the 3D geometry. The page opens with a bold colour-wipe transition before settling into the dark theme, and navigation stays out of the way behind a single circular Menu button plus a minimal scroll cue. Useful reference for how a professional-services firm can feel like a tech product without illustration or stock photography.

a8a7dcf689a74d768a1257dd3e3619ca.description: Site of the Ukrainian Laboratory of Legislative Initiatives (Лабораторія законодавчих ініціатив), an analytical think tank publishing research on parliamentary, judicial and anti-corruption reform (Аналітика / Спецпроєкти / Новини, EN version available). The hero is a split layout: an authoritative high-contrast serif headline on the left, and on the right a collage that mixes architectural photography with abstract line art. Monochrome black-and-white base with sharp purple accents, generous whitespace and a strict editorial grid. Strong reference for think-tank / policy publishing: how to make dense analytical content feel premium and readable rather than institutional.

a240dd53638e4df795353d28bdc4c23e.description: Patreon is the membership platform where creators earn recurring income directly from fans (80M+ users, founded 2013). The hero is a cinematic photo/video of an artist mid-work in amber, brown and muted purple, with an oversized thin wide-set sans headline; the artist's hand and stylus overlap the type to create real depth, and a small featured-creator bubble supplies instant social proof. Notable blocks: a creator testimonial wall, a 'what can I offer my community' benefit grid (shoutouts, polls, livestreams, group chats, merch, early access), an integrations block ('Works with Patreon'), a creator-discovery module and an editorial resources row. Reliable reference for creator-economy positioning and warm, human product photography.

0f2c447e040e4c3ba73f490f37fc7f7b.description: Portfolio of Patrick Heng, a creative developer known for WebGL and interactive experiments. The domain resolves but paints only a blank canvas in a headless browser across repeated attempts, the usual behaviour for a WebGL-driven site. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render). Saved tags describe bright colours, big type, flat illustration and horizontal scrolling.

6cc6d3b4fa22423ea938f15a3ff241b0.description: Pauli & Sisters is a fragrance-free natural skincare brand built around an 11-botanical body oil, descended from the family formula behind Bio-Oil. It runs on Shopify but the front page is art-directed like a fashion brand: full-bleed photography in muted skin tones and pale blue, with every piece of type and branding set in a vivid lime green, pairing a playful serif for the central message with a bold rounded sans for navigation. Best detail to steal — an out-of-stock state handled as a full-page editorial hero instead of an apologetic banner. Product pages and a skincare blog sit behind it.

81ddff96aaed40769bcb5d763cbf92aa.description: Pebble sells the Pebble Flow, an all-electric semi-autonomous travel trailer pitched as "an iPhone-like experience for RVing" — self-hitching, remote-controllable, seven days off-grid. The hero is full-bleed redwood-forest footage with the trailer nestled inside it, overlaid by a huge lowercase tight-kerned geometric sans "meet pebble"; natural greens and browns get cut by an international-orange announcement bar and CTA, and floating rounded nav elements add depth. The page works as a scroll-driven film reel: each feature (Magic Hitch, Easy Tow, InstaCamp, Remote Control) is a still that swaps to autoplaying video, with a press-quote rail carrying Time, Forbes, CNET and Wired. Strong inner pages: /pebble-flow and /pebble-app.

2cd7b8e81d8880da9fe1ddb2f1244567.description: Peec AI is a Framer-built SaaS that tracks how brands appear inside AI search engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), reporting visibility, position and sentiment. Classic centred SaaS hero: a tiered two-tone headline, a subhead with inline pill icons embedded mid-sentence, dual CTAs, and a large dashboard preview anchored just below. Minimalist grayscale base (white, charcoal, soft grays) with colour pops reserved strictly for data-viz inside the product mockup. Strong reference for dense product-UI storytelling: mock dashboards, a quadrant chart of brands, a comparison-style ranking block, and a long list of tracked prompts as an interactive-feeling section.

9f42f67aff7d4a219fb1053388cd98f0.description: Peptone is a translational biophysics company using AI and experimental physics to design small-molecule drugs against intrinsically disordered proteins in cancer — the ~6,200 human proteins AlphaFold cannot model. The hero is the reason to save this one: a monochrome layout with a single vivid purple accent, over a procedural background of ultra-thin undulating lines warping around a purple spine of nodes, so the visual is literally protein folding rather than generic abstract tech. Depth comes entirely from layered linework, no gradients or 3D. The strongest inner block is a three-step Process (Measure maps transient pockets → Model models moving ensembles → Design designs candidates), followed by pipeline cards (AR-NTD, c-Myc, TDP-43).

16b1cdb92fa44504b2d96931fb2b772f.description: Phantom is a multichain crypto wallet. The hero blends a large geometric-sans headline with a playful, iridescent pastel 3D scene: a peeking mascot, a floating debit card and golden star accents over a grainy blue gradient with frosted-glass elements. Playful brand integration turns abstract product features into an inviting landscape, with a strong central hierarchy between big type and a high-contrast CTA. Further down the page cover product UI, feature blocks and a closing call to action.

9f7149225e42439ebb098b0717556098.description: Phenomenon Studio, a boutique product design and development agency (founded 2019, 70+ specialists across Europe, USA, Estonia and Switzerland). Hero is a big-type / product-shot hybrid: a huge tight-tracked sans headline on deep black, generous negative space, and tilted overlapping device mockups that showcase UI work with real depth. High-energy orange is reserved for the primary CTA while the secondary button sits in low-contrast grey, a clean example of button hierarchy. Solid reference for agency sites that need to prove UI craft in the first screen.

165b0bc8d79340dabdbb037931fc586e.description: Philosophical Foxes is an NFT art project; the site now shows a farewell/sunset screen for the collection. It centers a detailed pixel-art illustration that reimagines Raphael's 'School of Athens' with blockchain motifs and busts of Satoshi and Vitalik, on a muted cream and sand palette with a vibrant orange fox and deep teal accents. The 'crypto-classical' blend of high-art composition with 8-bit retro-gaming visuals is the memorable move worth stealing.

2fc7b8e81d8880658373c303576491cf.description: Photoncycle (Norway) sells year-round home energy: solar plus a compact underground store based on patented solid-hydrogen technology (up to 10,000 kWh, roughly 20x denser than lithium-ion), delivered as a monthly subscription with installation included. The site translates hard deep-tech into a warm consumer story: a full-bleed autumn photograph of a home with a frosted-glass card holding the headline, generous leading, and a soft rounded-corner language across buttons and containers. Palette is seasonal - autumn golds and sky blue against white and translucent grey - which quietly reinforces the "store the summer sun for winter" pitch. Notable blocks: a how-it-works sequence explaining the reversible fuel cell in plain language, savings claims (10-50% of energy cost), and an FAQ carrying the objections a homeowner would actually have. Good reference for glassmorphism used with purpose rather than decoration.

16c7b8e81d888024b0fac767b4744c57.description: Picsart is an AI creative platform for photo, video and audio generation and editing that aggregates 125+ third-party models (GPT Image, Seedance, Sora, Nano Banana, Flux, Kling, Veo) behind one subscription, plus agents, personas and a node-based "Flow" workflow builder. The hero is a dark split composition: bold rounded sans headline and magenta CTA on the left, a vertical style-carousel of the same portrait re-rendered in different AI styles on the right, and a floating prompt-bar mock of the real product UI at center bottom — high-contrast neon-on-black with saturated blues, reds and purples bleeding out of the generated imagery. Steal-worthy blocks: the side-by-side model comparison, the huge Flow-template card wall grouped by use case, the model catalog with capability chips (4K, Audio, Cinematic, Reference input) and a stats band (1B+ edits/month).

99440d62e4a64a9ca20b29b2ac8c70d8.description: Pipe is a fintech offering embedded capital and revenue-based financing for small businesses through software platforms. The hero uses an asymmetric split: a stark black panel with bold white sans type and a terracotta-orange accent word, set against a warm candid lifestyle photograph of a real business owner. The tension between the editorial black text block and the human, textured photography is the distinctive move — it humanises financial software and is worth stealing for any B2B fintech that wants to feel less corporate. Supporting blocks include a partner logos bar, funding stats and customer case studies.

7804a9cdd1d444b3a96ab8a824a1ee53.description: Pitch is a collaborative presentation and deck-building SaaS, now positioned around AI deck generation. The hero is a centred oversized geometric sans headline on a deep purple-to-violet gradient, with blurred presentation thumbnails layered behind it for depth and a lime-green sign-up button as the single high-chroma accent. The move worth stealing is the functional AI prompt box sitting centred at the bottom of the hero, turning the primary CTA into a working interactive demo. Below it, a large template gallery grid and a plan comparison block.

28c7b23ec3ef4bf9af23310a4ec37aa5.description: Planet of Lana is a cinematic indie puzzle-adventure game. The hero centers oversized, light-weight all-caps sans type over a cinematic video background in stark black-and-white. Its most distinctive move is the 'blueprint' framing: minimalist dashed-line geometric borders around the logo, buttons and platform icons that make the UI feel technical and intentional against the vast dark background.

334321b42d8a4db797690b3ea8eec629.description: makemeplay is the gaming arm of Paris interactive studio makemepulse, building WebGL games and playable brand experiences. Dark charcoal hero with a color-split wordmark (white plus lavender), oversized overlapping translucent circles and a lone circular Click me button as the only CTA. Below the fold, project thumbnails are embedded directly inside giant display type, turning the case gallery into typography; navigation is reduced to tiny corner links.

110fa5567add4325b8389775c770d8b5.description: The Galactic Marketplace inside Star Atlas — a Solana-based space MMO — where players buy and sell ships, crew, collectibles and resources from each other or from ATMTA on an order-book model, paying in ATLAS or USDC via a connected wallet (Phantom, Backpack). Strong reference for a dense trading/dashboard UI rather than a marketing page: deep charcoal and black base with a left nav rail and top global menu, vibrant teal, violet and gold accents encoding item rarity, and a bright yellow system notice bar for network status. Uses glassmorphism, subtle gradients and neon glows to mark active selections, with high-fidelity 3D ship renders slotted into modular cards. Runs a visible pre-alpha build badge. Good for studying rarity colour-coding and order-book layout at high information density.

2887b8e81d88802d854dc800f494b269.description: PlayerZero is an AI production-engineering platform whose agents build a living world model of a codebase to autopilot SRE, support triage and QA (customers include Verizon, Zuora, Georgia Pacific). Centred text-first hero on white: dark-grey type with a signature terracotta accent on the primary CTA, and the distinctive move is a large monospaced headline used as a code signal against clean sans nav and body, with an inline low-friction email capture instead of a button pair. Strong supporting blocks: a hard-hitting stats row (3 days to 15 minutes triage, 98% MTTR reduction, 84% fewer tickets), a delegated-questions ticket thread plus parallel simulation-run panels as product UI, and a four-step learning-loop process.

0162f5c2faf742f09e686da5b51956c7.description: Pluto is a corporate-card and AI spend-management fintech (UAE-rooted, with a US locale page) covering cashback cards, invoice and procurement automation and AI bookkeeping. Behind a country-selection modal the hero is a centred heavy large-scale headline on a deep teal/forest-green field with vibrant lime-green CTA buttons and an italic display treatment on the emphasis word; visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render). Content structure is a strong B2B SaaS reference: a spend-volume stat bar, alternating feature sections with product-UI screenshots, logo wall, testimonial quotes, an old-way/new-way comparison table, three-tier pricing with a free plan, FAQ and closing CTA.

3177b8e81d888033b8f9d029e457e45d.description: Poch Studio is a small Framer-built design studio (branding, web, packaging, 3D/VFX, motion) with a deliberately unserious voice. The hero is a surreal 3D scene on true black: oversized everyday objects, a pink plastic chair, a metallic die, a giant cucumber, inhabited by miniature human figures, mixed with halftone-patterned 2D elements and a hand-drawn lo-fi GET STARTED button against clean white sans type. The most useful block for a studio is the transparent productised pricing ladder: four named packages (Sprint $999, Start-Up $2000, The Identity $3000, Bombastic $6000+) with plain-English positioning lines like When your ass is on fire, plus add-ons priced individually. Other blocks: deep case studies with per-project image carousels (Avant-Garde Territory, Open Office, Trapeze, Crystal Car VFX, Modern Mayr Dilijan), a two-panel services split (Branding / Digital), an FAQ, and a package-preselect contact form. Strong reference for productised creative services and scale-play surrealism.

95b304667eec43dabcf6ea6aaa2c8c2d.description: Polestar is a Swedish electric performance car brand (Nasdaq: PSNY). The homepage hero is a full-bleed product shot of a black Polestar 3 staged on raw jagged marble/stone ledges, a strong textural contrast between polished vehicle and industrial stone, shot low for structural luxury. Palette is strictly monochromatic (stark white, cool grey, deep black); typography is Swiss-influenced sans with bold headings, tight leading and restrained outline CTAs (Discover with a stroke and arrow icon). Notable inner content: a model-switcher row of side-view car cards, and a sustainability block that uses paper-craft / cut-paper illustration (wind turbines, power lines, sun) to make life-cycle-assessment data feel tangible, a good reference for making dry technical data warm.

fea74efef5db4492898d65f5c2c56565.description: Polymer Workshop is a European maker of high-performance cycling equipment — carbon wheelsets, handlebars, rimsets and seatposts — selling direct via a Sanity-backed storefront. The hero is a dark, moody, high-contrast forest/trail photograph under a strictly monochrome scheme of pure blacks, charcoals and off-white text, with a heavy custom all-caps geometric wordmark centred and navigation pushed to the extreme top corners in widely-tracked technical sans. Worth stealing: nav links prefixed with plus signs (+SHOP, +SUPPORT) for a directory/codebase feel, brutalist minimalism that lets the imagery dominate, and a frosted-glass backdrop-blur cookie bar. Notable editorial extension: the "Machine Portrait" series profiling individual bike builds.

6b2ed980b84c49e8a1d617a98fcecc0d.description: Porn Week is a public-awareness and education campaign, with navigation split for different audiences (Parents Click Here, Facts, Tips). The design's whole argument is tonal: a heavy bold uppercase sans title on a light pink field, partially occluded by shiny yellow 3D balloon forms (rings, donuts) that float and rotate both in front of and behind the type to build real depth on a flat screen. Useful reference for handling a sensitive or provocative subject with playful, disarming visual language instead of clinical seriousness, and for using 3D objects to layer around a headline.

8eacf453379143bba50077a09cb7b437.description: Postevand is a sustainable beverage brand selling water in plant-based, eco-friendly cartons. Clean white, black and light grey with natural blue sky tones; bold oversized sans headers against minimal body copy. Notable: detailed exploded product diagrams that break down the packaging materials layer by layer and carry the sustainability argument visually, plus high-contrast layouts and generous white space. Stats block quantifies the environmental claim.

1d07b8e81d888046b26dd509360d3b41.description: Profluent uses generative AI to design new proteins and gene editors (OpenCRISPR, Profluent-E1); backed by partnerships with Eli Lilly and IDT. Site by Bunsen studio, built in Webflow. Split hero: an oversized statement line, "Grounded in nature, authored by AI", set against a scientific 3D point-cloud rendering of molecular structures, in a clinical but warm palette of mint, coral and deep forest green on white, with a monospaced font used for utility labels. Distinctive technique is turning hard biological data into stylised dot-grid artwork so a deep-science company still feels designed. Also has a floating pill announcement bar, a partnerships module, a press/news feed pulling NYT and Forbes, and a team block. Great reference for biotech and deep-tech AI branding.

0eee818302304655a073f194de80890a.description: Proof provides AI-powered sustainability business intelligence and compliance services for companies and investors. Stark white and black with electric lime accents and a clean minimalist sans. Video hero using expansive earth footage, glassmorphism on product icons, smooth parallax. Structurally useful: a process block explains the methodology before the product UI showcase, which suits a category where buyers need to trust the data before they care about the interface.

55332aef967642b786145769742def84.description: The saved marketing site is gone. propel.me now resolves to a bare PropellerAi SSO login portal: a single white card on an off-white field, brand blue and red logo, 'Use your full work email address' and a 'Sign in with Microsoft' button. No marketing copy, no product story, and none of the 3D, big-type, scrolltelling agriculture/manufacturing page that was originally saved. Kept for the record only.

970f2a9d711b460298f2f112c1153e33.description: Provider Store is a Sydney (Surry Hills) homewares retailer on Shopify, selling slow-made Japanese ceramics, candles, knives, kitchen tools and pantry goods since 2014. Editorial e-commerce styling: a muted organic palette of slate blue, charcoal, cream and warm coffee brown, high-contrast serif headlines against minimalist sans utility type, and extreme close-up texture photography (woven linen, knitwear, ceramics) that sells the tactile 'slow made' story. Notable blocks: a new-arrivals product rail, an 'Our Favourites' collection block with long-form category copy, a Journal with recipes and neighbourhood city guides, and a candle-making workshops block with dated sessions and a private-booking enquiry.

b779bee8edd8418896b54242573996fa.description: Prozora (Transparent Network) is Ukrainian fintech infrastructure for instant account-to-account payments made directly inside a user's own banking app, bypassing card rails ("Instant & secure account-to-account payments in your bank's app"). The hero is a light, airy illustration: soft-glow blue/cyan/violet gradient graphics with drifting confetti particles on white, set in a lightweight geometric sans. Immediately below the fold sits a partner-bank trust bar (altbank, city24, MTB Bank, Bank Pivdenny), which is the key credibility move for a payments product. Good reference for B2B fintech that stays light and friendly instead of defaulting to dark enterprise blue.

0bc136f9c5fb4e75822baa3bc232d542.description: Serhiy Prytula Charity Foundation, a major Ukrainian NGO funding military, humanitarian and education projects. Split hero pairs a bold geometric sans headline ("Invincible when united!") with abstract floating 3D cubes and a live fundraiser card, in a signature periwinkle-lavender accent over black and white. The whole page is a masterclass in charity transparency UI: a bento grid of rounded tiles at varying sizes, active fundraisers with collected-vs-goal progress bars and real-time funding stats, and military aid categories (drones, optics, communications) each showing hard impact metrics like units purchased. Also has a partner logo carousel and subtle glassmorphism on interactive elements. Useful whenever a nonprofit needs to prove accountability through data rather than appeals.

2887b8e81d888025a3b0dd942a6d0cc8.description: Purpose Talent is a New York executive-search and talent consultancy (founded 2020 by Andrew Blancato, ex-Kickstarter, Etsy, Casper). Webflow build with an asymmetric, illustration-driven hero: bold stacked display lettering ("Work / that / matters") on a textured cream ground, with loose hand-drawn character GIFs animating in the margins. Palette is cream, mustard yellow, purple and red accents on ink black, with a risograph-style grain overlay that gives it a tactile print feel. Craft details worth stealing: the hand-lettered headline doubling as the brand graphic, a live "New York | 9:41am" clock, and a 100% preloader counter. Also runs an infinite client-logo marquee and a numbered 01-04 services list.

b3a1766d916e45f786dacc603618a8b6.description: Product page for QIQI's "Go Deeper" clarifying shampoo, a professional haircare brand with a fashion-editorial tone. Atmospheric lifestyle hero on vivid magenta with the product name overlaid, then high-contrast black-and-white sections carrying maximalist type. The brand's distinctive zigzag translucent bottle silhouette is used as a recurring graphic device, and the SHOP NOW CTA is set in screen-filling type wrapped around the bottle. Best idea to steal: the similar-products block opens as minimalist vector line-art outlines of each bottle shape before resolving into a horizontal scroll of real products — an elegant way to show a range by silhouette. Asymmetric editorial layouts throughout.

16c7b8e81d888022babcca41cd8b9632.description: QuatreCentQuatre is a Montreal web agency (strategy, design, UX/UI, development, SEO, e-commerce, Craft CMS and Magento), bilingual FR/EN. The hero runs on an unusual deep terracotta ground with an ultra-light geometric sans headline and flat, thick-outlined illustrations given just enough perspective to sit forward off the background — an earthy, non-primary palette that reads mature rather than startup-bright. The move worth stealing is a conversational hero: instead of a single CTA it drops a "How can we help you?" selector with pill options straight into the first viewport, segmenting visitors by intent before they scroll. Inner pages split cleanly into Design & Brand Experience, Technology & Development and Digital Tools, with a projects index. Good reference for agency positioning that qualifies leads in the hero.

38017c5493d740a49a24dd50eb3e2ba2.description: Qude is a French creative audio agency in Toulouse doing podcast creation, production and distribution. Hero is oversized all-caps neo-grotesk type on matte black, with the brand name rebuilt at the bottom as massive geometric letter-blocks in coral, amber, cyan and green — a 'Scroll or play' prompt and a pulsing red dot on the 'Let's record' pill signal the audio industry without words. Notable: a client reference wall where each logo carries year + podcast count (Alpine F1 '5 Podcasts', Stade Toulousain '31 Podcasts') with an inline MP3 per client; a numbered Creation/Production/Diffusion process; a 'Nos métiers' team block where every role plays an audio clip; and a browser mic-recorder CTA letting visitors leave an actual voice message. Site by Pam (thisispam.com).

2147b8e81d88800980e5d8dc8f36d90f.description: A standalone SS25 lookbook microsite for Quechua (Decathlon's mountain-sports brand) — a scroll-driven digital editorial rather than a shop. It opens with a percentage preloader, then a grain-textured full-bleed alpine hero with a huge tight-kerned sans headline and a picture-in-picture video CTA; the palette is earthy (misty green, slate, tawny brown) on white with a cobalt accent. Standout blocks: geo-tagged chapter dividers with real GPS coordinates, an MH500 vs MH900 product toggle that swaps specs and imagery side by side, spec callouts (20,000 mm water column, weight in grams), shoppable model shots and a colourway swatch switcher. Strong reference for outdoor lookbooks, product A/B toggles and scroll storytelling.

d7ad4f01afef404fac97f5894249b481.description: Quipo is a digital loyalty and customer-communication app for local shops, covering loyalty programs, messaging and digital receipts. The hero centres a large colourful geometric logotype with a paper plane animating through the type, on a mint and pale-blue background accented in forest green, teal, coral and yellow. Steal-worthy: an emoji-integrated marquee scrolling business types (restaurant, bakery); a scrapbook feature layout where sticker-like assets (coffee cups, coins, bonus labels) float around oversized type on scroll; and a device mockup showcase pairing app UI with floating physical props (oranges, bread). Also runs an interactive smiley cursor and organic wavy section dividers.

b59fc97bda07442cae546ff87c51c13f.description: Quote Velocity is a US insurance customer-acquisition company (Boca Raton) running a programmatic marketplace that delivers high-intent consumers to carriers and brokerages. Hero mixes an ice-blue and navy palette with a high-contrast lime CTA, an oversized ultra-light sans headline ('Customer Acquisition Excellence') and a stylised 3D character walking over faint large-scale background letterforms, layered so the figure overlaps the type. Notable blocks: a numbered three-step service breakdown, a big stats row ($200M saved yearly, 100 clients, 200+ people, $6.5B in customer value) anchored by a running-character illustration with a separate cast-shadow layer, an office-map block with per-location counters, and a careers CTA. Good example of making a dry B2B lead-gen category feel premium and playful.

b2c4f3c209954c1ba41bb4acda756062.description: Railway is a cloud deployment platform for shipping apps without managing infrastructure. Dark mode built on deep charcoal and midnight purple with neon purple and pink accents, a geometric sans, and an illustrated night-sky hero with soft purple clouds behind a centred headline. Two techniques worth stealing: a continuous vertical line that threads sections together like a rail or circuit to pull the eye down the page, and small vendor icons (AWS, Heroku) placed next to feature headers to position the product against competitors without a word of copy. Feature blocks pair with dashboard mocks that read as live software rather than screenshots.

63090a0fc7c24e2f8ee01e16be0fa538.description: Rainforest is embedded payments infrastructure for software platforms. The hero is a clean split — left-aligned copy against a warm lifestyle photo of an actual payment being taken — in an eco-fintech palette of deep forest green, white and vibrant lime for CTAs. Worth stealing: a floating header contained in its own rounded card that separates nav from hero content; contextual photography that shows the "why" of the product in a relatable setting rather than abstract fintech imagery; and large corner radii across image and buttons to keep a payments brand approachable. A cookie banner sits over the fold on load.

16c7b8e81d8880319f76e1f65c7fa4aa.description: Ramp is a spend-management platform bundling corporate cards, expenses, bill pay, procurement, travel and banking, now marketed heavily around AI agents for finance teams. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) — three capture passes failed on renderer timeouts — but the markup shows a background-video hero (homepage-hero.webm) behind the headline "Time is money. Save both", an inline email capture as the primary CTA, and two live counters (share of US corporate payments processed by Ramp, agents at work today) that make the hero feel like a running system rather than a poster. Notable blocks: a customer logo bar where each logo carries its own savings stat (Notion $1M+ saved, Shopify, Perplexity), video case-study modules with named-customer quotes, and a large "We've got the receipts" testimonial wall of roughly 18 quotes with company logos.

50f704ffa35e4a0cb5c8a315f94f45cb.description: Groupe Randolph is a Québec board-game company running eight 'pubs ludiques' (gaming pubs) plus an online game shop and event/team-building animation. The root is not a normal homepage but a two-choice splash gateway that splits intent between the online boutique and the pubs, using large interactive cards on a light grey field, deep navy and vibrant red, and a tall condensed all-caps sans. The technique worth stealing is frame-breaking: 3D dice, game pieces and burgers overlap the card boundaries so the products appear to spill out, giving a flat layout tactile depth. Real content lives one level down at /boutique/ and /pubs/.

4e5f7c2e59084c0585b92cbb089a4718.description: Readymag is a no-code web design tool, and the homepage leads with proof instead of pitch: a massive tiled gallery of real projects fills the fold, with the headline and CTA sitting below it. A clean monochrome UI frame keeps the eclectic, experimental typography of the showcased sites as the only visual noise, punctuated by a safety-orange CTA. Worth stealing: the inverted hierarchy that builds desire through visual inspiration before making the ask, the gallery-as-social-proof pattern for any tool whose output is visual, and the pill-shaped nav and buttons that keep the chrome friendly and contemporary.

16d7b8e81d8880d79915e328b8994987.description: Redbrick Coffee is a specialty roaster in Canberra, Australia (blends, single origins, subscriptions, wholesale, home barista courses), running on Shopify. Site by GO:OD. Asymmetric split hero pairing an oversized vibrant-red serif headline ("For Coffee Drinkers") with a warm top-down photograph of the brew, which gives an ordinary coffee shop an editorial, high-end feel. Red and white with wood and parchment tones from the photography, geometric sans for nav against the serif display. Clean modular blocks below: named blend cards, a rotating single-origin rail, a subscription builder pitch (bag size, grind, frequency), a barista-course promo and a wholesale enquiry section. Good reference for DTC food and beverage that wants brand over discount.

2497b8e81d8880759013d36a05fbb9a6.description: Redo Media is a design, marketing and AI partner studio based in Pune, India, offering branding, web, product UX, AI apps and growth marketing. Visually the boldest kind of agency site: a dramatic deep-red and burnt-orange gradient hero with near-black shadows, classical Renaissance "Creation of Adam" hand imagery, a heavy film-grain / noise overlay, and an elegant high-contrast serif headline with a soft outer glow for legibility — a premium glow-text-on-textured-gradient look worth stealing. The hero also carries a live local-time widget ("9:51 AM PNQ, IND"). Notable segmentation block "Where are you in your journey?" (Zero to One / One to N / Quick Solutions) works as an unusual self-qualifying entry-point grid, plus a "Trusted by 60+ organizations" logo bar and a repeating scrolling manifesto marquee. Built in Framer.

7fde1794a84a45a7ae6cc54d2d7d5c2c.description: Red Sofa is a creative recruitment agency. The hero sets the brand name in a massive bold geometric sans that structurally frames a central portrait, over a warm pale yellow ground with high-contrast charcoal type and neutral photography. Worth stealing: using oversized type as an architectural frame around a photo rather than sitting beside it, and a consistent pill shape carried across nav, banner and buttons that keeps the whole UI cohesive. A good reference for a people-business brand that wants personality without losing structure. A cookie banner overlays the fold on load.

f6d571a3d40a4861b3f5c92a2370be2b.description: Reed, a digital design and development studio. The domain still resolves but returns a blank white viewport in a headless browser on repeated attempts with extended waits, with no visible loader or cookie gate. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) and the site may have been taken down or replaced, worth checking manually. Saved tags describe a dark, 3D, big-type scrolltelling site with heavy motion.

ab5e739e4fd0486ca86e660b5e963598.description: REFIRE is an international hydrogen-energy technology company (founded 2015) doing R&D, design, prototyping, testing and manufacturing of fuel-cell systems for mobility and power, plus superchargers and grid-support products. This is its brand microsite hosted by studio Cusp, positioned around zero-emission hydrogen-electric mobility. Visuals unverified: the page throws a client-side exception in a headless render (typical for heavy WebGL/motion sites) and returns no server-side copy, so hero type is left unset and no visual details are recorded. Worth re-checking manually in a real browser.

7424f49c90664305a4a94e025af75028.description: Reflect is a networked note-taking app, and the site runs a full dark-mode cosmic treatment — deep violets and obsidian, neon purple glows, subtle star-like particles for depth, and a bold high-contrast sans headline over an abstract 3D portal that resolves into the product interface. Worth stealing: the "glow-as-bridge" technique where a central atmospheric light source leads the eye directly from headline into the app UI, and soft UI integration that blurs the boundary between landing page background and product screenshot so the two read as one continuous surface rather than a pasted-in mockup.

3177b8e81d88804cb606ce8cae2b175b.description: ReflexAI is a conversation-performance platform for contact centres: AI roleplay simulations (Prepare) plus automated QA of 100% of conversations (Assure), born out of crisis-line work and now used by the VA, Trevor Project, Pearson, Block and Cash App. The design is calm-but-serious: off-white base, deep forest green and vivid lime accents, and a bold tightly-kerned serif headline that reads as a single graphic block. Best thing to steal is the metric treatment: slot-machine odometer digits that roll into place for results (33% communication improvement, 22% faster onboarding, total individuals trained), which makes dry numbers feel alive. Also has a dual scrolling logo wall, a tabbed product showcase with real UI screens, a case-study quote block with portrait, and a security/compliance section (SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, GDPR, ISO 27001) used as trust proof.

3177b8e81d8880729da6e5993afb3d6f.description: Reflow (Framer, $15M seed) is a workforce and workflow intelligence platform: a system of record that shows how enterprise work actually happens, where it drifts from SOPs, and where automation would pay back. The hero is quietly premium: warm oatmeal-beige ground, elegant high-contrast serif headline, a soft deep-shadow CTA that reads as physically pressable, and a ghosted low-opacity input field on the right hinting at the AI product without cluttering the minimalism; a funding announcement bar sits on top.
