Notable blocks: a simulated AI answer card (What should we fix first to speed things up?) that demos the product as copy, slot-machine number counters for unit-economics metrics (avg activity, utilization rate, handle time, cost per unit), an automation/impact priority table with runs, deviation and savings columns, a Work has changed / Operations hasn't kinetic statement, a $1.2M-saved case study, an investor logo bar and a compliance badge row. Very good reference for unusual stats blocks and dashboards rendered as marketing sections.

e041250cd09748c2b17fa4779e8c7e2d.description: Regrocery is a sustainability-minded grocery/food brand. The hero is a tactile product composition (crumpled paper, stone-flecked ceramic, soft petals) with oversized high-contrast serif 're_' typography tucked into the 3D scene so it sits behind some objects and in front of others for depth. A tight terracotta, blush and ochre monochrome palette keeps a complex arrangement cohesive and high-end.

79ee1d1b66cf4caf9fe796dfba18a81a.description: Rekorder Studios (music/recording studio site) no longer loads: two headless capture attempts both timed out on navigation with a blank page, so the domain resolves but serves nothing renderable. Treat as dead; no visual reference recoverable.

22c7b8e81d888090b7fddfee0b468167.description: Relato is an AI content-operations platform for marketing teams — agents that research, draft, fact-check and optimize inside a project workflow. Split hero: left-aligned bold geometric-sans headline on an off-white base with deep plum type and buttons; the right side carries a detailed vector illustration of a Research → Draft → Review → Published pipeline with floating UI cards and multiplayer cursors over fine wavy background lines, and a technical monospace face handles metadata labels. Steal-worthy blocks: a multi-row scrolling marquee of "agent pills" each tagged with the model behind it (Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1) and doubling as links into the agents page, a clean Without Relato / With Relato comparison table, an embedded live agent demo card, and a Today / Day 5 / Day 30 onboarding timeline. Strong case-study inner pages.

73d195fe03844bd28f083c943397809a.description: A marketing site for Remote, the global HR/EOR platform for hiring, managing and paying international employees and contractors, hosted on the domain of design studio Buro (madebyburo.com) — so it reads as the studio's build or concept work for Remote. Split hero with a large headline left and a high-fidelity product UI mockup right; clean white background, dark charcoal text, signature vibrant purple for accents and buttons, modern geometric sans. Worth stealing: a tabbed interactive demo inside the product showcase that swaps between platform modules without leaving the section, a bento grid of features, sticky sections that reveal content on scroll, and subtle entrance animations on individual UI components rather than whole blocks.

e1954cc681c44e90abd472fd919f5c3d.description: The saved design is gone. Resonant Link (wireless power for medical devices, EVs and phones) wound down operations after being acquired by Motive Companies in early 2025; resonant-link.com is now a black single-screen transition notice pointing medical enquiries to rlmedical.com and non-medical IP licensing to an operations address. What is there now is a split layout with big sans type on black, teal links and a floating exploded-view 3D render of the charging hardware in copper tones — that exploded-view device is the one thing still worth a look. The original light, flat, grid-based site no longer exists.

16c7b8e81d8880d982c6f7c12d6a97b2.description: Amici is a French restaurant group (Lesquin, Sophia-Antipolis, Meylan) built around shared plates, cocktails, afterwork, live DJ sets and open mic nights. The hero is pure typography: a high-contrast display serif statement centered on warm cream, everything set in one deep olive green, with thick checkerboard bands framing the top and bottom of the viewport like a bistro tablecloth — a cheap, very reusable way to give a type-only hero a strong frame. A keyword marquee (RENCARD, AFTERWORK, TAPAS FIESTA, LIVE DJ SET, OPEN MIC) runs along the bottom and repeats deeper down the page. Notable blocks: dense mosaic photo grids of food, bar and interiors, decorative stamp graphics and a custom cursor. Site by Beaucoup (beaucoup.studio).

60075208c00244319fdbc161636ac89a.description: Revenant is a Glasgow-based creative studio doing high-end CGI, VFX and animation; the page captured is the creative-executive showcase for Kevin McCrae. It is essentially one full-bleed showreel used as the interface — sci-fi environments, character animation and abstract motion play behind everything, with the reel doing the job a hero image and a case-study grid would normally split between. Palette is dark and cinematic (blacks, greys, warm golden highlights bleeding out of the footage). The typographic move is the one to steal: a bold stylised display serif set with aggressive overlapping and very tight tracking, with all navigation and contact links pinned to the extreme corners so nothing competes with the work.

68d0258aa7534c10af3e12a6022cf3db.description: Revolut is the London-based neobank and all-in-one finance app (75M+ customers across 40 markets) covering accounts, cards, savings, stock and crypto trading, eSIM plans and its AI assistant. The hero pairs an oversized tight-tracked "Banking & Beyond" headline in pale metallic silver with an emotive portrait on a deep blue gradient, layering the type behind the subject's head for depth and floating a glassmorphic balance card over the photo, with warm beige CTAs cutting the blue. Deeper down: autoplaying product-UI vignettes with tabbed switchers (Adventure/Wedding/Moving, Physical/Virtual cards), an awards badge strip, and a five-tier plan comparison. Note the site is geo-variable — this read is from the UK homepage.

3177b8e81d888064932ddb787235c25c.description: rh.design is the one-man studio site of Robin Holesinsky, a product designer and ex-founder selling subscription design to funded startups (from $4,995/mo). Off-white and black with an acid-lime accent, bold tight-set sans headlines, and a small product screenshot embedded inline inside the headline sentence. The hero doubles as a draggable canvas of work thumbnails ("Drag me") that turns the portfolio into a toy. It is a masterclass in conversion blocks for a solo/freelance offer: credibility stats (10+ years, 50+ projects, 100M users), client cards with outcome copy, transparent pricing with monthly/3-month toggle, and a three-way comparison table (in-house hire vs agency retainer vs founder-led partnership) that reframes price as savings. Also has case studies with metrics, a rich FAQ and a personal founder section.

3437b8e81d8880c4ac4cf92f7bbe4091.description: Rhetorich (by MySpeaker OY) is a human+AI coaching platform that trains lawyers to speak persuasively in courtrooms, negotiations and client meetings. Deep forest-green hero with an elegant serif headline ("Speak like you're worth it"), a painterly classical-portrait illustration instead of a photo, mint accent CTAs, and floating metric chips (Persuasion +26%, Credibility +31%). Notable blocks: score-card UI mockups (CLAPPS "Big 6" analysis), an impact stats band (1,000+ professionals trained, 92% more confident), three-tier pricing named Whisper/Orate/Resound, testimonial slider (Bayer, ABB, Lundbeck) and a long FAQ. Screenshot includes a small cookie banner at the bottom.

cf746ba1010d4fe4ba47a8630e090dda.description: Portfolio of Richard Ekwonye, a London-based creative developer and Design Engineer at Stripe specializing in web animation (site designed by Gil Huybrecht, developed by Richard). The hero is minimalist with a brutalist edge: a light-grey background, stark black type and a muted desaturated portrait, with a bold modern sans setting a large all-caps "CREATIVE DEVELOPER". Asymmetrical grid alignment, dramatic scale jumps and generous whitespace give it a high-end editorial feel, while the work itself is showcased through big images and subtle micro-interactions. A clean reference for restrained, typography-first engineer/designer portfolios.

3a37b8e81d88806f9bf2e477d69d50d0.description: Radian is a Dutch electric enduro motorcycle startup launching the EXR with a tool-free 30-second swappable 8.6 kWh battery, 70 hp / 1060 Nm, from EUR 14,450. The homepage opens on a full-bleed cinematic hero video plus a symmetrical head-on shot of the yellow-and-black bike against gunmetal, with a single high-saturation yellow used only on the product and the primary CTA. Worth stealing: a numbered "01/09" section indicator with sticky in-page chapter nav, a horizontal feature carousel, a parallax forest CTA scene built from layered tree and motor PNGs, and a limited-edition 01/50 counter. Strong inner pages: /exr/specs and the /pre-order configurator. Webflow build, site by UNCOMMON.

2be8eabce833470faf8d267f8875b1b4.description: Corporate home of Riot Games (League of Legends, VALORANT, TFT, Wild Rift, Arcane). The hero is a full-bleed piece of game key art — a Shadow Isles character in deep teal and obsidian with neon spectral cyan glows and metallic gold branding — paired with a chiselled 3D serif game logo and a clean sans for everything else. Techniques worth stealing: internal light sources inside a dark silhouette to create an instant focal point, atmospheric fog layers separating subject from background, and a single high-contrast cyan gradient CTA doing all the work. Below the hero it settles into a tiled grid of games and news. Useful reference for dark, art-led brand pages that still need a clear conversion path.

f586c6004c714d709c515004cf8eab52.description: Rive is an interactive design-and-animation engine — state machines, rigging and data binding, shipped natively to web, iOS, Android, Unity and Unreal. The site sells itself by running on its own product: a deep-black hero with a massive all-caps geometric sans headline, warm golden-amber CTA and a soft pulsing glow above the button, then an immediately following category grid where every tile is a live Rive animation rather than a static image. Also carries a customer logos bar (Spotify, Duolingo, Google, Disney), feature breakdowns and a comparison-flavoured pitch against After Effects/Lottie workflows. The best available reference for "show, don't tell" product marketing where the hero and gallery are the demo.

2147b8e81d88800dbd4ec324a6edbe63.description: Rivian is a US electric adventure-vehicle maker (R1T truck, R1S SUV, new R2). The homepage is a stack of full-bleed cinematic lifestyle photography — trucks on coastlines, motion-blurred road shots — with a translucent header and near-monochrome UI so the imagery stays dominant; a single warm amber accent carries the CTAs. Notable blocks: a tabbed feature switcher (Technology / Performance / Design), two parallax foreground-background layers driving the safety and charging sections, a 3D configurator entry point, an award badge module and a full-width brand video finale. Strong reference for automotive photo-led marketing pages and parallax layering.

cd3613a909e94b75b9266c7098aa0cfe.description: Roboto Entertainment is a game studio, and its site opens straight into an explorable real-time 3D environment rather than a static hero — a "Scroll to Look Around" prompt turns the fold into a 360-degree scene of warm sandstone architecture and foliage greens. Typography mixes a heavy wide custom sans headline with a monospaced font for technical UI details. Worth stealing: cinematic post-processing (chromatic aberration and lens bleed) that gives high-fidelity 3D a gritty filmic quality instead of a clean render look, and retro media-player controls folded into a modern UI for a tactile developer-tool feel that matches the world-building theme.

0e6b8d0b153c42af8ca05e9f33deda18.description: RocketAir is a remote-first design and strategy studio doing brand, product and motion ('Digital experiences that Win by Design'), with clients including Coursera, QED Investors, Software AG and Qlik. The hero is high-contrast black and white with a single lime-yellow 'Get in touch' button, massive sans headline in mixed weights, and a thin horizontal rule bridging disjointed text blocks to create flow across dramatic negative space. Two brand-voice details worth stealing: a cookie banner that breaks the fourth wall ('Oh look, another website...') and 'CHECK OUT THE HYPE' replacing a generic scroll cue. Below: a design reel video section, Brand/Product/Motion service tiles, a draggable client logos bar and case studies (NewLimit, Surf Internet, FocusVision).

8f667c1787634f4fb5d35b7529dbf4f4.description: Concept brand site (built in Webflow) for Rogue & Rosy, a startup making alcohol-infused ("boozy") all-natural fruit jam. The hero stages product jars amid floating fruit and liquid splashes on a high-energy monochrome red background, paired with neon-yellow accents, a bold condensed block sans, and an arched outlined display font. Notable blocks include a punchy zero-calorie / zero-fat / zero-carb stats row, an "As seen in" logo strip, a monthly-subscription CTA, and an Instagram gallery. Pop-art CTA buttons with hard offset shadows give it a tactile, retro-modern feel.

0ea453690ee348fb832b864e6a43f7db.description: Rollie Nation is an Australian-owned footwear brand (founded 2012 by designer Vince Lebon) selling ultra-lightweight shoes with memory-foam insoles across 11 countries, on Shopify. The homepage leads with a full-bleed lifestyle photo hero (Going Somewhere or Not, plus a Shop New CTA) in a neutral earthy palette of muted beiges and greys punctuated by a bold yellow element, set in a clean modern sans. Notable: a glassmorphic newsletter modal with a frosted-blur container and pill buttons, and a Shop by Category split-tile grid where each tile offers separate Women/Men entry links. Visuals only partly verified, the newsletter modal obscured part of the hero in both headless attempts.

88875c3e9a814504a67911e5b062e78d.description: Editorial site for Rose Family, a multi-generational Ukrainian restaurant group, presenting its three dining venues. Cream base, black type, warm earthy food and interior photography. High-contrast stylish serifs with heavy italics mixed against a modern sans. Techniques worth stealing: overlapping collage layouts, grain texture over imagery, vertical sticky navigation text, and smooth parallax transitions between venues. Good reference for hospitality brands that need each venue to feel distinct inside one parent identity.

22c7b8e81d888075b19dfc7e4bd7bb73.description: rubustech.io now 301-redirects to rucoria.com — a rebrand of the same company (Rubus became Rucoria, announced alongside NOK 21M in funding), not a parked page or a different business. Rucoria is Nordic and European residential-construction software (flatfinder, home customization, digital handover, warranty handling) used by Peab, Nordr, OBOS and Veidekke. Visually it is warm and editorial rather than cold SaaS: a cream / off-white ground, a heavyweight black sans headline ("Build as one, get more done.") with a single-word coral-red colour-split highlight, deep-burgundy structural bands and faint grid rules. Notable blocks: a monochrome client logo bar, an oversized stats block (40,000 homes / 1,000 projects / 2,500 companies) on a dark shape-patterned panel, and a rich testimonial carousel with a portrait plus company logo per quote. Multilingual (EN / NO / DE / SV).

34e7b8e81d88807cb06ed55679062ec3.description: Runlayer is an enterprise AI control plane: MCP gateway, shadow-AI discovery, agent governance and spend monitoring ($30M Series A from Felicis and Khosla). Grayscale, dev-tool aesthetic: bold geometric sans headline "Go all in on AI" over vertical data-stream line patterns, monospace labels and floating contextual UI pins ("prompt injections blocked") that demo product value right in the hero. Strong customer-logo bar (Gusto, PagerDuty, dbt Labs), pull-quote testimonials from Cursor and the MCP co-creator, case-study cards, FAQ, and an "AI summary" footer block linking to Claude/ChatGPT/Perplexity — a novel AEO pattern.

5b22fc64dc464ba4933efab2eec06037.description: The domain now serves a different site than the one saved here: runway.com is currently an FP&A / financial planning platform, not the travel-and-logistics-flavoured 3D scrolltelling site the original Travel & Hospitality tags describe. Current target: a big-type hero centred over an airy light grey-blue gradient with charcoal text and a bold amber CTA reading "Talk to a human", plus the "peek" effect showing the top edge of the app interface at the fold. Worth stealing: the human-CTA in high-contrast amber as a warm counter to standard automated SaaS flows. Old tags left intact — worth re-checking whether the saved reference still exists elsewhere.

7ba881bc4e8f43c993b7f9f350bc06c1.description: South African wine estate in Franschhoek founded in 1997 by Dr Anton Rupert and Baron Edmond de Rothschild, built around a deliberately narrow range of three wines. The homepage is gated by a full-screen age verification laid over a darkened aerial vineyard photograph, with high-contrast serif and spaced uppercase lettering in gold and white against moody greens and greys, and a text link instead of a button for the accept action. Copy is heavily editorial and heritage-led ("A meeting of Two Worlds", "The simplicity of Three"), with commerce split onto a shop subdomain. Beyond the gate visuals are unverified (loader/gate in headless render).

057293fcfe7a437d924009c3540e0379.description: Redirected: the domain no longer serves the Financial Services product originally saved. It now hosts "Safe-Haven Online Directory", a generic link directory for wellness, healing and personal-growth resources, built around a submit-your-site CTA on a soft pastel gradient, a vertical feed of latest submissions with thumbnails, a social-links sidebar and a long SEO about section. Standard directory template, none of the original design value remains.

e55d22c2bf204acebc2350943e0e8135.description: Sakharov.space is a nine-chapter digital biography of physicist and dissident Andrei Sakharov; chapter 1 covers family, childhood and youth, 1921–1940. Built as editorial Swiss design: high-contrast black, white and grey, a huge minimalist sans headline deliberately broken across lines, vertical sidebar branding running up the edge, thin horizontal rules and asymmetric blocks. The standout move is a numbered chapter timeline (01–05) that works as both index and navigation, with archival photography carrying the narrative. Strong reference for museum, archive and memorial storytelling.

31577292adb14d8180f710fc4dd7d32a.description: Sakuga is a Webflow HTML website template aimed at startups, apps, SaaS and tech products (by Maxim W.), sold on the Webflow marketplace with a built-in CMS blog and motion throughout. The hero is asymmetrical, a left-aligned type stack beside a large abstract graphic built from overlapping translucent circles, soft gradients and glassmorphism. A warm orange/yellow/amber palette sits on clean white with charcoal text and high-contrast CTA buttons, plus generous whitespace. A tidy example of modern SaaS template styling: bold geometric headline, gradient blob art, and airy layout.

2147b8e81d88804a916ddac67bce6d1e.description: Sana (Sana Labs, Stockholm) sells a no-code enterprise AI-agent platform grounded in company knowledge; this is the AI-agents product page. Typographic-led dark hero — near-black base, high-contrast serif headline with an italic emphasis, geometric sans for UI text, an electric-purple pill CTA, and floating product-UI cards on a blurred backdrop for Z-axis depth. Strong reference for AI/SaaS marketing: a rotating results block pairing an anonymised customer sentence with a hard number (62% time savings, 10h/week saved), autoplaying in-page product videos with a Replay control and tabbed captions, a phone-frame mockup for the meetings feature, and an illustrated three-part RAG/reasoning explainer.

5c6842d413dc46d1907c323c049e43da.description: Sapiens is UI8's free character-builder microsite for their modular illustration library — the whole page IS the product. Instead of a marketing hero it drops you straight into a configurator: a large character sits centred inside a soft circular mask on an off-white ground, with peripheral icon rails for activity, gender and style that swap body parts instantly. Palette is warm red, sunny yellow and ochre; typography is a light functional sans used only for UI labels. The stippled grain shading on flat shapes is the signature technique worth stealing. A strong reference for turning a downloadable asset pack into a playable demo that sells itself, plus a lesson in making the hero interactive rather than decorative.

352d736b6cbf46b0bc1e0f444b5e232e.description: Sapori e Natura di Calabria is an Italian artisan-food e-commerce selling almond-based sweets: amaretti (classic, pistachio, clementine & rum) and mandorlotti, made from 100% Italian cold-processed almonds. Site by WOW Web, featured on CSS Design Awards. Structure is a product-led shop with category and product pages built around ingredient and provenance storytelling. Visuals unverified (the headless renderer failed repeatedly on this site), so hero type is left unset and no visual details are invented; the existing tags describe a monochrome, pastel, big-type scrolltelling layout with visible borders.

ff449456f9794e0c986ebe22c01fc617.description: Portfolio of Sarah Fatmi, a Montréal-based illustrator and designer working in editorial, branding, textile design and typography. Built as a flamboyant horizontal-scrolling one-pager: the hero is a tri-tone lavender / deep-black / off-white composition with custom chunky hand-drawn display lettering (typeface “Moche” by the Pépite collective), and black cloud-shaped blobs layered both behind and in front of the letters to fake three-dimensional depth inside a flat 2D layout. A hard horizon split separates the purple sky from the black ground and gives the irregular lettering structure, while a central SCROLL badge signals the sideways navigation. The rest of the page is an illustrated scenery-driven gallery of client work. Designed and coded by Sarah Fatmi with Michaël Garcia.

2497b8e81d888012855fe310ce53173b.description: SayBriefly is a Mac app for freelancers and studios that turns meetings, emails, Slack and Figma comments into locked briefs, tasks and projects, then flags scope creep against the agreed brief. Centred hero on a warm cream ground with deep forest-green headline type and vibrant yellow marker-highlighter emphasis, heavy sans headline paired with monospaced nav and tags. Hand-drawn green doodles frame the content and SVG section titles are used as artwork, giving it a charming lo-fi analog-meets-utility feel aimed squarely at a design audience. Best blocks to steal: a horizontally scrollable comparison table against Granola, Otter and Fireflies, and a stats row framed in money saved ("$3,000+ billable protected", 6 hrs/week). Site by HustleJar.

33f4d481d0354a86a123f826e1b3fbd0.description: Scale AI — data labelling and evaluation infrastructure for frontier AI models, positioned around "Reliable AI for the world's most important decisions". The domain resolves and the site is live, but it served an ERROR 500 page on two consecutive headless renders, so only the error state, sitemap footer and closing brand-headline block were observable: dark forest-green and black theme, large-radius rounded content containers, oversized bold sans branding type. Visuals unverified (server error in headless render) — worth re-capturing on a later pass.

4ce5eb1b4ba4443584fd64cc35fcff06.description: UPROCK is a Russian-language online school for UX/UI, web, product and graphic designers, founded by design director Evgeny Kuzmin, teaching in a design-studio-internship format with real client projects and job placement. The hero is high-contrast monochrome black and white with bold geometric sans headlines centred for impact, spiked by an electric blue and purple brutalist promo bar pinned above a minimalist header, plus a floating white pill sub-nav that separates resource links from the main menu; stylised high-contrast cut-out portraits of instructors give it a personal-brand feel. The dense conversion landings at /uxui, /ultimate, /product-design and /graphic-design are the strongest inner pages.

2cd7b8e81d8880d5be49c77a4fa5b3dd.description: Scout AI builds a foundation model for defense robotics: a vision-language-action model that takes live camera feeds plus text prompts and outputs robot actions, with secure over-the-air model deployment. The site sells seriousness. A cinematic, full-bleed environmental photograph puts the robot in its actual operating context (forest, low light) instead of on a studio pedestal, with a militaristic palette of deep forest green, bark brown and charcoal against high-contrast white. Typography pairs a bold sans headline with a wide-tracked uppercase technical sans for navigation. Worth stealing: the slim announcement bar above the fold used for funding/traction news as instant credibility, and the frosted semi-transparent header that lets the imagery stay full-bleed while keeping the nav legible. Clean, restrained deep-tech reference with visible borders and flat UI.

17a7b8e81d88807bb51cfe36b2ac46d6.description: Scout Motors is Volkswagen Group's revival of the original American Scout SUV, launching the electric Traveler SUV and Terra truck (reservations open, from under $60,000, production targeted 2027). Astro build. Hero is cinematic golden-hour product photography and video of both vehicles in a desert landscape, with the headline anchored bottom-left and the navigation broken into separate rounded modules that float as distinct segments rather than a single bar. Warm amber, ochre and bronze earth tones. Standout blocks: a 1961 heritage timeline that sells the brand's lineage, a twelve-frame "viewfinder" gallery, a reveal-event video section, and a two-card product duo. Excellent reference for automotive and heritage-relaunch storytelling.

94fe8562c5674d76a26ffe9b12a826ba.description: Promo site for the Rossinavi SeaCat, a hybrid-electric catamaran superyacht, tagline "New Superslight Generation". Entry is a black minimal splash with the SEACAT logotype in a futuristic geometric sans, high-contrast dark UI with an orange accent, gated behind a cookie consent wall. The main WebGL experience throws a client-side exception in a headless render, so visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) beyond the splash. Worth revisiting in a real browser for the 3D yacht scrolltelling.

c0ca0a5b85464563a8d15722d8ab926e.description: Secrid is a Dutch wallet maker (since 1995) selling RFID-protected aluminium card protectors and leather wallets ethically made in Holland. The hero is a lived-in angled product shot of the Envelope Wallet with cards and coins spilling out, set on a warm tan background tonally matched to the cognac leather for an expensive, cohesive look; a bold condensed all-caps headline pairs with a small italic serif, plus solid-white primary and ghost secondary CTAs. Notable blocks: an editorial three-up 'Wallet makers since 1995 / Crafted to last / Responsibly made in Europe' band split by thin vertical rules, wallet category cards segmented by capacity (Essential Carry vs Expanded Carry), an engraving customization feature block with phone mockup, and an 'Our icons' product row.

0127431e88804464862bcb7cf7c8b2f0.description: Seed sells DS-01, a clinically studied synbiotic (24 probiotic strains plus a pomegranate-derived prebiotic) sold on subscription in a refillable glass jar. The hero is a macro product shot rendered against deep forest green with off-white and black, giving a premium biotech rather than wellness-fluff feel, set in a clean minimal sans that reads as clinical authority. The conversion pattern is the thing to steal: review count as social proof sitting immediately beside benefit-driven bullet points and the CTA, so proof, promise and action live in one eyeline. Deeper pages lean hard on trial data, strain-by-strain science, delivery-technology explainers and FAQ. Best reference in the base for science-led DTC health products.

a84f91cebc3942f991843af147d50b02.description: Seedlip is the Diageo-owned pioneer of distilled non-alcoholic spirits (Spice 94, Garden 108, Grove 42), positioned around "what to drink when you're not drinking". The homepage runs a short declarative headline hero into an icon-driven benefits row (no sugar / all the flavor / no calories), a product carousel of botanical-pedestal bottle shots, an awards logo strip, a recipes grid, a founder-story block and newsletter capture. Localised per region on a Contentful-backed stack with an AI concierge widget. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) — a cookie banner plus a discount modal blocked the capture, so hero treatment is inferred from HTML only.

50f2a8909c3246bda71539f66c2e5e5d.description: Potion (sendpotion.com) is a SaaS product with a clean, minimal marketing site. The big-type hero sits on white with a single vibrant purple accent, a floating pill-shaped navbar for an app-like feel, and a stylized underline that draws focus to the key use case. Generous whitespace and tight-tracked geometric sans give it a premium, breathable aesthetic.

34e7b8e81d8880d4b2d1e0511f283ce4.description: Shader is a Swedish creative development studio (Norrköping) building interactive 3D, WebGL and AI experiences for brands and agencies worldwide. Homepage is a playful scroll-driven experience: "A Creative Development Studio, Plugged into the Future" hero, a project carousel of "closed deals", long tongue-in-cheek corporate-speak manifesto ("We don't troubleshoot printers", "send a fax") and contact block. Screenshot currently shows a blank/loading frame — the WebGL scene does not render in headless capture, so no visual claims beyond page copy. Worth revisiting in a real browser for the 3D work.

c3e3c3b43dcb4001b341fe3b779244ff.description: ShaderGradient — a tool for animated shader gradients that ship as live components in Framer and as exportable visuals via a Figma plugin. Deep black base with white type and an orange-red accent button; large bold serif titles against clean sans secondary text, and a floating glassmorphism dock navigation pinned at the bottom. The page sells the product by showing it: sections demo the gradients running inside browser mockups, inside interactive UI components with a colour palette tool and hex codes, and inside the actual Figma plugin panel with its export settings (range, pixel density, frame rate). Closes on a centred animated gradient block asking "What makes this natural movement?". Good reference for a tool site that demos rather than describes.

184e3b97edff46128f42b4bdfc2f94b6.description: Shift Nudge is Matt D. Smith's (MDS) professional interface-design training program for working designers — a $1997/yr membership covering 8 modules, live workshops and a year of critiques. The hero is dark-mode and typography-led: near-black canvas, white type, and a single magenta accent reserved exclusively for CTAs and directional arrows, with ghosted low-contrast geometric shapes sitting behind an asymmetrically offset headline. Its standout trick is a live countdown timer to the next training baked straight into the hero for functional urgency. Notable blocks: a logos bar (OpenAI, Figma, Google, Netflix, Pentagram, Apple), dense scrolling testimonial cards sourced from real LinkedIn/X posts, a four-up stats row (8+ weeks / 5+ hrs per week / 8 modules / 1 year of critiques), a framework-and-method breakdown, founder section and accordion FAQ.

16d7b8e81d8880859d19ffdddb3c26c0.description: Shift Robotics sells Moonwalkers, AI-powered wheeled footwear that lets you walk at running speed (400W drivetrain, up to 7mph; $999 Aero and $1,399 8-wheel original), a TIME Best Invention. Shopify; site by IDOL. Hero is a full-bleed lifestyle video with centred big type over a muted ochre and tan grade, plus a small persistent "Watch video" thumbnail pinned bottom-right that invites deeper engagement without cluttering the frame. Best blocks: a numbered scroll-through story sequence (1/5 Stay active, Be social, Trailblazing tech...) where each step swaps the background video, a press-quote marquee cycling TODAY, The Verge, WIRED, The Guardian, TIME and Reuters, a community UGC testimonial wall, and an app/ShiftAI section. Strong reference for consumer hardware that has to explain an unfamiliar product.

16282c02749e4605a5d22ac33e2fbfee.description: Shine is a French neobank for freelancers and small businesses, offering online business accounts and e-invoicing. The hero is deliberately minimal: an oversized high-contrast serif headline does all the work, with no product shot and a lot of whitespace, so the €0/month price point becomes the unmistakable focal point. Palette is deep forest green, white and a periwinkle-blue pop; serif headlines over sans nav give it an established, almost editorial authority rather than the usual playful fintech look. Good reference for how a challenger brand can signal trust through restraint instead of illustration.

3177b8e81d8880eca218fb80f567692b.description: Shopify Editions Winter '26, the RenAIssance edition, is Shopify's biannual product-release microsite shipping 150+ AI features (proactive Sidekick, agentic storefronts that place products inside ChatGPT and Perplexity, natural-language store editing, 2048 product variants). The concept is an art-history gag played straight: the hero is a digital collage of Renaissance painting and modern street culture, classical figures wearing sneakers and holding takeout coffee, in muted olive, cream and terracotta with high-visibility neon pink, under a high-contrast serif headline with a stylised italic ai ligature. The hero's centre is given over to a functional table of contents rather than a CTA, framed by a fine geometric grid that keeps the busy artwork readable. Notable blocks: a chaptered release index, feature detail sections with product UI, and heavy motion/scrolltelling throughout. Best-in-class reference for release-notes-as-campaign and anachronistic collage art direction.

ae01c68310fb4a49a9d64fb0897b3669.description: The official MrBeast merch store on Shopify (canonical 301 to mrbeast.store, a domain rename rather than a different site), selling youth and adult apparel, toys, school supplies and Feastables. The hero is a hybrid product-shot/big-type Back to School Clone Collection lockup with a dynamic angled product arrangement over layered background textures (diagonal stripes, topographic lines), in high-contrast black and white with electric cyan and hot-pink accents and a bold wide futuristic sans. The standout reference block is the philanthropy stats section: three enormous raw un-abbreviated counters (55,824,283 Pounds of Food / 46,520,235 Meals Delivered / 8,186,988 Individuals Fed) used as a giving-back proof device instead of the usual rounded metrics.

f94b37d728a24839a2163eb1e339307a.description: Sikha is a professional haircare brand selling colour, shampoos, masks and styling products. The hero pairs high-impact photography of a model with neon pink hair against oversized bold sans headlines and a split CTA (Discover more / Watch video), in a youthful palette of neon pink, deep purple, lime and white. Notable blocks: colour-coded category cards that use full-bleed imagery to separate Hair Color, Hair Care and Styling; a sustainability block that leans on large type and certification iconography for vegan and cruelty-free claims; a featured-products slider with from-pricing; and a horizontal value-prop ribbon for shipping, international availability and free samples. Solid reference for colour-blocking as an e-commerce navigation device.

22c7b8e81d888050a3aad86081a08652.description: Silna Health is a care-readiness platform automating prior authorizations, benefit checks and insurance monitoring for US healthcare providers. Calm, premium hero: white ground, a centered eyebrow leading into a high-contrast elegant serif headline ("Make care your primary focus."), sans subcopy and an eggplant CTA, with a soft pink-and-lavender radial aura glow rising from the base to frame the composition. Floating price-tag cards ($35.00 → $12.00) animate the cost-reduction story without showing a screenshot. The serif-headline plus geometric-sans-body pairing is the distinctive move — trustworthy and medical-appropriate rather than generic SaaS. Below: a provider logo bar, a G2 badge, a scale stat line (1,000+ payors, 50 states, 150k+ patients), a three-function feature block and a dreamy "Taking care of healthcare" cloud illustration section with icon-inline sentences.

ecec6a67d2cd40e8bce54ba348204b13.description: Silver Oak Cellars is the Napa Valley and Alexander Valley Cabernet Sauvignon house founded in 1972, known for ageing exclusively in 100% American oak and for LEED Platinum wineries. The site is a Shopify DTC build whose hero is a full-bleed autoplay video announcing the 2025 Sauvignon Blanc, its first white in 54 years, followed by paired bottle-on-landscape product cards for the two Cabernets, Experience/Reserve visit blocks, a second video block for the origin story, and gifting and events tiles. Deep inner content at /pages/american-oak, /pages/winemaking and /pages/sustainability. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) — cookie banner plus signup/age modal blocked the capture.

f858fc1f25c345cf96a95731d9bec5e7.description: Silversquare runs coworking and flexible workspaces across Brussels, Louvain-la-Neuve, Liège, Antwerp, Zaventem and Luxembourg — 12+ years, 2000+ members, furnished offices and hot desks with 24/7 access, positioned as spaces “imagined by artists” to give workspace extra soul. The hero is typographic and asymmetric: black-and-white base with a muted salmon-pink block, and a heavy all-caps sans headline (“The most exciting square meters in town”) sized for impact. Its signature move is a massive solid geometric “SQ” element that carries the branding as a structural block rather than a logo in a corner. Good reference for a multi-location real-estate site: the strongest inner pages are the per-location coworking pages (European Quarter, Brussels Central, Kanal, Delta University, Bailli-Châtelain), each sold as its own neighbourhood story across NL/FR/EN.

000964a4bca84b41a86027bd59ab79ae.description: Portfolio of Silvia Sguotti, a Bologna-based art director, graphic designer and illustrator (14+ years, CSS Design Awards). The hero is a monochrome editorial split layout structured by sharp horizontal and vertical grid lines, with a high-contrast serif name overlapping the boundaries and a clean sans for secondary details; a right-hand 'Passion is the point' manifesto CTA anchors it. Reference for grid-driven, type-forward designer portfolios in black and white.

16c7b8e81d888044995cec1af7e2f3c7.description: sites.research.google is not one marketing site but Google Research's host for editorial project microsites; the strongest page here is the Language Inclusion site (/languages) about extending Google AI to thousands of under-represented languages. Its hero is a full-bleed cinematic video montage of cities and faces under a legibility scrim, with a large Google Sans headline ("More languages. Fewer barriers.") on tight leading and a single Google-blue "Watch video" CTA against otherwise transparent navigation. Notable blocks: a horizontally scrolling five-step model pipeline (collecting data → pre-processing → training → testing → rollout) with paired grey/blue abstract icons, three documentary case studies (India / Project Vaani, New York / AAVE, Ghana / Waxal) each with photo galleries and researcher pull-quotes, a leadership quote, a research-papers list and an FAQ. Worth cataloguing at the /languages URL rather than the bare host.

41c02643e1bc4d048b340ce88154851e.description: SIXMOREVODKA (SMV) is a Berlin concept-art and illustration studio working on major games and entertainment franchises (Riot Games, Warner Bros Games, Marvel, Hasbro, Guerrilla Games) and publishing its own tabletop RPG IP. The hero is aggressive editorial typography: an ultra-bold, vertically stretched condensed sans at screen-filling scale in charcoal and safety orange, layered over central sketches, with secondary copy set upside down and a subtle grain that gives the digital layout a print feel. Framed by a Bukowski quote ('IT BEGAN AS A MISTAKE' / 'FAMOUS FOR NOTHING'), the site splits work into 'Famous Work' and 'Not So Famous Work', with 'WE DRAW.' marquees between. Site by Spatzek Studio.

67be0960ebad4935a61054c3d2f174b7.description: Slite is a team knowledge base / docs tool. The hero is warm and restrained — off-white ground, charcoal type, a single vibrant coral CTA, and a bold tight-kerned sans headline. Worth stealing: compliance badges (SOC 2, GDPR) placed directly adjacent to the CTA so trust lands at the exact moment of conversion rather than buried in the footer; a hand-drawn circle around "Verified" that breaks the digital grid with a human mark; and the "peek" effect where the product mockup bleeds up into the hero from below to create continuity and pull the scroll.

86517b0b6685417db90935ff7d938717.description: Smarkia is a Spanish cloud platform for intelligent energy management: real-time consumption monitoring, inefficiency detection and cost optimisation. The hero pairs big bold sans with a floating dashboard mockup that gives instant proof of the interface without cluttering the screen. Palette is deep forest green and white with a high-contrast lime CTA. The headline plays on "(r)evoluciona" with a bracketed prefix, a small copy trick worth keeping for bilingual or wordplay-friendly markets. Clean reference for energy and industrial SaaS that needs to look serious and modern at once.

4446782dcf3c4daf831cab7be19f243a.description: Smart Bunkers is a Ukrainian manufacturer of autonomous bomb shelters and bunkers, sold in Family, Public and Military configurations. The site is built as one long scroll-driven 3D narrative: the hero is a top-down aerial 3D view of a residential backyard that pans and re-angles as you scroll to show the bunker being lowered into the ground. Palette is black and charcoal with electric blue and vibrant yellow; headings use a bold condensed sans that reads industrial and urgent. Worth stealing: the delivery-truck animation that drives across the screen as a literal scroll progress indicator, the specs presented as stat callouts ('2+ months of autonomous living'), a Process block for install/delivery, an interior render gallery per model, and a lead-gen CTA anchored by a 3D container model.

3d1d4c0850e04f6895dbc8363b8a8989.description: Web3 sneaker community and NFT collection, site by Antinomy Labs. Red-white-black hero: aggressive condensed uppercase type with a 3D sneaker character sandwiched between the nav and the giant background title (z-depth layering); duplicated-word text animations, marquee gallery of illustrated characters, project cards (Blast app, sneaker.cloud), core team grid. Strong ref for streetwear energy, depth-layered type heroes and web3 brand pages. Still live despite NFT-era origin.

2a240eb21d6243b9bcae5abc36cc4d50.description: SOGAI is an editorial web experience about generative AI in arts and culture by freelance creative developer Huy NG. It reinterprets iconic artworks through Midjourney and DALL-E 3 prompts and walks through case studies of AI art events and controversies (copyright, authenticity, misinformation). Saved tags describe a dark, big-type scrolltelling piece. Visuals unverified: the WebGL-heavy page repeatedly crashed the headless renderer.

0ad616b3a43b4cae949bcbf2306701ba.description: The domain still responds but sits behind an aggressive security layer: headless requests are met with a Cloudflare "Sorry, you have been blocked — you are unable to access solace-store.com" page, and the store no longer surfaces in search results under this name, so it may have been retired or renamed. Visuals unverified (bot block in headless render); nothing about the original design could be confirmed. Worth re-checking manually from a normal browser before relying on this record.

f6a0218c3ecf4dcd94b25f58d1feea96.description: Somefolk — portfolio site of design director Jason Harvey, offering branding, web design + dev and content creation across London, Bangkok and Los Angeles. The hero is an immersive 3D scene: a rotating metallic object behind the "SF'26" wordmark, which scales dramatically as you scroll. High-contrast monochrome punctuated later by deep amber and gold imagery, mixing a bold modern sans for branding with an elegant high-contrast serif for editorial copy. Techniques worth stealing: scroll-triggered type scaling, heavily layered composition (letterforms overlapping video and imagery), a section anchored by one massive letter "S", and a clean grid of Awwwards / GSAP / FWA / CSSDA accolades. Closes on "Quality digital goods (for sale)" in screen-scale type.

c208d7662a1d45489c0502384cd4b23e.description: Somvai is a smart alarm / sleep-tech device brand ("Unlock Perfect Rest – a new kind of smart alarm"). The hero is a soft, warm product shot: the device rendered in shallow depth of field with a glowing wood-and-cream lighting setup that sells calm rather than tech specs, palette of beige, tan, cream and natural wood, lowercase geometric sans wordmark. Small site (About / Contact), so the value is the art direction: how a hardware product can be lit and framed as a lifestyle object, and how a fully warm pastel palette can still read premium in the health/sleep category.

3a37b8e81d8880dca558cceb35eca655.description: Son Daven is a Ukrainian design resort aparthotel in Yaremche, Carpathians, sold as an investment project by developer blago — 304 apartments across two sections marketed on guaranteed 10% annual returns. Hero is a moody, low-key architectural photograph in desaturated earth tones (deep charcoal, warm mocha, muted bronze) with a heavy fringe-textured display logotype against wide-spaced geometric sans UI text and thin-stroke bordered buttons. Distinctive techniques: a branded video preloader with a percentage counter, an interactive Yaremche map with walking-time hotspots, a summer/winter toggle, drag-to-slide apartment galleries with floorplan SVGs, an animated financial-indicators block and a construction-progress timeline. Bilingual EN/UA.

16c7b8e81d8880d68c1dcfdbfe5eb441.description: Sound Ethics is a Hollywood-based research lab and advocacy org for ethical AI in music: neural fingerprinting to detect copyrighted material in AI output, AI-rights standards, and a "Labs to Legends" university program with UCLA, NYU and UC Irvine. The hero is a cyber-noir big-type/photo hybrid — an ultra-bold condensed industrial sans SOUND ETHICS layered over a moody spotlit stage photograph, with an elegant high-contrast serif sub-line creating deliberate brutalist-versus-classical tension, on near-black with electric-lime accents. The steal-worthy part is the analog-music-artifact UI: tilted tape-strip CTAs, ripped-sticker news cards, barcodes, "guaranteed genuine" stamps, and a vinyl Side A / Side B record-player module that shuffles through the org's principles. Numbered solution cards, a standards section and an updates feed round it out. Site by Some Folk (SF.CO).

b69703271de449798fcb3f8ac694eed6.description: Speedy is a fintech/payments product. The dark hero layers floating glassmorphic UI cards over a central abstract 3D sculpture for strong dimensionality, on a grainy dark gradient with tactile texture. A rotated 'Awards & Certifications' sidebar breaks the standard horizontal grid, and international flags signal global coverage. Bold, tight-set sans reinforces the modern fintech aesthetic. Product UI and feature blocks follow below.

3de47ab7bb0745b98c8f4ea964deb26b.description: Squarespace, the website builder and e-commerce platform. Cinematic video hero (basketball silhouettes) under big centred type, aspirational rather than showing the software, held in monochrome so colour only enters through customer site mockups. Best blocks to steal: an animated stats bar counting up 14M+ entrepreneurs, $36B+ earned, 200+ countries; a tabbed service carousel (Services, Online Store, Invoicing) that swaps mockup and copy so a huge product surface fits a compact interactive space; an AI onboarding split offering "Build with AI" or "Browse templates" to serve both hands-on and hands-off users; an inline domain search bar; and a closing CTA anchored by an expanding dot-sphere graphic. Throughout it uses layered floating UI mockups over photography instead of dry screenshots.

d4c8e662b499410c9c39a8c558c13c60.description: stan.vision is a UI/UX and Webflow agency focused on SaaS products. Big-type hero on dark with Clutch, Awwwards and Webflow Partner badges as immediate social proof, then the page transitions dark-to-light as you scroll into the work. Strongest reference material for agency positioning: a numbered 01-05 service breakdown that defines the offer in minimal sections, data-driven case studies pairing high-fidelity product shots with hard outcome metrics surfaced right in the portfolio feed ("78% more time spent on pages", funding raised), and a floating awards section where badges react to interaction. Uses glassmorphic 3D renders to visualise abstract services like UX strategy and discovery, plus a sticky nav that inverts against the background.

d7e31db75a844ad1902997d93f970349.description: Star Atlas is a blockchain-based AAA space game. The hero uses high-fidelity 3D game environments behind a diegetic 'terminal' lead-capture modal complete with a system-log timestamp, grounding the signup form in the game's lore. A cinematic teal-and-black palette with high-frequency cyan glow CTAs gives a tech-noir feel, and blurred depth layering behind the crisp dark UI suggests a vast world.

31e90506c3a04dc88fc85688caf94985.description: Stella Domo, modular architecture and prefab holiday homes. The hero is a photoreal 3D architectural render at golden hour, warm ambers and sand against deep teal ocean, with the dark charcoal modular structure as the anchor. The headline is a massive high-contrast serif with an italic serif tagline and minimal sans navigation. The technique to steal is Z-axis typography: the display letters weave behind and in front of the structural pillars so the type lives inside the scene, reinforced by high-detail foreground grass that pulls the viewer into the environment.

4d7077ec2be24106800ac652263b55d0.description: Stenger Bike is a German premium bicycle retailer / e-commerce shop with a 99-year history, selling on personal advice and test rides as much as on product ("Dein Stenger-Bike-Erlebnis"). The hero is warm golden-hour lifestyle photography of two riders in open countryside, with white type placed over the darker, quieter part of the frame so no scrim is needed, plus a heavy italic red wordmark for speed and heritage. Strongest commerce move: a top utility bar that front-loads trust ("Über 99 Jahre Erfahrung", "Persönliche Beratung & Probefahrt", Google Reviews 4.9/5) above the fold. Good reference for CRO-driven trust stacking in retail.

3a37b8e81d8880399b44e468f8854d31.description: Steno.ai builds "AI Twins" — voice-and-chat agents that clone experts, coaches, influencers and brands, headlined by a Tony Robbins endorsement. Hero is a split editorial layout on cream with charcoal high-contrast serif headlines against a modern sans for UI, warm earthy landscape imagery and a single lime-green play accent. Steal-worthy details: the subject's head breaks out over the image frame for depth, rounded slightly-rotated image containers, and the Robbins testimonial styled as an audio player to signal the voice-AI product. Also carries an infinite marquee of chat-bubble cards, a three-step Design/Launch/Influence process and a dense video testimonial wall.

5d894651bfaf4438a8b04a08be75406e.description: Portfolio of Camille Frairot (SteviaPlease), Paris-based freelance motion designer and art director, ex-AKQA. Known for playful blobby UI with physics-based interactions, fluid and frosted-glass mouse effects, a 3D Memoji easter egg and a saturated green-pink palette. Headless render only reaches the branded 404 page: pastel rose-lavender gradient, giant Oopsy display type, tilted Polaroid photos with sparkle doodles. Homepage visuals unverified (JS-heavy render in headless).

2cd7b8e81d888029bfbfed2d4ef40025.description: Working Stiff Films is a commercial and branded-content production company (20+ years, clients from banks and burger chains to state agencies and luxury hotels), site under the Buzzworthy domain. Loud, maximalist, deliberately anti-corporate: high-contrast charcoal, vibrant red and cream, an ultra-bold retro-chunky display sans that feels like 70s advertising, a script logo, and a heavy grain overlay that gives the whole page a printed-paper texture. The mascot (a set of chattering wind-up teeth) is integrated straight into the type, replacing the O in GOOD. Best details to steal: the vertical repeating "WORK" ticker used as a border between copy and the video reel, the massive type scale as a confidence signal, and how horizontal scrolling and motion carry the portfolio instead of a standard case-study grid. Strong reference for a production-house or agency site with real personality.

44e19404c2dd4bde94832ba141cb8290.description: Google Store is the first-party retail site for Google-made hardware — Pixel phones (Pixel 10 / 10 Pro / 10 Pro Fold / 10a), Pixel Watch, Fitbit and Nest — plus financing, trade-in, free returns and Pixel Care+ coverage. Captured mid-launch, the landing hero is a dark product-reveal teaser: deep black canvas with metallic rose-gold and bronze highlights raking across an extreme close-up of the device, dramatic low-key lighting used to pull out texture and curvature, and Google’s own clean geometric sans (Product Sans) throughout. A centred white modal sits over the dark hero as a lead-capture tactic and doubles as a hard visual hierarchy break. Useful as a reference for mass-market hardware merchandising that still reads premium, and for how a huge catalogue is organised into category and comparison pages.

34e7b8e81d8880d39e2fd57726afb6fd.description: Product/docs site for StringTune, Fiddle.Digital's open-source JavaScript library for smooth scrolling, parallax, cursor tracking and attribute-driven web animation (featured on Codrops). The page itself is the demo: samurai-themed scrolltelling copy ("To master the String is to master the code"), split text with safe kerning, masonry feature cards, progress easing and sticky sections, closing with npm/Discord links. Screenshot currently shows the branded intro/loader (a single Japanese glyph on charcoal) — the WebGL-like scroll experience does not render in headless capture; details above come from page content.

a2288f34a6c6408f85eb1b8b0b2c3c32.description: Stripe is the payments and financial-infrastructure platform for internet businesses. The hero is asymmetrical and left-aligned — copy and CTAs anchored left, with Stripe's signature diagonal multi-colour sash gradient (purple, magenta, orange, yellow) sweeping across the right on a white ground. Typography is a geometric sans in a bold headline weight, with the colour-shifting text treatment where letterforms adapt to the gradient behind them. A muted monochrome customer logo strip sits directly under the fold as social proof. The canonical reference for gradient-sash heroes and restrained corporate slate-plus-Stripe-blue palettes.

0617a6f54d674c64805e99fca3312ed3.description: Studio Tumulte is a Lyon graphic-design studio (founded 2012 by Cloé Barraud and Camille Paquien) specialising in visual identity, editorial/publishing and cultural-sector art direction. The hero is a symmetrical, minimalist split-text layout with extreme negative space: a custom condensed '-TUMULTE' wordmark top-centre, a circular 'MENU' toggle, and two thin wide geometric-sans service labels ('création graphique' and 'direction artistique') on a warm off-white field. Reference for elegant, restrained studio landing pages.

5f3fd6d5fdb34fc19e432381cfce2c46.description: Morflax Studio is a browser-based 3D mockup and motion-graphics platform (devices, clothing, branding, abstract elements, SVG-to-3D) exporting up to 4K with no install. The homepage leads with a full-width looping post-processing effects reel and a spotlight card rail; the visible feature modal pairs a high-contrast display serif over a glitch-art bust with chromatic aberration, scanlines and halftone dithering on near-black, with pill-shaped ghost and solid CTAs. Strong blocks: a Creative Toolkit card grid of ten tools, a dense latest-templates masonry with Remix actions, featured collections, and a live in-browser 3D editor with keyboard-shortcut overlay. Visuals unverified (persistent feature modal blocked the headless render); hero type derived from the HTML effects-reel MP4.

cfff47db8e114f0c876747144acb07dc.description: Studio D is an Arnhem-based urbanism, landscape and architecture studio using design and research to tackle societal challenges; site handcrafted by Exo Ape. Hero is a clean split: stark white and black type over a full-bleed architectural visualisation, a serif italic sub-headline against a massive sans headline that slightly overlaps the image for depth, vertical side text and a showreel play control. Notable blocks: a numbered three-card services split (Plans / Vision & strategy / Research by design), a project showcase where each cover render transitions into a tall hero render, a societal-themes block, and a personal contact card with the founder's portrait. Strong reference for architecture and spatial-design portfolios.

fb62002581df43edaae7811a841c7880.description: Summer Water is a California zero-sugar rose brand (93-point Wine Enthusiast, Grenache base) on Shopify, also selling orange wine, magnums and a Societe subscription. Visuals unverified (an email-capture modal stacked over a 21+ age gate blocked the hero in headless render), so the hero itself was never seen; the observed modal used a blush pink / cream / pool-blue summer-chic palette (theme colour #fbd7e7), a high-contrast serif headline over clean sans, and a 50/50 split with lifestyle photography plus a frosted-glass blur isolating the CTA. HTML confirms a benefit marquee (Sugar Free / Award-Winning Wine / Homegrown in California), an As Seen In press logo bar (Forbes, Town & Country, PureWow, Stylecaster, Parade), a delivery-partner logo bar (Uber Eats, Instacart, GoPuff), and a pull-quote testimonial from Wine Enthusiast. Site developed by Attomik.

22e5a7300f3f4433ac0041a75955a0fe.description: Superpower is a consumer longevity / preventive-health membership built around a 100+ biomarker blood panel with an app-based results dashboard ("What we test", Reviews, FAQs, Become a member). The strongest thing to steal is its aggressive lead capture: an entry modal offering free protocols (energy, heart health, pace of aging) with "Join 150,000+ others", backed by physician headshots and Stanford/Harvard/UCSF/Oxford authority logos, over a blurred lifestyle background with the app mockup. Charcoal + white with earthy photography and soft pink/violet product UI. Note: the underlying hero itself is obscured by that modal in a headless render, so its exact composition is unverified (visuals unverified: entry modal in headless render).

4dbb512e56914342864d8277d4e18b64.description: Swab the World, a nonprofit campaigning for stem cell donor diversity. The hero is an asymmetric vertical split: on the left, oversized mustard-yellow condensed display type colour-blocked against deep teal with a photo of a diverse group; on the right, a light lavender-grey panel holding navigation and a CTA card. Palette is deep teal, earthy mustard-orange and soft cool greys. Strong reference for cause-driven sites that need editorial punch, and for split heroes where one half carries emotion and the other carries the action.

90e0eeed2e0748e99ac5bc477c96a07c.description: The saved SWAG design is gone. Swag was rebranded into Employment Hero in January 2025 and swagapp.com now resolves to Employment Hero's jobs site — a deep royal-purple hero with big white type, an oversized "2,000,000+ Jobs" stat used as instant social proof, light-blue accents and a single map-pin graphic. The original bright, playful, pattern-heavy SWAG superapp identity no longer exists at this URL; the app itself is now Employment Hero Work. Kept as a record of the rebrand — the current target is worth a look only for the oversized-statistic-as-hero device.

6df72ee1c80c4fb7a64a8325c0777dc0.description: Switch-Lit is a collaborative fiction platform ("Collaborative Stories for the Collective Imagination") where users co-write branching stories, with a Prompts and Library section and a Subrosa mode. The hero is a surrealist line-art illustration that morphs open books into hills and mountains, an instantly readable metaphor for storytelling as landscape, set on off-white with black display type and a vintage accent palette of dusty rose, teal, sage and pale yellow, plus an elegant serif subhead. Worth stealing: the hand-drawn metaphor illustration as the entire hero (no product UI, no photo), and the display + serif pairing that makes a web app feel like a printed book.

61690f1db06c4e33b4023835803f800e.description: Symbol Audio handcrafts high-end audio furniture, turntable stands and vinyl storage in solid North American hardwood, now expanded into full living-room furniture (sofas, sectionals, coffee tables), with collaboration lines for McIntosh and USM. The hero is full-bleed lifestyle photography with a massive bold sans wordmark used as the central graphic element, typography-as-texture rather than a headline. Palette is earthy and vintage-leaning: olive green, mustard yellow and warm wood tones. Distinctive touches: a scrolling marquee ticker for the NYC showroom announcement, and a newsletter modal rendered in a brand-accurate mustard so it reads as an intentional design layer instead of a generic interruption. Product grids carry Exclusive / Bestseller tags with from-pricing and colourway swatch counts.

22a1c39eb5114f2e95a507d3160458c5.description: Synthesized provides governed synthetic and test-data management for enterprise stacks (SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, PostgreSQL), letting teams validate software, migrations and AI agents before production. The hero is a split: left-aligned text against a large detailed isometric vector illustration of data concepts, in a clean white/black/grey palette punched by an electric-green accent on buttons and illustration highlights, with a dark nav bar framing the bright airy hero. Typography is geometric sans with a heavy tight-tracked headline. Notable blocks: a scrolling customer logo marquee, a four-column why-us grid, a numbered 01–03 process section, a tabbed platform showcase by database, and a large integrations logo wall.

6ab6e4f2053648abb3cf7d4f57eba641.description: TAG Heuer Connected collection page (FR/EN locale) for the brand’s luxury smartwatch line, currently the Connected Calibre E5 (40/42/45 mm) alongside the older Calibre E4. Positioning leans on Swiss watchmaking heritage fused with wearable tech — chronograph-style crown and two pushers, high-end case materials, heart rate, GPS, altimeter, SpO2, sleep and HRV tracking, plus pre-installed TAG Heuer Golf / Sports / Wellness apps and collaboration editions such as Connected Calibre E5 x New Balance. Useful as a reference for luxury-meets-tech product merchandising, where a watch configurator and per-reference product pages sit under one collection page. Visuals unverified (the server returns an Access Denied / 403 bot block in a headless render), so no hero type recorded.

346be45831844908b6bfcbc6f4f832c2.description: BOOST (takeboost.com) is a single-SKU immunity gummy vitamin with elderberry, vitamin C and zinc, positioned bluntly around "get sick less". The hero is one big orange-to-yellow gradient field carrying an enormous ultra-bold geometric sans headline in white, with a 3D product render overlapping the type so the jar sits physically in front of the letterforms. Navigation is reduced to thin outlined pills so nothing competes. Worth stealing: the circular floating "BUY" badge acting as a second focal point right next to the product instead of a conventional button, and the confidence of running an entire hero on scale plus one gradient. Good reference for single-product DTC brands with attitude and a small asset budget.

27806b65cadc446494660be46e27420f.description: Portfolio of Tanya Timal, a Miami-based beauty, fashion and portrait photographer working worldwide, with high-end retouching and dramatic lighting. The standout technique: the ultra-bold condensed sans wordmark is layered between the background and a cut-out of the subject (mask PNGs are served alongside each photo), so the model physically overlaps her own name, and the type inverts colour as it crosses a cool off-white vertical band into the warm bronze and chocolate photo. Editorial serif body copy alternates roman and italic mid-sentence, and a film-grain texture runs across the whole page. Project pages like /portraits and /commercial carry the same treatment. Designed by Maks Stepenko / THE FIRST THE LAST.

2147b8e81d88806daf66f7c5d78d5953.description: Tars AI is a Solana-based AI architecture protocol — an AI Market / super-app for deploying, tokenising and trading AI agents, plus a native LLM search engine (TGPT), the Sona cognitive trading framework and $TAI staking. A Solana Foundation grant recipient, with Gate.io, Bybit and Nvidia listed as partners. The layout is crypto-tech: large greyscale 3D console and figure renders, a stacked-card feature narrative around agent frameworks (Eliza, Rig, Solana Agent Kit), an LLM-provider logos bar (OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini) and a slide-indexed AI Market showcase with icon-driven navigation. Strong inner pages: /manifesto, /tokenomics, /brand (brand guidelines). Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) — the page throws a Next.js client-side exception in headless Chrome.

3177b8e81d8880e1a7fdceda79b97ffe.description: T-Bank (formerly Tinkoff) is Russia's largest branchless digital bank - cards, loans, deposits, investments, insurance and a business arm - and its homepage is a reference for how a huge product portfolio can still feel light. The hero is deliberately minimal and centred: an airy white/light-grey canvas, one heavy bold sans headline carrying the current offer, and a single canary-yellow CTA that owns all the contrast on the page. The thing worth stealing is the navigation: instead of a text menu, the product rail uses tactile 3D icons in blue, gold and teal that give a premium, app-like feel and make a dense catalogue scannable. A personalised top banner sits above the hero without competing with it. Overall: high-speed, low-noise fintech UI where colour is used as a budget, not as decoration.

b6c828f929dd4fcf898b351902dd7a50.description: tbh is a student mental-health platform connecting young people with licensed therapists and peer communities; the site is by Studio Voila. The hero is a photo-illustration collage: real photography cropped into speech-bubble frames, overlaid with hand-drawn doodles, arrows and script accents so the whole thing reads like a scrapbook rather than a healthcare product. Palette is bold orange, soft blue and sunny yellow on off-white; a heavy expressive serif headline is offset by handwritten accents and clean sans nav. The interesting tension is making a clinical service feel peer-to-peer without looking unserious. Strong reference for healthcare or wellbeing UI aimed at a young audience.

7adbd3abf2d94d7ca17429ea1ffd38f1.description: The saved design site is gone. Teamway was a Copenhagen member-owned society for hiring remote tech teams, but teamway.io now serves unrelated Greek-language filler prose seeded with casino references — typical of a lapsed domain repurposed for SEO. No branding, navigation or product content remains, and www.teamway.io/companies returns empty. None of the original pastel, card-based HR page survives. Kept for the record only.

8c5f3ed3c713483bb288049d97798145.description: TechSpeed is a Portland-based, women-owned BPO doing data entry, data processing, annotation and back-office support since 2002, pairing AI tooling with human teams (clients include Bank of America, Harvard, Red Cross). Visuals unverified: the page paints only a solid burgundy frame in headless render (JS/animation gate), so the hero could not be captured. Saved tags describe a bright, illustrated, card-based site with patterns and motion.

2887b8e81d8880058a3cd8b22e8ece0c.description: Terminal Industries builds an AI-native Yard Operating System that uses computer vision to digitise logistics yard operations: gate check-in, asset visibility, spotter dispatch and dock management (Ryder, Coca-Cola, HP, DSV, Prologis, Lineage). Heavily video-driven page, with a separate prerendered mp4 for every benefit section in both wide and vertical variants, animated odometer-style digit counters for the stats (85%, 90%, 50%, 4x ROI), and numbered 01-06 sequencing. Two distinct logo rows, one customer marquee and one investor/partner "built by the industry" strip, plus a competitor comparison table against Project44, Manhattan and Kaleris and an interactive yard-efficiency calculator. Site by rejouice. Visuals unverified (Playwright screenshot timed out twice), so hero type is left unset.

3177b8e81d888085aaf3e686278ae1bb.description: Terminal X is an AI agent platform for institutional investors (hedge funds, PE, family offices) that indexes a firm's private data alongside 100M+ public sources and returns decision-ready investment research. The site is a confident dark-mode fintech layout: deep charcoal background, oversized high-contrast white sans headline (Inter-like), and colour reserved almost entirely for the product interface. Best techniques to steal: a "peek-a-boo" product UI cropped at the bottom of the hero so the app proves itself without a full screenshot; an animated counters block (0min to first report, 0x more data, 0% research time reduction) that counts up on scroll; and a horizontally scrolling use-case marquee (Hedge Funds, Family Offices, PE, VC) that doubles as segment navigation. Clean feature grid with monoline SVG icons on a subtle grid pattern.

ac77950e80154866b7cf96627483e9b3.description: The CubeHouse is a next-generation office building in Amsterdam's Zuidas — the district's first hybrid timber build, 75% reclaimed or biobased structure, Paris Proof on delivery, WELL-gold indoor climate, with a publicly accessible rooftop garden and ground floor. The hero is a golden-hour 3D architectural render in ambers, soft greys and white, with a massive light-weight sans title and a small serif subtitle. Worth stealing: spatial layering that pushes the oversized headline behind architectural elements for real depth, and extreme scale contrast where tiny nav and subtitle make the title feel monumental against a hazy soft-focus cityscape.

ee05a80793d64dfd912b2bd3b6cc5cd7.description: The Art of Documentary is an online film school for documentary makers: 7 courses and 500+ video lessons taught by working filmmakers. Dark cinematic site in black and white with amber accents; the hero pairs bold sans headlines with a monospace split-flap countdown timer that builds enrollment FOMO. Below: numbered process steps over dramatic silhouetted film stills, a logos bar of student brands, and warm golden-hour to teal grading that makes the page itself feel like a film.

3a37b8e81d888016b54cc65d42af172d.description: The Drake is a Toronto boutique-hotel group (Drake Hotel on Queen West, Drake Devonshire, Drake Motor Inn) with a strong art-and-culture positioning. Hero is a full-bleed video and photo carousel with a modular boxed grid navigation header and numbered 01/02/03 property thumbnails doubling as carousel controls — high-contrast black and white with a signature deep red accent and gritty editorial photography. Heavy-weight sans headings with italicised accent words sit against uppercase utilitarian nav type. Notable blocks: a multi-tab booking widget (Hotel / Dining / Event), a Drake Art section framing the hotels as a pop-up gallery, a "What's On" event calendar rail with genre tags, and a blog carousel. Strong inner pages: /drake-art, /events. Site by Locomotive.

4826639b4c7a42a18ee5ac65dc6bdf01.description: The Drop Store is an awareness campaign disguised as an online shop — "your market for a world in water crisis" — where each product page prices an everyday item by the water it takes to make. The burger collection breaks a single hamburger into bun, sauce, lettuce, tomato, pickle and beef to reach roughly 2,500 litres, closing with "this product at this price doesn't exist. Yet." Sibling collections cover insects, bread, rice, soda, coffee and phones. Featured on Communication Arts. Strong reference for cause-driven e-commerce framing. Visuals unverified (page renders blank in headless capture), so hero type and blocks are left unset.

e9082c3f40df47738b730ec2841c0c08.description: Themekaverse is a gaming/NFT world-building project. The hero is an immersive, illustrated fantasy world-map with distinct biomes (glowing citadel, ochre desert), enclosed in a rounded glassmorphism-style border that gives it a HUD feel. Oversized geometric sans headlines mix heavy solid fills with hollow outlines and are anchored by a small, minimalist 'Explore' CTA; the high-fidelity cartography as a landing environment signals world-building depth.

4dbffd55e68e43e38f910dd9da26eb16.description: A wartime tribute project by Obys Agency dedicated to Ukrainian cities. The hero is a vertical split: the left pane holds a large artistic headline where experimental flowing script glyphs are used as decorative initials inside a bold sans, while the right pane works as an interactive dashboard with a city selector (Kyiv, Kharkiv and others), an illustrative centre block and a live population counter. High-contrast monochrome with sepia-toned, halftone-treated archival imagery, and a minimal hamburger anchored bottom right. Steal-worthy: pairing an emotional narrative pane with a data pane inside one viewport, and script-outline glyphs used as ornament rather than headline.

a42faf75d5474dbeac4af97574698bc3.description: Patch is a patient-acquisition marketing engine for direct-pay healthcare clinics: custom CRM buildout, nurture sequences, ads support and an AI admin that texts leads and books them on the calendar. Electric blue site with a blueprint-style grid overlay, brutalist condensed mega-type and a whimsical hand-drawn mascot in the hero; orange CTAs pop against the monochrome blue. Numbered process steps with oversized 01 digits and thin visible borders lead into a strong CTA section.

93751bf79f694479a8312b99561a0c6d.description: The Public Diagnosis is an awareness campaign site for The Brain Cancer Centre (Australia), campaign by The Royals, build by Oliver Grace and dnpg.dev, animation by Soma Studios. Patients and families share the filmed moment of their brain-cancer diagnosis. The entry screen is a minimal big-type gate on muted mint-green, pale grey and charcoal with heavy cinematic film grain, and a motion-blur smear across the word 'Public' that visualises the fog of a diagnosis; a circular loading ring around ENTER signals a guided journey rather than a page. Inside: a scored audio track with an on/off control, a content warning, a shared-diagnoses archive of individual story pages, full-bleed video and a donate CTA. Strong reference for emotive charity storytelling and type-as-metaphor.

c06a2aa38daa4389abc6d68877e26513.description: Raw Materials is 'an unusual design company' that designs and launches creative digital products, working with early-stage startups and established brands including Meta, Peacock, JP Morgan Chase and 7-Eleven; the team spans product designers, brand designers, strategists and technologists. The site is a client-side JS app (raw HTML returns only 'You need to enable JavaScript to run this app') with a black theme-color. Two headless render attempts, including a click-accept retry with a 14s settle, returned only a flat warm cream field — an unresolved intro/loader state. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render).

73055ff256284a0cb3ff4836b26260a9.description: "The Web Can Do What!?" is a Chrome for Developers advocacy site; this chapter argues for WebAssembly as a way to compile non-JS code and reuse native codebases in the browser. It is structured as a scrollytelling article — TL;DR, a four-up benefits row (Consistency, Flexibility, Time, Performance), a Snap/Snapchat case study with an animated walkthrough and an engineer pull-quote, a supported-languages logo strip (C++, Swift, Python, Rust and others), and a feedback widget. In headless render the page fell back to a flat amber viewport with a "your browser does not support some of the features used on this site" notice and residual card controls, indicating an interactive WebGL card scene that did not load, so visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render). Site by Hello Monday / DEPT.

2c38b1ada55c45e4b890e1a8d6a7394e.description: DASH is a Dutch worktech company building digital platforms to modernise temporary staffing and recruitment. Pitch black, neon lime and royal blue with an exceptionally bold brutalist sans. Techniques worth stealing: a persistent "Dashboard" side navigation with a light/dark toggle that turns the site chrome into a product metaphor, parallax image reveals inside geometric masks, and scroll-triggered horizontal movement on large type and marquee elements. Footer notes it is part of THE WORKS.

3a57b8e81d888020b399f69b5da6471c.description: Case study page on the site of Lopez Design (Gurugram, India) for the Accel Atoms rebrand — the pre-seed founder program by VC firm Accel for India and South East Asia. The hero is deliberately austere: massive bold sans-serif title over near-empty space, a red all-caps service list (STRATEGY + BRAND IDENTITY + TONE OF VOICE + VISUAL SYSTEM + UX&UI) acting as the anchoring subhead, and the descriptive copy pushed low-right — a strong reference for asymmetric big-type heroes built on negative space. The page itself is a long editorial scroll of full-bleed identity assets, animated GIFs and inline MP4 brand films alternating with short narrative copy, ending on a results block ($0 paid marketing) and a link out to atoms.accel.com. The identity is worth stealing on its own: intentionally colourless, drawn from whiteboarding language, with 0 and 1 as framing devices and an arrow between them used as a content-responsive illustrative system.

0d7267ddd0af4d76a2e1a22fea167163.description: Magma positions itself as "the trust layer for real estate" — unifying documentation, BIM, scans and operational signals into a validated digital twin with a measurable data-integrity index, sold to owners, lenders, insurers and cities. Awwwards Site of the Day; site by Cuberto.
