The preloader alone is worth noting: a full cobalt-blue field with the brand line "Experience Real Estate Agility" in clean white sans and a 0-100% counter, using the loading state as a brand statement rather than a functional afterthought. Main visuals unverified (loader never completes in headless render), so hero type and blocks are left unset.

3687b8e81d888002876ecf048ea1f44a.description: Author profile page (scenarist Jean Van Hamme) on the official Thorgal comic-universe site by Le Lombard. Astro-built experience with sound toggle, numbered menu (01 L'univers ... 05 La communauté), profile hero with name, role and tome/series counters, brush-stroke patterns and a large grid of all 29 album covers he wrote, plus a biography teaser. Headless capture caught the intro state: a full-screen backdrop of ghosted, low-contrast hand-drawn character line art — itself a steal-worthy technique for using busy artwork as quiet texture. Site by Caracal Agency.

85a84048a0b541b6bb0df04280604105.description: ThoughtLab is a US 'category-first' brand and product studio (New York, San Francisco, Salt Lake City) offering category design, brand systems and digital experiences. The hero is a stark dark-mode minimal composition — deep black with crisp white type and a single vibrant signal-red accent on the logo and pill CTA — built on a balanced three-column header that separates brand, tagline and actions for instant clarity. Note: deeper scrolltelling sections did not fully render in headless capture. Reference for confident negative-space, high-contrast agency branding.

cabea9ee23674b6a8c460e4751bf6c6f.description: Tilton Group is a Quebec family-owned manufacturer of ecodesigned thermoformed plastic packaging for food and pharma, founded 1985. The hero layers a large thin-weight sans headline ('Packaging designed for the future') over a shallow-depth-of-field product photograph, the packaging's greens and radishes reading as colour against a moody charcoal field — an editorial, premium treatment for what is normally a dry industrial category. A minimal header and a large circular scroll cue keep the imagery dominant. Below: About/Expertise/Approach feature blocks, a gallery of house brand cards (Repost, Brio, Forno, Awave), and a contact plus order-samples CTA. Bilingual EN/FR.

65a24e905a2e49bea52e5a865de4be20.description: Marketing site for TimeFrame, a concept "social diary" app — a calendar-based social network where people share upcoming plans and past memories as multimedia Slots (photos, video, music, voice memos). Hero is an editorial collage: charcoal near-black base, a massive white bold sans headline and a layered offset stack of portrait photography with canary yellow, teal, pink and green pops; scattered date and time markers ("JULY 30", "MONDAY 3:45 pm") float across the layout to literalise the time theme. The scroll-driven phone-UI walkthrough of Feed / Friends / Search / Profile and a giant "Every Day Counts" type finale are the parts worth stealing. Credited in the footer as created by JP; Webflow staging domain, 2021 spec project.

c3fdb29b08c54d6896e7548169f9c8d2.description: Titan — wealth management aimed specifically at high-performing tech professionals, combining AI tooling with human advisors. Split-screen hero: bold value proposition and headline stats (AUM, client count, founding year) on the left, black-and-white lifestyle office photography on the right; stark white/black base with cream and soft grey container blocks. Unusually rich set of trust-building blocks for a finance site: a direct fee comparison table against a traditional advisor (0.40% vs, $500 minimum), a horizontal advisor-profile carousel, a logo grid of employers (SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic), and two case studies explaining concentrated-stock diversification via visual flowchart diagrams. Also a clean numbered key-facts table. Good reference for making financial complexity legible.

890353119eb04ade85ea4714e72c8301.description: Tomas Than is an Italian luxury handbag brand founded in Milan in 2014, selling limited, hand-made men's and women's bags through its digital flagship. The landing is hyper-minimal: a stark black-and-white field centering the wide all-caps extended sans wordmark 'TOMAS THAN' in generous negative space, with only a small corner nav (Info, Instagram, Contact). Reference for luxury-fashion minimalism that leads with pure brand identity.

73e5391cf44d40da96401e76abbff0c5.description: Tortik Annushka is a Moscow designer-cake studio and confectionery — wedding, children's and corporate cakes to order with same-day delivery, plus a pastry school. The hero is a split screen: a muted slate panel against warm cream, with an ultra-sharp art-directed shot of a sculptural geometric cake carrying all the colour, and carousel pagination at the bottom. Navigation uses a widely tracked geometric sans for a premium read; hero copy shifts weights instead of sizes to build hierarchy. The catalogue behind it is a straightforward priced product grid by occasion. Good reference for craft food e-commerce where the product photography is strong enough that the layout should stay neutral and get out of its way.

a73d8ecba8ef4b09bc54ef1698d67627.description: ToyJoy© is a sexual-wellness brand that frames pleasure as an open, educational topic rather than a taboo. The hero runs oversized thin high-contrast serif type over a deep dusty-purple ground with a pronounced crumpled-paper texture, and drops the photography into an arched window cutout that pulls the eye down the page — a monochrome aubergine/lavender palette holds it all together. Notable blocks: a background video hero, a five-product carousel, an icon-led three-up benefits row, a scrolling marquee of pleasure words, and a footer with an animated letter-by-letter SVG logo reveal. Site by tubik; the cart currently sits in a sold-out state.

2cd7b8e81d888075b401cc30f238adfc.description: Transform9 sells AI voice agents to specialty physician practices (orthopedics, derm, ophthalmology), handling scheduling, patient navigation and outreach on top of Athena, Epic, ModMed and NextGen. Webflow build with a video-driven hero (tablet product footage) behind the headline, and a genuinely unusual interactive block: a form that has the AI agent call you live. Also worth studying for its heavy trust stack, a dual-row client logo marquee, a stats row (2,000+ providers, 96% satisfaction, 8:1 cost savings, 80% drop in call abandonment) and a testimonial carousel where each quote carries its own metrics. Site by Tubik Studio. Visuals unverified (loader in headless render); hero type read from HTML video source.

1d07b8e81d8880c9bc16f4a00b702b83.description: Travelwise is a travel booking business. The homepage currently serves a plain, near-static "Travelwise International" independent travel-agent page (welcome copy plus a short "Why book with us" list of trust points: 60+ years combined experience, access to 100s of operators, low deposits, in-store or phone service). Nothing of the bright, patterned, scrolltelling design language originally tagged on this record is visible in the live HTML, so the site appears to have been replaced or heavily stripped back. Visuals unverified (headless screenshot capture failed repeatedly).

c3dd4baf1cc7452ea9f6912609f41a61.description: Treebytree is a Dutch B Corp (Den Haag) that lets companies and individuals gift real trees as a digital product, with reforestation projects in Tanzania, Madagascar, Ecuador and Kenya. The hero layers an oversized elegant serif headline over full-bleed forest photography in an earthy palette of deep greens, red-brown soil and pale mint, with sans-serif nav and CTAs — editorial serif over busy imagery is the technique worth stealing. Strongest blocks are the partner case studies (Justdiggit, Bôndy, Selva, REEFolution) built as alternating photo/logo storytelling panels, an infinite logo marquee of 500+ corporate partners, and a clean numbered 1-2-3 process section. Inner pages Impact and For companies extend the same system.

2147b8e81d8880c6a84dc918d74a6116.description: TrueKind is a Mumbai-based clean/performance skincare brand (serums, cleansers, sleeping masks) on Shopify; the site is an Awwwards SOTD and CSS Design Awards winner. The hero is a split-screen composition built on extreme macro skin photography — dewy, glistening wet-look texture in fleshy pinks and tawny browns — with centred typography bridging the two panels: an elegant italic serif set against a bold modern sans. Worth stealing: the visceral macro-crop skin imagery and the serif-italic + sans pairing that reads premium without feeling clinical. Fully client-rendered store, so the block inventory comes from the render rather than the HTML.

523526f2877248c0b3b6f4d6c703e4aa.description: AI accounting platform (lease accounting, audit automation). Redesigned since saved in 2023: now a dark emerald hero with high-contrast serif headline and white accents instead of the old light look. Sections: platform pillar cards (Agents, Workflows, Knowledge), why-us list, role-based tabs with dashboard screenshots, testimonial slider with client logos, resources. Strong ref for enterprise fintech that swaps generic SaaS blue for a premium dark-green + serif identity.

2cd7b8e81d88805cb493e0d5e5005435.description: Ditto (trustditto.com) is an AI "CSR copilot": a single source of truth for sustainability and compliance data that auto-fills questionnaires, RFPs and framework reports (CSRD, VSME, EcoVadis, ISO, CDP), claiming up to 90% less reporting time, used by 500+ companies. The design makes a bureaucratic category feel editorial and confident: warm cream background, charcoal/navy text, an authoritative high-contrast serif headline paired with a clean sans for UI, and a single high-energy yellow card used to spotlight the priority framework (CSRD/VSME) inside an otherwise neutral grid. Worth stealing: an interactive card grid sitting directly in the hero as instant entry points to each service, and a centred email-capture field that converts before the user ever has to navigate. Also has customer stories and an industry/framework matrix.

dbd491cfa76b49e0b1d0685354684efc.description: Redirected: the domain has been dropped and repurposed. The saved reference was Bored Cow, an animal-free milk brand built on fermentation-derived whey protein. That store is gone; the domain now serves a Dutch-language online casino / sportsbook affiliate directory branded ZONDER CRUKS (headline: Beste Casino Zonder CRUKS in 2026, Veilig Spelen Buiten het Register), with nav for casino bonuses, bookmakers and fast-payout listings and no mention of milk or dairy. Search engines still return stale Shopify URLs (/pages/our-story, /collections/all) but all now fetch empty. The replacement is a stock affiliate template (purple #5e00c3 on white, bold sans, dense comparison cards with star ratings and licence badges) and is not usable as a design reference.

37553fe266c240d78ebc23cb24eba189.description: TUGG is a Swedish burger chain with an unusually committed brand world. The hero pairs a black background with bespoke 3D characters that anthropomorphise the ingredients, building an invented "Burgerian" nation as brand lore rather than just showing food photography. Type is heavy geometric sans with tight tracking, and the accent palette is primary red, yellow and green carried by the characters themselves instead of by UI. The value here is the commitment: a food brand that replaces appetite-appeal photography with character design and still makes you hungry. Strong reference for restaurant and FMCG work that wants personality over the standard dark-moody-burger look.

2147b8e81d88806e91f1ebfd28c8df4f.description: Turn.io is a WhatsApp-native chat platform for health and social-impact organisations (telehealth, appointment reminders, AI triage, chatbot journeys), used by WHO, MomConnect, Penda Health and CARE. The hero is a split composition on a deep forest-green field with mint highlights and a high-contrast coral CTA: a bold geometric sans headline with a colour-highlighted keyword, set against a layered collage of photographic cards, floating chat bubbles and system notifications that demonstrate the product in context instead of showing a dashboard. Strong blocks: testimonial cards fused with hard stats (600k patients, 567% engagement), a red-cross vs green-check comparison table of the traditional way vs Turn.io, a four-stage patient-journey process strip, an NGO case-study grid, and a 50+ million people reached figure over a world map.

e500332b7bee49c8b167b0eb1b8ff3a8.description: Dead — nothing renders. The domain still resolves and the document has scrollable length, but two separate headless renders (video and a 15-second-wait screenshot) both returned a completely blank white page with no text, imagery or layout.

1cbacb20ff854ef5aa07084eae7a136b.description: Twice Media House is a film / content production agency ("Chasing the elements") selling itself on story: the hero is a full-bleed cinematic video still, deliberately soft-focus, with a huge condensed all-caps line ("THE BEST STORIES DESERVE TO BE TOLD") sitting on top, plus a salmon-pink accent against dark blues and blacks. Notable blocks are the Work case-study grid and the reel/video sections. Worth stealing: keeping the background footage low-contrast and slightly out of focus so oversized type stays legible without any scrim, and the small ©-marked agency lockup in the corner as a prestige signal.

557cc9a3491144a3bdef9d2f453a8c56.description: Twingate sells Zero Trust Network Access, positioned as the replacement for the corporate VPN. The hero subverts the "fast, cheap, secure — pick two" engineering trope with a colour-popped "Pick Three", which does the entire positioning job in one headline. Palette is deep charcoal with white type, soft lavender support and a neon-yellow highlight reserved only for the punchline word. Headlines are clean sans; monospace is used for technical UI labels, a small touch that signals credibility to a developer audience. On the right, an abstract node-and-connector diagram explains the Zero Trust flow with icons instead of a screenshot. Good reference for security and infra SaaS that needs to explain an invisible product.

c59d47c0622a427492cb3b6f1e4b57e0.description: Two Good Co — an Australian social-enterprise store (soaps, homewares, apparel) that funds work supporting women leaving crisis. Full-bleed hero runs a background video montage of food preparation and community scenes with oversized black kinetic type scrolling over it, transitioning "CHANGE THE COURSE" into the brand name. Strictly monochrome black-and-white system with all-caps geometric sans, letting the photography carry colour. Notable blocks: a mission statement set in screen-scale caps ("We believe in people, until they believe in themselves again"), a "Words of Goodness" testimonial carousel with a send-your-own-message CTA, and an impact section pairing body copy with black-and-white documentary portraits of the people supported. Footer closes with a First Nations land acknowledgment. Good reference for commerce with a mission narrative.

7075cae56f2f4fcf9073bad85eea7d71.description: A specimen level inside Typefinder, a font memory game by studio bigbump, dedicated to Mencken, the Scotch-Roman serif by Jean François Porchez (Typofonderie). It is an atmospheric, type-led hero: a grainy monochrome base of deep blacks, greys and white with a single vibrant coral accent on the "Scroll down" CTA. Massive Mencken serif and italic weights are layered over soft organic shapes (jellyfish) for ethereal depth, while thin-line icons keep the UI minimal so the typeface stays the focus. The heavy film-grain texture adds a tactile, analog feel worth stealing for type-specimen or editorial work.

665612381afc4556ba2d4339bf48805e.description: Obys Agency's educational project on typography principles — how they choose fonts, combine them, handle alignment and contrast — split into chapters with examples pulled from real agency work. Black background, white and grey text, an enormous bold sans PRINCIPLES headline set on an asymmetric grid, and a 3D magazine mockup reinforcing the print-to-web theme. A vertical chapter list handles navigation and a floating card in the corner cross-promotes the Design Education Series. One of the most-referenced examples of dark-mode editorial education sites; sub-pages cover fonts, alignments and contrast.

5bb58f0271554307acfdf8e5b682b473.description: Enrollment/sales landing page for UI Expert, a Brazilian online UI-design course by Lucas Assis (154+ lessons, ~54h, students build a website, app and dashboard from scratch). Long-form conversion page led by a split hero: high-contrast headline with a vibrant blue CTA, hand-drawn vector doodles (lightning bolt, asterisk) for personality, and social-proof badges (4.9 rating, 10+ years experience) with subtle glassmorphism. Below it runs the classic course-page stack, curriculum modules, pricing with installment options, student testimonials, a money-back-guarantee, and an FAQ. A solid reference for structuring a trust-heavy info-product sales page.

927ea58f709c4625b10f1101d3a0cee1.description: Unbench — a Ukrainian talent-matching platform connecting businesses with vetted developers, marketers, designers and recruiters in under 48 hours. Typography-led hero in heavy uppercase sans on a dark abstract background with a yellow accent CTA, opening into a light body of white and peach section blocks. Useful blocks for a marketplace/HR product: a numbered three-step how-it-works card layout, a talent-profile carousel with hire-now buttons, an interactive stack of profile cards paired with an accordion of benefits, a vertical stats block (3100+ specialists), a grid of tech roles rendered as colourful abstract 3D icons, a testimonial slider, and a numbered FAQ accordion. Nice honest touch: a peach banner plainly stating freelancer profiles aren't supported. Footer carries a smiley in Ukrainian flag colours.

6f49bcebe2cd4cf39718c79e683c39c5.description: Award-winning campaign microsite for Picsart's "Unboring Boring" (Awwwards SOTD, FWA), the story of Picsart traveling to Boring, Oregon to help three small businesses rebrand from boring to unboring. Its signature idea is a custom dynamic typeface (with type designer Marta Cerdà Alimbau) that flips between a clean "boring" mode and a playful "unboring" mode through motion. The intro is a stark, high-contrast splash, deep charcoal, off-white irregular type, and a wiggly hand-drawn circular border, using extreme negative space to set the tone before the experience unfolds. A strong reference for concept-led campaign sites built around a transforming typographic system. Note: headless render stopped at the intro splash, so later sections are described from the campaign's documentation.

3cb8edffb71d4e9ba49a3d62fc1c76cc.description: Uncommon is a Melbourne brand and digital product studio (Kismet healthcare platform, Roblox corporate redesign, Peter Jackson e-commerce). Cinematic dark-navy hero sets an experimental serif UNCOMMON with mirrored letterforms and layers the portrait subject between the letters for 3D depth; a floating Featured Project thumbnail, pill-shaped MENU and /HOME breadcrumb anchor the corners. The case gallery overlays a text project list directly on media, plus a Melbourne location clock for a global-studio touch.

410e0072c12f4734a4d8940d0fbc3fd2.description: Undercat is a subscription design-and-development agency — unlimited requests, a pro team, one fixed monthly fee. High-contrast black, white and lime green with a clean geometric sans and a big-type hero. This is the reference to pull for productised-service positioning: a Comparison table (Undercat vs Freelancers vs Agency) where the winning column sits inside a rounded black spotlight container, a scarcity mechanic showing remaining client slots (e.g. 2/5), an interactive 'drag your request' placeholder inside the services list, plus a process block, stats, logos bar, team and closing CTA.

07d5b4bc7cbe4a2ea5631fb99e55f709.description: Baunfire agency showcase site for Unifi Protocol, a blockchain/DeFi platform built around economic sustainability and stablecoin-native tokens. The hero is an isometric 3D composition of abstract cubes with hyper-realistic textures (water, grass, stone) mapped onto them, a material collage over a light off-white base with charcoal, neon green and holographic gradient accents. Typography hybridises a clean modern sans with a bold pixelated display face for Blockchain Solutions, a low-fi/hi-fi contrast that reads as digital-native, and subtle vertical background grid lines add structural precision. Site by Baunfire.

4e4e96d498a94489819ed77a009990b3.description: UNION© is a Quebec contractor based in Baie-du-Febvre doing ceramic tile and flooring installation plus kitchen and bathroom renovation, RBQ-licensed and working with both trade professionals and homeowners. The site is far more confident than the category norm: stark black ground, monochrome sans, extreme type hierarchy and a monumental UNION wordmark cropped so it bleeds off-canvas along the base. The French service description sits centre-left while contact details and the RBQ licence number are pinned right. A strong model for making a small local trade business read as architectural rather than generic.

caf2719cea0a485aa3190b603501c232.description: Units™ sells compact modular prefab housing as an investment product, framed around "investments in the future of living" and the line "a unit is where your freedom begins". The positioning leans on radical efficiency — "there is nothing unnecessary inside the unit" — turning a small footprint into the selling point rather than a compromise. Visuals unverified (site crashed the headless renderer on repeated attempts), so hero type and blocks are left unset rather than guessed.

2147b8e81d8880b09d28d36c8ff19ff1.description: Unlearn is an AI clinical-trial company building digital twins — AI forecasts of a participant's control outcomes, qualified by the EMA — sold as a Plan/Monitor/Analyze platform (Scout, Hindsight, SimLab). The hero is pure editorial typography: a high-contrast serif headline juxtaposed against a geometric sans on a cream/charcoal palette, with soft lavender wash-highlights instead of solid button fills and a faint scientific grid backdrop that signals data rigor without noise. Notable blocks: an oversized stats strip (33% control-arm reduction, 4+ months enrollment saved) with asterisked approximate values, a three-part solutions section with product-UI screenshots per pillar, biotech-CEO quote testimonials and a press feed. Strong inner pages: /digital-twins, /evidence. Webflow build.

265de303847f4d90a2d42623b53e8df8.description: Untitled UI sells a Figma UI kit, React component library and icon library on pay-once licensing, claiming 380,000+ designers. The hero is a split layout: a bold tight-tracking sans headline on the left against an isometric collage of stacked UI mockups on the right, white and grey with vivid purple accents, and user avatars plus star ratings sat directly above the CTAs so social proof reduces friction at the exact click point. Secondary platform-specific buttons (React/Figma) segment the audience in the hero itself. A near-complete marketing stack follows: stats (900+ styles, 10,000+ components), logos bar, marquee, product UI showcase grids, three-tier pricing, a 'Wall of love' testimonials page, FAQ and Dribbble gallery.

6c4278173e1e4ed686bfea0a6940cdf7.description: Boba x Ice Cream is an AAPI-owned Los Angeles brand making super-premium small-batch ice cream built around boba — flavours like strawberry jam with panko bits and brown sugar boba, or caramelised banana with pastry flakes. The main site handles brand and story; collection packs sell through a separate Shopify storefront at shop.bobaicecream.com. Visuals unverified (the site repeatedly crashed the headless renderer on both desktop and mobile viewports), so hero type and blocks are left unset rather than guessed. Worth capturing manually — the existing bright/fun/illustration tags suggest a strong reference for playful food branding.

c019409f405c426ca72d90bfacf85370.description: Health By Habit (now branded 'HABIT') is a US direct-to-consumer wellness brand selling science-backed vitamin and supplement capsules across sleep, stress, libido, hair and multivitamins. The hero is a loud lifestyle product shot with the capsule bottle held in frame, framed by vibrant lavender-purple and electric-blue color-blocking and a massive ultra-bold sans-serif headline overlaying the image, with a clear 'Where to Buy' CTA. Reference for high-energy, color-blocked supplement branding aimed at mass retail shoppers.

4200c47f9ea74c358a1f983a532a8c22.description: Drop is a social-commerce and social-CRM platform letting brands sell and run campaigns directly through Instagram DMs. The hero is stark white with jet-black hyper-scale neo-grotesque type ('The Future of CRM is Social'), a soft lavender accent card, oversized corner radii and an asymmetrical layout that offsets body copy and CTA to the right of the headline. Most steal-worthy is a scroll-driven 'the old world / the new world' comparison that animates between two numbered states, plus an infinite 'trust them, trust us' marquee and a hover-reveal client grid where photos swap to hard metrics (19x ROAS, -50% CPL, 75% avg CTR). Retailer logo bar (ASICS, Galeries Lafayette, Hot Topic, Detroit Pistons) and a templates gallery round it out.

08baac2594d4404d808bc1ba76b76970.description: Flowkit was a UI-kit and design-system product for Figma; the domain still resolves but the product is discontinued and the page is now a single-screen end-of-life notice telling visitors the kit is no longer sold, with only a Contact Support CTA for existing customers. Layout is split-screen — a layered stack of product-UI mockups on the left, explanatory copy and the support CTA on the right — in a vibrant monochromatic violet palette with white and black accents and a bold italic display headline. Soft drop shadows give the mockup stack a floating dimensional feel. Worth keeping only as a reference for graceful product-sunset pages.

23253345810a4dd281ebcc9d41af61a3.description: Nash is an AI logistics platform that unifies and automates delivery decisions across fleets and fulfilment networks. High-contrast dark mode: deep navy/charcoal with neon yellow-green accents and a bold sans with clear weight hierarchy. Notable: a live "orders processed" counter used as running social proof, glassmorphism on UI cards, and an embedded interactive tour that lowers the barrier to exploring the product. One of the denser B2B pages in the base, stacking case studies, stats, testimonials and a bento grid before the closing CTA.

1d07b8e81d888023976edea388229e9e.description: Origin Financial is an all-in-one AI financial advisor (budgeting, spend tracking, investments, forecasting, estate and tax planning) claiming to be the first SEC-regulated AI advisor, 100k+ users. Webflow build. Hero uses a looping blue-sky cloud video with an italic serif headline ("Own your wealth") and, crucially, a working glassmorphic AI prompt bar seeded with a real question ("Where am I overspending?"), so the core value proposition is demonstrated in the first viewport. Below it, a long product UI showcase built from clean app-screen cards (portfolio performance, budget builder, subscription cancelling, net-worth forecast to age 90) and a short testimonial row. Strong reference for fintech app landing pages and for putting an AI input field inside the hero.

7fd0234d2fb2447fb250fd736b48271c.description: The saved /survey-2021/ URL no longer exists (it renders a branded 404 with oversized colour-blocked panels on charcoal); UX Tools now points to the 2024 Design Tools Survey at uxtools.co/survey/introduction/about-this-report. The current Framer-built report opens with an asymmetrical grid hero plus a persistent chapter sidebar, on black with vibrant pink, white and muted olive accents. Typography mixes pixelated monospace nav markers and bracketed chapter numbers against clean sans headers — a neo-brutalist dashboard look with visible structural rules. The steal-worthy pattern is the chaptered long-form research report navigation with inline data charts and sponsor cards.

999c6757256c451792ab424e9e5dd803.description: Vaayu is a Berlin-based carbon and environmental-impact software for retail and fashion brands, automating real-time emissions, water and waste calculation (now part of Carbonfact). The landing pairs an elegant serif big-type headline with a high-contrast black-and-white bark texture inside a merger-announcement modal, over a sophisticated olive-green, charcoal and off-white palette. A yellow-green announcement bar tops the page for visibility. Reference for editorial serif type and source-bleed natural textures on a climate-tech SaaS site.

2147b8e81d8880d5a955c1ba837972c6.description: Valdera is an AI-powered B2B sourcing and procurement platform for chemicals and raw materials (Toray, BASF, Dow, Evonik as customers). Dark, high-contrast hero: deep charcoal, a centred bold sans headline paired with a serif sub-line, an acid-lime CTA as the single accent, and a product peek where the top of the dashboard UI pokes above the fold to pull the scroll. Notable blocks: an oversized word-by-word marquee, an unusual stats block that uses chemical-macro imagery as the visual bed for 400K+ suppliers / 1.7M+ chemistries, a Then/Now comparison, a photo-tile industry grid, executive video testimonials and a video-background footer CTA.

ae5967aabb9844bfb3e713f7a724b640.description: Varier is a Norwegian ergonomic furniture brand (Oslo, since 1979) known for movement-friendly seating like the Variable and Gravity kneeling chairs. The current site opens on an extreme macro product shot of a knitted chair textile that fills the viewport, using a restrained charcoal-and-off-white palette and clean sans-serif navigation to signal high-end craftsmanship through texture and restraint. Note: the saved /eng/ path now 404s and the live site uses the /en locale. Reference for tactile, material-led minimalism in furniture e-commerce.

37a7b8e81d88806380dac4435b01bc55.description: French manufacturer of custom CBRN-hardened modular shelters, premium industrial storytelling. Cinematic full-bleed photo hero with HUD-style corner brackets, trapezoidal nav bar and orange scroll accent; below: looping product videos per spec section, numbered logistics timeline (001-003), protection matrix cards and a 5-scenario use-case slider. Strong ref for making heavy technical product feel high-end; note the loading screen with hatched progress bar.

a70b6cb3ed5d43ebb0e0ea65f4178575.description: Vendredi Society is a France-based digital design studio that assembles a bespoke team of senior freelancers per client (“one mission, one epic team”), sold through two clear models: Custom Package (fixed price) and As-You-Go (subscription). Clients include PrestaShop / The Merchant Lab, Otio and Press Play On Tape. The .fr is the French locale of the same site (EN lives on .com). The hero is a centred-copy composition over a high-angle split-texture landscape — harvested field against green field as a growth metaphor — in earthy tans and forest greens with a lime-yellow logo and buttons, white wide-tracked sans over translucent dark UI chips for legibility. Distinctive: a numbered frame-counter preloader with an FPS/Player Timeline readout, and results stated as KPIs rather than praise (3M DOOH impressions, 264K views in ten days, +2k users in week one). Notable blocks: a two-model pricing split, KPI cards, and named client testimonials with roles.

a561a0fd2d644475ad3c32ad63c0422b.description: Ventriloc is a Quebec business-intelligence and data consultancy helping companies turn data into growth and adopt AI; the site is in French. The hero is minimal big type: bold sans with tight leading and kerning on off-white, high-contrast black text and a single muted gold accent. Two details worth taking — the hand-drawn underline used to emphasise one keyword in the headline ("croissance"), and the pill-shaped floating nav bar. A restrained, confident consultancy look that gets a lot out of one accent colour.

e4be7ecfa9ae4a63a995051d04a1f40f.description: Vetcity is a Moscow network of veterinary clinics. The hero treats the brand name as the main graphic: oversized bold geometric sans in black on white, with a photograph of a dog partly overlapping the letterforms so the type and image share depth instead of stacking. Palette is stark white and black with one piercing electric blue reserved for interactive elements, and large corner radii on the white and blue containers soften what would otherwise be a very hard layout. Useful reference for healthcare and clinic sites that want to feel confident and modern rather than pastel-medical — the whole personality comes from scale, one accent colour and rounded containers, no illustration system needed.

5185c6c336f644b8b1bc496bd0febbe4.description: Vibor is a Milan-based manufacturer of pressure, temperature and level switches and sensors for industrial, automotive and mobile machinery. The Webflow-built homepage opens with an oversized VIBOR wordmark filling the upper half of a pure-black screen, stacked directly above a desaturated high-contrast industrial video panel — a brutalist editorial feel in near-monochrome black, charcoal and off-white with all-caps utilitarian sans body copy. Notable blocks: silent looping Vimeo background video sections used as chapter breaks between product families, a three-card Why-choose-us feature triptych with cutout product renders, and a catalogue-download CTA. Site by Studio Sen Tempo with Microsys.

3177b8e81d888028924dd7f02f025c13.description: Vibrant is a Noomo Agency showcase site for a wellness/supplement brand, built as a heavy WebGL 3D scrolltelling experience with card-based product sections and motion-driven transitions. The domain resolves and the project is still hosted, but it is a GPU-dependent build: the headless capture returned a minimal 500 page (monospaced 500 / Internal Server Error / Error creating WebGL context) because the render environment could not initialise WebGL, so the attached screenshot shows that error rather than the design. Treat this record's visual notes as unverified and re-check in a real browser. Marked Live rather than Dead since the failure is a rendering-environment limitation, not a missing site.

1dff9fdbe2e44e44a9f882cda6c12855.description: Viens-là is a Paris digital and branding agency (founded 2011, 30+ Awwwards wins including Site of the Day and a Developer Award) working across corporate, food & drink, sport, luxury, finance and education. The tone is playful and self-aware all the way down: even the cookie banner is a designed neo-brutalist yellow-and-purple block with rounded corners and the line 'Let us taste your warm cookies'. Notable blocks: a latest-projects showcase, a three-part services breakdown (brand universe / design / production) with tag lists, a 2010-2024 awards timeline, a 'VL spam explorer' reasons-to-choose-us section, and a yes/no contact CTA. Hero itself unverified (the cookie wall blocked the headless render), so hero type is left unset.

31debb45fc9945c5b6f1bba341a8664d.description: The domain no longer serves Vikki Breusova's product-design portfolio (previously a UX/UI portfolio and design courses by an Awwwards judge). It now renders 'FoundAI', an unrelated free Chrome extension that adds an AI-powered summarizing search feed to Chrome — a genuine repurpose of the domain, not a slug change. Dark premium-tech hero: deep midnight-navy ground, royal-blue primary actions, white bold geometric sans headline 'Search Smarter. Find it Faster.', green status dots as sparing accents. Worth stealing on the current target: a glassmorphic browser-window mockup with a floating 'AI Summary' overlay, soft blue radial glows behind CTAs, and trust microcopy ('No sign-up required, Zero tracking') sitting directly under the buttons. Existing tags describe the original portfolio.

5cdc5dfe14484c55b6baf1b3446a1857.description: Vivid+Co is a New York full-service agency and strategic advisor spanning strategy, communications/PR and creative, with the ability to invest capital. The hero is a big-type statement built on a rotating word cycle — 'We are Storytellers / Strategists / Creatives / Marketers / Technologists / Vivid+Co' — over a white, near-imageless Gatsby build (Twitter creator meta credits ToyFight). Notable blocks: a three-column expertise breakdown with long service lists, anonymised case studies (Fintech Company, Data Automation Tech Company, Major European Government), a large client logo wall plus a separate 'Featured in' press logo wall, and an expandable team/advisors section with long-form bios. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render); hero type derived from the HTML rotating-word heading.

a9d736737a3147958bb482e2c6f4bfc5.description: VJ-Type is an independent Paris type foundry from studio Violaine & Jérémy; the saved page was the specimen for 'Voyage', a romantic high-contrast display serif (2019, extended 2024). Status Redirected: the saved /6-voyage path now returns a 404 (editorial thin-serif '404' on beige, with a playful 'VJ WEARS MARSÈLL SHOES' header) — the Voyage typeface has moved to vj-type.com/collections/voyage. The foundry site itself remains live.

3a62a416be4847c3a05137bd54075a59.description: VOS9X presents itself as a multi-asset investment and growth equity firm, delivered as an immersive narrative experience rather than a standard site. What renders headless is the entry screen: near-black background, oversized clean sans headline centred with everything else pushed to the perimeter (logo and firm description sit in the top corners), plus a Start CTA and an audio toggle. The 3D and scrollytelling content sits behind that Start gate and is unverified in a headless render. The perimeter-branding trick — clearing the whole centre for one typographic statement — is the takeaway from the intro screen itself.

7fea6d5ec9c542c6a0870a6dce514e73.description: Landing/docs site for Vuesax, an open-source Vue.js UI component framework (by Lusaxweb) with its own distinctive, non-Material design language. The hero is a live product showcase: real UI components (cards, inputs, buttons, toggles) float around the CTA on a clean high-contrast background, anchored by a vibrant primary blue with pops of coral, red and cyan. Soft drop shadows, rounded corners and interactive toggles/play buttons demo the framework's components directly in the hero. Good reference for framework/library sites that sell themselves by making the product interactive on the first screen.

3347b8e81d88807ba966c8207a9e40c2.description: Waabi is a Toronto physical-AI company building autonomous trucks and robotaxis on a single end-to-end AI model trained in its own neural simulator (Waabi World). The hero is a full-bleed cinematic truck video with an oversized slab-serif headline (Built to think. Born to haul.) that acts as the layout structure itself, a centred pill-shaped floating nav, and a single magenta accent used only on interactive elements against a gritty charcoal-and-ochre backdrop. Notable blocks: a long parallax image/video scrolltelling section that alternates road footage, simulator renders and team portraits, a Scalable / Practical / Safe pillar switcher, a tech showcase of three video cards (Waabi World, Mixed Reality Testing, the Waabi Driver), a partner section with a Volvo executive quote, and a dated insights feed. Great reference for premium AV/robotics brands and video-led scrolltelling.

16c7b8e81d8880138c1af4db86c15408.description: Walbi is an AI-agent crypto trading platform (no-code trading agents, high leverage, a "Lighthouse" signal engine), built on Astro with multiple language variants. The hero is a pure-black stage where an oversized ultra-bold lowercase "walbi" wordmark is used as a background structural element, with a tablet product shot held in hands layered in front of it for depth and broken vertical neon-green light streams reading as falling data. The all-caps headline uses wide tracking and the CTA is a solid neon-green pill. Notable blocks: an "I SEE / I READ / I THINK / I ACT" four-step agent-persona scroller with a skip control, a Lighthouse visualization video, an iPhone mock with the AI-signals UI, community counters (X, Telegram, Discord), a press-quote row and an infinite app-store review marquee with a repeating rating ticker.

fe2ed3b47e28435ba06e594333657d03.description: Wealthsimple is Canada's fast-growing consumer fintech covering chequing, credit card, trading, crypto, investing, mortgages and tax. The hero runs a full-bleed brand film ('More is more') whose frames read as a layered photo collage of life moments stitched together by a thin hand-drawn white line over a muted blue-grey gradient, with a large elegant serif headline, geometric sans sub-copy, a white ghost CTA and a pause control. Notable blocks: a rotating promo ticker above the nav, a five-card product switcher, alternating full-bleed product feature panels with phone-UI and 3D illustration art (floating mountaintop for Summit, pie graph for Classic), a video-led TLDR newsletter block, and a 'Trusted by over 4 million Canadians' social-proof CTA.

2147b8e81d88800dbc37d57e554cb8f7.description: Athleats is a performance-nutrition recipe and meal-planning iOS app founded by two brothers — macro-tracked recipes, weekly meal plans, auto-generated grocery lists, cooking mode and micronutrient tracking. The brand runs a warm editorial food palette: cream grounds, an olive-sage green, charcoal text, a high-contrast serif for headlines against a clean sans for utility text, and bespoke hand-drawn food illustrations (cast-iron skillet, running shoe, beet, labelled salmon fillet) used instead of stock photography. Distinctive blocks: a scrolling multi-row marquee of micronutrient chips (Omega 3, Iron, Vitamin B12, Selenium), macro-annotated recipe cards showing protein/carbs/fats plus cook time, a dense recipe gallery, phone-screen app UI showcases and athlete testimonial portraits. Site by Fourth Floor (fourthfloor.design). Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render) — a promo modal with backdrop blur could not be dismissed.

4c11071211b7499d81aa81734ae7d8bd.description: Motto is a strategic branding agency working with tech, culture and innovation clients. The hero is aggressively typographic and near-monochrome: heavy black sans on off-white, set at wildly different scales and orientations so the headline deliberately breaks the grid and reads as motion rather than a static block. A vertical boxed label runs up the side as an editorial accent, and an oversized arrow glyph does the scroll cue instead of the usual chevron. Almost no colour and no imagery in the first screen, which is a confident move for an agency selling positioning. Worth stealing for the overlapping off-grid headline treatment and the vertical side label.

2cd7b8e81d888035a26eeba2ae73c3d1.description: Weavy is now Figma Weave (rebranded after joining Figma; the domain still serves the marketing site and app.weavy.ai still works). It is a node-based canvas where creative pros chain AI models and professional editing tools into repeatable workflows, with free/Starter/Pro/Team/Enterprise tiers and workflows publishable to the Figma Community. The hero is the product: a light-grey canvas grid with the node graph drawn directly on it, high-contrast black type, and an oversized acid-yellow "Start Now" button that breaks the header grid to grab all the focus. Worth stealing: node-based storytelling that demonstrates the mental model instead of explaining it, and the subtle canvas grid background that makes the whole page feel like the workspace itself. Note for the archive: the record still says Weavy, the live brand is Figma Weave.

3a37b8e81d88809389f1cfa5316697e3.description: Cleo is the "world's first AI financial assistant" — a budgeting, savings and cash-advance app known for its roast-you personality; the marketing site runs on Next.js with DatoCMS and Mux video. The page is editorial and video-led: a phone-screen-with-lighting-reflection hero image under "Money talks. Cleo talks back.", art-directed original photoshoots rather than stock, a tabbed product switcher (Save / Cleo Card / Debt), a review carousel of App Store quotes with video thumbnails, a dated press-mentions list and a dual app-store CTA. Declared theme colour is deep maroon. Visuals unverified (loader/gate in headless render).

6cb49724edd44d9f999e1a2b94e8ecd5.description: Webflow's No-Code Conf event site, now serving the 2021 edition as an archive (the event has since been rebranded Webflow Conf). The hero is big type on a deep textured navy field with a film-grain overlay, punchy magenta, peach and electric-blue accents, and a delicate high-contrast serif date set against an ultra-bold sans headline. A full-width magenta announcement bar carries secondary news without cluttering the layout. Strong reference for conference sites: agenda, per-session pages, themed session tracks and a speed-build challenge all live as inner pages.

5cd94ece532f456391ffc8b7e01a6d08.description: Showcase site for Redis Agency's Webflow department, a San Francisco design studio (12+ years, 50+ multidisciplinary designers) that positions itself as "designers who code" making award-winning, 3D and motion-rich sites in Webflow (Awwwards SOTD, FWA). The site is celebrated for interactive, animation-heavy craft as a portfolio of their no-code capabilities. Note: the headless render repeatedly failed with a client-side application exception, so the current visuals could not be captured and are described from the studio's known, award-winning work rather than a verified frame.

14bdae41ca384915877f4ce08f1a0f65.description: Webisoft is a Montreal software engineering studio (blockchain, AI, custom development) selling on team quality: "An elite team of software engineers". The hero is a brutalist big-type composition, terracotta red and black with an off-white header card that breaks the full-width nav convention, plus a repeating horizontal-bar pattern that melts and shifts on the right edge for a glitch/motion effect. Heavy geometric sans for branding, monospace for technical readouts (/0026, MTL (CAN), ENGINEERING_). Worth stealing: the data-readout micro-labels and the pattern-distortion device as a substitute for imagery on a services site.

3a37b8e81d88808a896ddc0733fe4d15.description: Wembi (by Innoverse Group, Italy) is an open-source "Instant Digital Twin" platform that turns machinery and IoT assets into remotely controllable virtual replicas with predictive maintenance; the site is Italian-language. Visually it is editorial-tech minimalism: a muted desaturated teal and powder-blue canvas with neon lime accents, a custom segmented geometric display wordmark treated as central architecture, and a large soft translucent 3D sphere for depth. Content is indexed like a catalogue (n.001 WHAT / n.002 HOW / n.003 WHY / n.004 WHERE), with a two-part stepper driven by per-step webm loops, a sector switcher (Industrial, Energy, Aerospace, Medical) and floating pill HUD navigation in the bottom corners. Credits: e-t.studio.

6fd3f24d5eac4469b85d7304c436b347.description: Swwim, a UK social media and content-creation agency (Portsmouth/London, founded 2018). The hero is a collage: heavy wide all-caps sans headline layered with small photographic inserts, a central megaphone illustration and a scribbled hand-drawn circle, all on a saturated cerulean-blue field with gold and beige accents. Custom fluid script logo plays on the aquatic name. A scrolling ticker bar at the bottom keeps constant motion. Good reference for editorial collage heroes and for agency sites that need personality without heavy 3D or WebGL.

d5a0a1164ad544bc883c185e8ae9b64f.description: Whereby is a European, privacy-first WebRTC video-calling company offering two products: Meetings (instant, in-browser calls) and Embedded (a video API/SDK for building calls into platforms like telehealth and eLearning). Built in Framer, the split hero pairs a serif headline with clean sans on a warm peach background and deep-indigo CTAs, layering a product-UI window over a lifestyle photo (soft-brutalist rounded corners). Notable blocks: a trusted-by logos bar, a Meetings-vs-Embedded comparison with feature checkmarks, an industry carousel (Telehealth, eLearning), pull-quote testimonials, customer-story case studies, and an FAQ. Strong reference for warm, human SaaS branding and showing product context without dry screenshots.

e2df4a88007a471795f0d4a1b3134717.description: Widelab is a product design studio positioning itself as 'AI-native, senior-led', building and testing digital products for established, high-valuation teams. Minimal high-contrast black and white with a vibrant lime-green accent on every interactive element; bold modern sans throughout. The hero uses dynamic headline text that swaps its key verb (perform / scale) around a centred product mockup. The strongest positioning move is the stats block: huge animated counters totalling the combined valuation of client companies (north of $110 billion), which does more for credibility than any copy. Also has a dense client logos grid (WeWork, Circle K), detailed case studies (CloudKitchens, Circle K, Traba, Founderpath) with large UI previews, and a floating lime 'Play video' cursor that tracks the user as a persistent interactive element.

9c0057a092b348fdb7d303f5af6b6daf.description: Wild Souls is a Greek plant-based food brand — nut butters, halva and unprocessed pantry products, sold under the line "Taste the Wild. Find your Soul." The hero is graphic-led: one massive stylised illustrated object anchors the frame, with the headline ("STAY JUICY") set in a bold distressed vintage sans and placed behind parts of the illustration so the layers interlock. Palette is deep forest green, rich tomato burgundy and muted off-white; navigation stays in a clean geometric sans so the distressed display type reads as deliberate. Worth stealing: the z-index layering of type behind artwork, and the stamped texture on the headline that sells a craft, small-batch story without any photography of the factory.

7fc1ceda6d904f49a5532ac99518e2f3.description: Wimba makes 3D-printed orthotics and prosthetics for animals, and the site sells the outcome rather than the technology — the split hero puts a happy dog in a natural setting opposite the copy, in soothing lavender and deep royal purple anchored by saturated photo greens. Worth stealing: an organic S-curve divider between the text column and the photo that breaks the rigidity of a standard split grid, and a benefit list built from punchy "No [pain point]" statements that reads faster than any feature table. A good reference for healthcare or veterinary UI that needs to feel warm rather than clinical.

e65217e6109e45f794643b7a978f92e0.description: Wirewerks is a Quebec-based manufacturer of optical fiber and copper structured-cabling systems for data centre, enterprise and broadband networks. The hero is a centred all-caps bold sans headline that rotates through positioning statements on a deep navy monochrome field with white and light-blue accents, framed by a floating side Contact tab and a Scroll cue — high contrast, lots of negative space, industrial and technical. Strongest block to steal is the stats bar (29 years, 23 industry awards, 50K+ products, 30M+ installed, 50M+ ft cable shipped) plus a horizontal text marquee of system categories. Site by Locomotive.

2028f6c7e1df4c5caea838bd5454e617.description: wise.design is the public showcase and documentation portal for Wise's global brand identity system. The hero is a horizontal carousel of photography and product shots masked into circles and pill shapes, which is the core device of the whole identity: irregular organic masks instead of rectangles. Palette runs the full Wise green range from deep forest to electric lime against white and dark neutrals, with Wise Sans (bold geometric) carrying the type. A top toggle switches the whole page between Inspiration and Direction modes, a neat way to serve both brand-feel browsers and spec-hunting implementers from one page. Best-in-class reference for how to publish a brand system as a site rather than a PDF.

16c7b8e81d8880978c9ffda75ca99a2c.description: Wix is the mainstream website builder, now positioned around a hybrid AI builder (the Aria assistant, vibe coding) sitting next to the classic drag-and-drop editor. The hero is a centered big-type headline over a soft white-to-pastel blue and lavender gradient, with layered, softly shadowed editor UI panels floating above the background to fake depth: a cursor mid-drag, an add-element panel and an AI generation window together tell a "watch it being built" story instead of showing a static screenshot. The page then runs a template picker grid, an Aria AI section, feature accordions, a domain search, a business-dashboard showcase, a numbered six-step how-to, customer stories and a long FAQ. This is the standard Wix marketing homepage, not a campaign microsite.

293d521b76f543b38cc051b2f2ce290f.description: Wonderland is an Amsterdam brand experience design studio (also at wonderlandams.com) positioning itself around sustainability and "meaningful value for people and the planet". The About area sits inside a dark charcoal, off-white and orange system where the site's numbered outline navigation (1 HOME, 2 WORK, 3 ABOUT US 3.1–3.5, 4 BEING HERE, 5 MANIFESTO) is itself the main visual element — a utilitarian, high-contrast index that replaces imagery with hierarchy, and a genuinely stealable pattern for studio sites. Sub-sections split "Us & you", "How we do this", "Expertise areas" and "Brands", alongside a manifesto on responsible desire and green goals, and a Being Here section covering team, diversity, perks and traineeship. Strong inner pages: the Sustainable Digital Design case study documents real technical decisions (SVG sprite sheets, subsetted fonts, a 158kb JSON animation cut to a 45kb dotLottie, CPU wake-up audits). Contact block copies role-specific emails to clipboard. Hero type left unset — headless render only captured the open menu overlay.

c833943d19734ca1ad596d35cd3a7fe7.description: Wonderwall Studio is a Polish premium brand selling artist-drawn made-to-measure wall murals, wallpapers, tiles and paints, with showrooms in Warsaw and Kraków and a full WooCommerce catalogue (200+ wallpapers, 500+ paints, outlet). The hero is full-screen painterly lifestyle photography with an oversized high-contrast serif headline set into the scene, over muted moss green, antique gold and soft brown — gallery-catalogue art direction rather than e-commerce. Minimal sans UI and a soft glass "go to catalog" button keep the image dominant. The block worth stealing is the Constructor: a live personalisation tool where you crop, mirror, rescale, recolour and resize a pattern to your exact wall, taught through an inline product video with icon-labelled controls (rotation, scale, material, colour, saturation, size). Free-sample request and yearly downloadable PDF catalogues back the premium claim. Multilingual PL/EN/FR/DE. Site by Obys.

34e7b8e81d88809396cdc81465ea8a6d.description: Personal site of Won J You, a 20+ year UX veteran (AmEx, Porsche, ESPN, Intel) who pivoted to design coaching, mentorship and teaching ("Professor of UX"). Hero is pure textual architecture: ultra-bold condensed uppercase type in tomato-red on black, stacked with tight leading into a monolithic block, with a small centered nameplate layered on top. Scrolltelling narrative ("Same passion. New mission."), a repeating 20-YEARS marquee, showreel video, and a brand-experience logo wall where hovering names swap in client imagery. Roman-numeral section nav (I.Intro ... VI.Get in touch) is a nice editorial touch.

e34e2b7603fb4d79b1dd294a671071f8.description: Wope is an AI-driven SEO research platform focused on competitor analysis and hidden keyword opportunities. The hero is full retrowave: deep violet and neon purple over a dark cosmic background, with a glowing perspective grid and horizon line creating depth, plus a subtle particle layer for a premium space feel. A glassmorphic dashboard preview is cropped at the bottom edge, showing the product without breaking the aesthetic. Headline is bold sans with tight leading. Good reference for dev and marketing tools that want an atmospheric dark hero and still need to prove there is a real product behind it.

96ba77a202734b8e987d32f796518747.description: Workleap, an HR / employee-experience software suite (engagement, performance, onboarding). Hero runs a royal-blue to indigo gradient with white type and a warm coral accent on interactive elements. The headline mixes a clean sans with a flowing italic serif on the key phrase, an easy trick for editorial emphasis in B2B SaaS. Stylised product cards and mock chat bubbles overlap real human portraits to humanise the software, and an "Ask" input sits directly in the hero as a low-friction entry point. Good reference for HR and people-software UI, gradient SaaS heroes and mixed serif/sans headlines.

2cd7b8e81d88807eaee0c9b32f4d3327.description: Work Louder is a designer-focused mechanical keyboard and macropad brand (Creator Micro, Nomad, Knob1, plus a Framer collab), built in Framer. Dark split hero with photoreal 3D product renders as the centrepiece: deep black canvas, an electric-blue light bleed gradient rising from the bottom edge, and toxic lime-yellow accents on CTAs and nav. Geometric sans headers give it a technical, premium tone. Steal-worthy: the floating pill-shaped centred nav, the layered light-bleed glow used to anchor text on black, and an emoji-driven marquee ticker that carries the brand voice into the footer.

ad75acf0b7c94759a1065809a9602f55.description: Site of Pact (Pact Studio Inc), a design-led, development-driven studio in Montreal and Victoria focused on high-conversion DTC and Shopify+ builds, with past work for Nike, Glossier, Aritzia and Knix and $500M+ in client sales. The hero is a typography-driven editorial layout: a warm cream background with charcoal text, a massive ultra-bold condensed sans headline paired with an elegant high-contrast serif, and soft lavender/mauve pill buttons. An oversized stylized script ampersand breaks the headline block for a premium touch, and by omitting imagery the studio centers authority on bold messaging and whitespace. Strong reference for confident, image-free editorial studio branding.

43efbc594f114b75b921e277ee83182f.description: The saved design site is gone. wowpage.io now 301s to forelinksters.com, a Vietnamese live-sports streaming portal branded CakhiaTV (trực tiếp bóng đá) built on WordPress, with football/basketball/tennis/esports streams, fixtures, standings and results. Nothing of the original dark, illustration-led IT services page remains, and the domain renders blank in a headless browser before the redirect resolves. Kept for the record only.

1e02699d9a7a4ba1af0bcf2ce12577d0.description: Y42 is a turnkey data orchestration platform for building, monitoring and maintaining data pipelines. Deep space aesthetic: black and dark purple with neon cyan and violet accents, and a clean modern sans. Steal-worthy: interactive product tours embedded directly inside the feature sections so the demo lives where the claim is made, plus glowing mesh gradients and glassmorphism on UI components for depth. Dense, well-sequenced B2B page with product UI showcase up top and testimonials before the closing CTA.

3b9e55575c0248afa50153260e5738fa.description: Portfolio site for designer Yaremenko. Opens on a minimal cream loader with oversized serif progress numbers, then cuts hard to a solid black hero for a dramatic luminance reveal. The hero is a digital collage: the hands from Michelangelo's Creation of Adam recut as graphic stickers with thick white outlines, muted painterly flesh tones against the black, paired with a rotating circular badge repeating "Keep scrolling" that works as both ornament and CTA. Good reference for the classical-art-as-sticker treatment and for using a loader-to-hero brightness jump as a transition device.

d5c3da5148ef449faa7ea18c8b997d75.description: Yolélé is a US-based West African food brand founded by Senegalese chef Pierre Thiam, built around fonio — an ancient gluten-free Sahel grain — with a stated mission of creating income for smallholder farming communities. The hero layers vibrant food and raw-ingredient photography under an organic blob-shaped text container instead of a rigid box, which reads artisanal rather than corporate. Palette is sunset orange-red, canary yellow and earthy greens and tans; a hand-lettered display face handles branding while a clean sans keeps navigation legible. Worth stealing: organic framing shapes for headlines, and mixing photography with flat graphic illustration to root a product in its origin story. Note the own-store checkout has been retired in favour of Amazon and retail.

8fddb252f7544aa4bba4f16318757862.description: Marketing site of Yonder, the UK rewards credit and debit card brand (moved from yonder.app). Warm lifestyle-photo hero of people dining with a floating tilted card render and bold geometric sans type, in a cream, brick-red and charcoal palette. Steal-worthy bits: an interactive monthly-spend-to-rewards calculator, swipeable partner reward card carousels, an app feature grid built from real UI snippets, and a cheeky conversational FAQ ("There are no stupid questions").

2d279aad1f384a649b638fccfc5ead50.description: Project page from creative director Youssri Rahman's portfolio (YR), covering the Maison Chateau Rouge x Air Jordan "Global Collab". Full-viewport macro photography of the garment carries the page, in warm browns, deep reds and cream, with an oversized sans headline laid over the imagery. A fixed vertical side navigation with a project counter runs down the left edge. Heavy scroll-jacking meant only the opening frames rendered headlessly, so deeper sections are visuals unverified.

b39e4cf7e55f4d9298e66b6d7de73911.description: Yuri is a German space-biotech company leveraging microgravity for drug development and cell research via in-house space labs (ScienceTaxi) and ground simulators, partnering with Sierra Space, ESA and The Exploration Company. The homepage leads with a text-dominant 'Space biotech for a better life' statement backed by an unusual three-up stats block (151 space labs launched, 61 customers on 4 continents, 138 space biology publications) and an institutional logos bar (MIT, UCLA, NUS, ESA, Charité). Strongest block is 'Benefits for Life Science' — six decimal-numbered items (.1 growing cell cultures in 3D through .6 advancing nanofluidics) each paired with its own illustration, plus a testimonial carousel featuring a former Merck CEO and astronaut Matthias Maurer. Brand accent is a lime-green. Visuals unverified (client-side exception in headless render); hero type inferred from a text-only H1 with no hero media in the markup.

22c7b8e81d88809f8dd7e2e02890fce6.description: Zapier is the incumbent AI-orchestration and workflow-automation platform (9,000+ app integrations, AI agents, MCP). The homepage hero is deliberately restrained and conversion-first: pure white ground, a vertically stacked bold high-contrast sans headline, subtext, and a primary / secondary CTA pair in the signature Zapier orange, with a social-proof row of key metrics and compliance badges (SOC 2, GDPR) sitting right under the fold line. Generous whitespace and no hero imagery at all — authority is carried entirely by numbers and trust marks. Useful as a reference for large-scale SaaS marketing IA (product UI showcases, integration directory, pricing tiers) rather than for visual daring.

2aa660e99555465fa87f6873360d0ef5.description: Zelt is an integrated HR platform covering the full employee lifecycle across HR, payroll and IT in one system. The hero goes ultra-large centred sans with tight kerning on a warm greige background, letting the value proposition carry the screen with almost no supporting furniture; amber-yellow is held back for the CTA buttons only. A 3D scene sits behind the type rather than competing with it. The greige-plus-amber pairing is a nice escape from the default HR-tech blue. Good reference for a crowded category where the differentiator is consolidation and the design has to feel calm and premium rather than busy.

4bbe8d834eb940d38f9077aef3740fd7.description: A scene inside "The Zendetta Story", an interactive cinematic narrative told as a chaptered timeline (this URL is chapter one / scene one). The experience is illustration- and motion-driven scrollytelling with a gritty, film-grain tone, structured so readers move scene by scene through the story. A useful reference for long-form narrative/scrollytelling structure where content is broken into chapters and scenes. Note: the headless render returned a "device unsupported" fallback (the story requires a modern browser/GPU), so the in-scene visuals are unverified and described from the site's structure rather than a captured frame.

d76aa83cfa5d4862aed3b8e06f3636b4.description: Zentry is a Web3 gaming / metaverse layer (formerly GuildFi) and one of the most-cited scrolltelling references of the 2024-2025 cycle, built around clipped-video reveals, oversized display type and heavy GSAP-driven section transitions. In a headless render the site never gets past its entry state: a solid black screen with the violet geometric Z mark (two opposing arrowheads in negative space) and nothing else. Visuals unverified (loader/WebGL gate in headless render), so hero type is left unset rather than guessed; treat the recorded style tags as coming from Andrey's own live viewing.

3177b8e81d88805fbf80ec326994c123.description: Zing is a pure-play Twilio Gold Partner that designs and builds Twilio Flex cloud contact centres, AI/bot automation and CX transformations for retail, finance, transport and non-profits (Oxfam, Age UK, Bennetts, CarFinance 247). Visually it is a friendly enterprise-consultancy site: off-white base with a fine dot-grid texture, deep navy anchors and soft lavender/lime/tan accents, bold sans headlines, and layered realistic UI mockups floating over organic colour blobs. Worth stealing: the numbered 01-04 services accordion where each step swaps its own illustration, the scrolling client logos marquee, and the customer-story cards that pair a brand logo, a portrait and a hard result ("38% cost-per-contact reduction"). Testimonial and case-study sections are strong; note a few unreplaced Webflow placeholder testimonials still ship in the DOM.

eefad78edfa24eefa74d55385a2d3ff8.description: ZOHO is a Ukrainian clothing brand (no relation to Zoho Corp) selling utilitarian, laconic, comfort-first apparel — verified still live as a working storefront. The hero centres a model photograph framed by large overlapping circular motifs and translucent geometric overlays that create depth, with big light-weight display type layered behind the figure. The palette is muted and sophisticated: dusty blue, taupe and warm greys, paired with thin-line icons and widely spaced minimal navigation. Reference for circular-motif layering and soft neutral fashion minimalism.

80b80f6c338047a993af38ad19fa3fbd.description: Zoox, the Amazon-owned autonomous robotaxi company. The hero centres a bold direct headline over a rounded video frame, on a muted mint-green field with charcoal text and teal-green accents, a "soft-tech" palette that swaps stark white for a branded pastel. Typography is clean bold geometric sans with wide-tracked navigation. Two things worth stealing: extreme negative space around the headline, and large consistent corner radii applied to every element (banners, buttons, video frames) so advanced autonomous-vehicle tech reads friendly rather than intimidating.

c48d5dc3c9d543c08eba200034881cd1.description: Longines Spirit Zulu Time — a dedicated campaign microsite (FR) for the brand’s GMT pilot watch, whose name traces back to the 1925 Longines dual-time wristwatch that carried the Zulu flag on its dial (“Z” being aviation’s letter for universal time). The hero is a lifestyle composition: deep navy and muted greys with warm metallic accents off the watch itself, shot as high-fashion photography with shallow depth of field, and a massive semi-transparent sans headline layered into the imagery rather than sitting on top of it — a clean example of type-integrated-into-photo done at luxury scale. Dark atmospheric colour grade throughout. Good reference for heritage storytelling: the site leans on the 1911 dual-time-zone patent and the 1925 origin to justify a modern GMT release.
